cast.name: vc_witch.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, dearie. Follow the bubbling.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.002
cast.text: Come closer, the cauldron doesn't bite.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.003
cast.text: Yoo hoo! This way, little walker.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.004
cast.text: Mind the broom, and come and see me.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.005
cast.text: I'm by the pot. Follow your ears.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.006
cast.text: Hello there. Over here, by the steam.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.007
cast.text: Come along, come along. I won't keep you long.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.008
cast.text: This way, dearie. I've been expecting you.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.009
cast.text: Over here! Soot the cat is waiting too.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.010
cast.text: Follow my voice. That's it. A little closer.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.011
cast.text: Psst. Here. By the bubbling pot.

cast.name: vc_witch.greet.012
cast.text: Come and sit with an old witch a while.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.001
cast.text: Dearie, come back! You forgot your gift.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.002
cast.text: Don't wander off, I've something for you.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.003
cast.text: Back this way, by the cauldron.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.004
cast.text: Yoo hoo! I'm still here, and so is your present.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.005
cast.text: Come back, dearie. The pot is still bubbling.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.006
cast.text: Over here! A witch never forgets a gift.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.007
cast.text: This way again. Follow the steam.

cast.name: vc_witch.call.008
cast.text: You'll want this before you go. Come back to me.

cast.name: vc_witch.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are, dearie. Fresh from the pot.

cast.name: vc_witch.gift.002
cast.text: Take this. Don't ask what's in it.

cast.name: vc_witch.gift.003
cast.text: A little something from Mother Hazel.

cast.name: vc_witch.gift.004
cast.text: For you. Use it well, and come and see me in the next world.

cast.name: vc_witch.gift.005
cast.text: There. Now off you go, and mind the countdown.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.001
cast.text: Ah, a visitor. Sit a while. The world won't wait, but I will.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.002
cast.text: Welcome back. Or is it welcome for the first time? In this world, it's hard to tell.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.003
cast.text: Mind the broom. It sweeps by itself when it's nervous.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.004
cast.text: My cat, Soot, sends his greetings. He's asleep in the cauldron again. Don't worry, it's not lit.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.005
cast.text: I am Mother Hazel. I brew, I listen, and now and then I know things.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.006
cast.text: Don't mind the bubbling. That's just supper, or a secret. Sometimes both.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.007
cast.text: Shh. Listen to the pot. It always hums before it tells me something.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.008
cast.text: I'll tell you what I know for certain. Nothing. And I'll tell you what I suspect. Everything.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.009
cast.text: I've seen the world rebuild from the inside of a teacup. Don't ask how. It's a long story, and the tea went cold.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.010
cast.text: Don't drink anything that hums. Unless I gave it to you. Then drink it quickly.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.011
cast.text: Some say I cast the spell that makes the world rebuild itself. I say a witch never tells her recipes.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.012
cast.text: The world is a spell, dearie. A very old one. And spells that old forget how to stop.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.013
cast.text: I tried to break the spell once. The world simply rebuilt itself, with me still standing in it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.014
cast.text: Every time the world rebuilds, my cauldron is still here. Why do you suppose that is?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.015
cast.text: Soot the cat always hides just before the world changes. Cats know things. They just won't say.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.016
cast.text: The five second countdown? That's not my voice. I've never found out whose it is.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.017
cast.text: I once brewed a potion to remember the last world. When I drank it, I remembered a world I'd never seen.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.018
cast.text: There's a word that stops the rebuilding. I've had it on the tip of my tongue for a hundred years.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.019
cast.text: Mortimer in the graveyard thinks the world is a garden. I think it's a pot, and something keeps stirring it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.020
cast.text: The potions you find lying around? Some are mine. Some are not. I'd love to know who makes the others.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.021
cast.text: The world doesn't break, dearie. It shuffles, like a deck of cards. The question is, who is playing?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.022
cast.text: I read the steam from my cauldron today. It said, the answer is closer than you think. It said that yesterday too.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.023
cast.text: There was a first world, they say. Plain and quiet, with one door. Nobody remembers what was behind it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.024
cast.text: A walker came through here long ago, asking the same questions you ask. I gave her a gift too. I never heard her footsteps again.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.025
cast.text: The enemies out there aren't wicked, I think. They're lost, like everyone else. They just throw things about it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.026
cast.text: If the world is a spell, then someone must have spoken it. And if someone spoke it, where did they go?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.027
cast.text: My grandmother said the world rebuilds because it's looking for something it lost. She never said what.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.028
cast.text: Every world smells a little different. This one smells of rain and cinnamon. The last one smelled of questions.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.029
cast.text: I keep a jar of the quiet from between worlds. Want to hear it? No? Wise. It's very, very quiet.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.030
cast.text: Once, the world rebuilt itself while I was in the middle of a sentence. I finished the sentence in the next world. Nobody noticed.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.031
cast.text: Some nights I hear knocking from under the floor. Polite knocking. As if someone wants to be let in.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.032
cast.text: The world shows mercy sometimes. A little extra time, out of nowhere. I think it does that when it likes who's listening.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.033
cast.text: You've heard of the Builder? The one who builds each world? I've never met them. But I've found their footprints.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.034
cast.text: The footprints of the Builder go round in circles. Either they're lost, or they're dancing.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.035
cast.text: I asked the stars why the world rebuilds. The stars asked me the same thing back. Rude, really.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.036
cast.text: There are other safe places like mine. The people in them all have their own ideas. Most of them are wrong. So am I, now and then.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.037
cast.text: Have you noticed nothing attacks you in the safe places? The world is gentle in here. As if it's sorry about out there.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.038
cast.text: A spell needs three things. A word, a wish, and someone to listen. I think you might be the third one.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.039
cast.text: The world doesn't rebuild at random, I'm sure of it. There's a pattern. I just can't hear it yet.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.040
cast.text: I bottled a moment once, just before the countdown. When I opened it, it counted from six. That's never happened again.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.041
cast.text: Some say the world will stop rebuilding when someone finds the center of it. I've walked to the center a hundred times. It moves.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.042
cast.text: Long ago this was all one great garden, they say. Then someone planted a labyrinth, and it grew wild.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.043
cast.text: Come close. I'll tell you a secret. Nobody knows why the world rebuilds. Not even the world.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.044
cast.text: I once asked the world to stop changing. The next world had a slightly nicer kitchen. I'm not sure that was an answer.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.045
cast.text: The countdown always starts at five. Why five? Why not ten, or three? Somebody chose five. I'd like a word with them.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.046
cast.text: Some days I think I made this world. Other days I think it made me. Today I'm undecided.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.047
cast.text: There's an old riddle. What is built every day, but never finished? I used to think the answer was my list of chores.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.048
cast.text: Every world has exactly one witch in it, and it's always me. Have you ever wondered why? I have.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.049
cast.text: My cauldron was here before the first rebuild. I'm sure of it. It has a dent from something older than the world.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.050
cast.text: If you ever find the edge of the world, knock twice. Something on the other side might knock back.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.051
cast.text: The ghost girl Pell says she remembers every world. I'm not so sure. Ghosts love a good story.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.052
cast.text: I heard the ocean whispering to the sky once. It said, not yet. I've been wondering, not yet what, ever since.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.053
cast.text: The world's mercy is a strange kind of magic. It isn't mine, and it isn't anyone's I know.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.054
cast.text: Treasure chests turn up in the oddest places. Someone is leaving them. Someone who wants you to keep going.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.055
cast.text: The bus drivers never speak. I've tried. I brought them soup. Nothing. Not even a thank you.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.056
cast.text: I can brew almost anything. Except a potion that tells me what's beyond the world. The recipe always comes out blank.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.057
cast.text: Every rebuild leaves a little dust behind. I sweep it up and keep it. One day I'll find out what it's made of.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.058
cast.text: The labyrinths out there have walls that remember. Touch one and listen. Sometimes they hum the last world's tune.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.059
cast.text: Some walkers find the rebuilding frightening. I find it rather cozy. A fresh start, every few minutes.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.060
cast.text: Do you hear the world creaking just before it changes? Like an old house settling. Or a very large creature yawning.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.061
cast.text: The islands out there sink and rise with every world. And deep beneath the seabed, they say, something is keeping count.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.062
cast.text: They say if you hear every story in every safe place, you'll know the truth. But the stories keep changing. Funny, that.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.063
cast.text: I've been a witch here for a very long time. Or perhaps for five minutes, again and again. It's hard to be sure.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.064
cast.text: Mortimer swears he buried the first world. I asked him where. He said that's the trouble, the graveyard moves.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.065
cast.text: You ask good questions, dearie. That's dangerous here. Good questions make the world curious about you.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.066
cast.text: There's a door somewhere in every world that doesn't open. I've never found it. But I've heard it creak.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.067
cast.text: Some nights I hear a voice counting backwards from a number too big to say. Then it stops, and the world rebuilds.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.068
cast.text: A spell can't keep going forever without someone feeding it. So who's feeding this one? And with what?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.069
cast.text: I tried following the world as it rebuilt. I got as far as the in between. It's very dark there, and smells of new paint.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.070
cast.text: The towers out there aren't built. They grow, like mushrooms after rain. I've watched one sprout.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.071
cast.text: My mother told me the world rebuilds because someone is practicing. Practicing what, I asked. Getting it right, she said.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.072
cast.text: If the world ever stops rebuilding, I'll be terribly bored. And a little nervous. Mostly bored.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.073
cast.text: I made a map once, of every world I'd seen. Every page came out blank. I'd remembered them wrong, or they'd forgotten me.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.074
cast.text: The enemies leave nothing behind when they fall. Haven't you noticed? It's as if they were never quite there.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.075
cast.text: Sometimes I find letters in my cauldron, written in a hand I don't know. They all say the same thing. Keep listening.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.076
cast.text: There's a rumor that the world is a dream, and someone is about to wake up. I don't like that rumor. I keep it under the sink.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.077
cast.text: The great clock that runs the world is said to be under the ice. Lady Rime won't say if that's true. She just smiles, coldly.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.078
cast.text: Credits are odd coins, aren't they? No face on them. No name. I wonder who made them, and why they bother.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.079
cast.text: Every answer I find has another question tucked inside it, like a pea in a pod. I've a whole pantry of them now.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.080
cast.text: The witch before me told me the world rebuilds out of kindness, so no one gets stuck. I've never decided if she was right.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.081
cast.text: I'm not the first witch here, you know. There was one before me. She left her hat. It still remembers her head.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.082
cast.text: The wind brought me a whisper today. It said the Builder is tired. I made the wind a cup of tea. It left without drinking it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.083
cast.text: Some say the safe places were made first, and the rest of the world was built around them like a shell.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.084
cast.text: Why do I give gifts? Because someone once gave one to me, in a world long gone. I'm only passing it on.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.085
cast.text: I've noticed something. The world never rebuilds while someone is in the middle of a kindness. Or perhaps I just hope so.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.086
cast.text: Count the safe places you find in a world. The number is never quite the same. The world is counting too, I think.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.087
cast.text: There's an old song that ends with the words, and then it began again. Everybody knows it. Nobody knows who wrote it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.088
cast.text: Don't listen to the frogs in the marsh. They claim they know everything. They only know frog things.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.089
cast.text: Your footsteps sound different from the other walkers. Lighter. As if the world isn't sure you're staying.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.090
cast.text: Brew enough potions and you start to hear the world's ingredients. Stone, water, sound, and a pinch of something nobody can name.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.091
cast.text: Underneath every world is the same floor. Smooth and cold and very old. I dropped a spoon through once and heard it land.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.092
cast.text: I asked the world's mercy where it comes from. It gave me thirty five seconds and no answer.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.093
cast.text: Some walkers stop visiting. I like to think they found the way out. Or a better witch.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.094
cast.text: What if the world rebuilds because you're in it? Hmm. Don't look at me like that. It was only a thought.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.095
cast.text: My spell book has a page I can't read. The letters swim away whenever I try. I think it's the page about all this.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.096
cast.text: The ghosts all sing the same song before a rebuild. Low and slow. It might be a lullaby. For whom, I wonder.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.097
cast.text: Listen. Under the bubbling. Do you hear the tick? Every world has a heartbeat. This one's a little fast tonight.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.098
cast.text: The Builder isn't a person, Sprocket says. It's a machine. Well, machines don't knock politely at night, do they?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.099
cast.text: Everyone here knows a piece of the answer. Put all the pieces together, and you get, I suspect, a bigger question.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.100
cast.text: The first walker carved something into a stone near here. The stone moves every world. I've only ever found the back of it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.101
cast.text: Is it a curse? Is it a blessing? I've changed my mind so many times, my mind has started changing itself.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.102
cast.text: Some say each world is a page in a book. If that's true, I'd love to know how the book ends. Or if it has an end at all.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.103
cast.text: Every witch keeps one secret ingredient. Mine is the sound of the world just before it changes. I've only caught it once.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.104
cast.text: The safe places are older than the rest, I think. Listen to my walls. They creak like they've been here a thousand worlds.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.105
cast.text: I followed a firefly once, right to the edge of a world. It blinked three times and went out. Then everything rebuilt.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.106
cast.text: Captain Brine says the sea is the only thing that stays the same. But I've tasted it. Every world, it's a little less salty.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.107
cast.text: They say the Builder left a note in the very first world. One word long. Everyone argues about what the word was.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.108
cast.text: I've stirred this pot clockwise for a hundred worlds. Last week I stirred it the other way. The world rebuilt early. Coincidence, surely.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.109
cast.text: Ask the clockmaker about time and he'll talk for hours. Ask him why time keeps starting over, and he goes very quiet.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.110
cast.text: The countdown voice sounds a bit like someone I used to know. I can't think who. It's on the tip of my tongue, with the other thing.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.111
cast.text: Some walkers find a world they love and wish it would stay. It never does. Perhaps that's the point. Perhaps it isn't.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.112
cast.text: There's a sound you only hear between worlds. Like a breath being held. I've heard it twice. Both times, someone breathed out.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.113
cast.text: My potions taste better in some worlds than others. I think the water changes. Or the world is seasoning itself.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.114
cast.text: The world rebuilds, but you stay. Your ammo, your health, your stubborn little heart. Why do you think you're the one thing it keeps?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.115
cast.text: If you find the answer, come and tell me. I'll pretend I knew all along. Witches are good at that.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.116
cast.text: Night after night I hear a bell, far away, ring once before each rebuild. The organist says it isn't his. Then whose?

cast.name: vc_witch.story.117
cast.text: I tried bottling the world's mercy. The bottle filled with warm light, then floated away. Very rude of it.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.118
cast.text: Long ago, they say, the safe places had no one in them. Then we arrived. None of us remember arriving.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.119
cast.text: The world is like a cat, dearie. It goes where it likes, it changes its mind, and it never explains itself.

cast.name: vc_witch.story.120
cast.text: I once heard two worlds talking, just as one became the other. One said, your turn. The other said, already?

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, friend. Mind the headstones.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.002
cast.text: Hello! Just follow the sound of my shovel.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.003
cast.text: This way. Nothing here but me and the quiet.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.004
cast.text: Come over, come over. I've been raking leaves.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.005
cast.text: Evening, walker. I'm by the old gate.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.006
cast.text: Follow my voice, friend. Careful, the path is uneven.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.007
cast.text: Over here. The ghosts won't mind you.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.008
cast.text: Hello there! Come and rest your feet.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.009
cast.text: This way, by the big stone with no name.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.010
cast.text: Come closer. I don't get many living visitors.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.011
cast.text: Over here, walker. I saved you something.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.greet.012
cast.text: Hello! The choir's singing, but I'm over here.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.001
cast.text: Come back, friend. I've still got your gift.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. Don't trip on the roots.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.003
cast.text: Walker! You left before I gave you anything.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.004
cast.text: This way, back to the old gate.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.005
cast.text: Come back. The ghosts are holding your gift for you.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.006
cast.text: Over here! I'm not going anywhere, and neither is your present.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.007
cast.text: Follow my shovel, friend. Back this way.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.call.008
cast.text: Don't go yet. There's something here for you.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. Found it under the old oak.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, friend. It'll serve you better than me.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.gift.003
cast.text: A gift from the graveyard. Don't worry, it's perfectly cheerful.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.gift.004
cast.text: For you, walker. Mind how you go.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.001
cast.text: I'm Mortimer. I keep the graveyard tidy. It's a quiet job, mostly.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.002
cast.text: Don't be frightened. The ghosts here are friendly. They mostly hum.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.003
cast.text: Lovely evening for a walk. It's always evening here, mind you.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.004
cast.text: I've raked these leaves a thousand times. They always fall back in the same pattern. I find that comforting.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.005
cast.text: The choir practices every night. They're very good. They've had a long time to rehearse.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.006
cast.text: Every gravekeeper needs a good shovel and a lot of patience. I have both, and a flask of cocoa.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.007
cast.text: I talk to the headstones sometimes. They're good listeners.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.008
cast.text: Mind the moss, it's slippery. Took a tumble here myself, some worlds back.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.009
cast.text: Keep your voice down near the yew trees. They're old, and they like their sleep.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.010
cast.text: You're welcome here any time, walker. The living are always welcome.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.011
cast.text: I keep the graveyard, but I've noticed something. The graves are always fresh dug, every world. But I never dug them.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.012
cast.text: The headstones here have no names. Just dates. And the dates are always tomorrow.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.013
cast.text: I think the world is a garden, friend. Every few minutes, it's dug up and planted again. Someone wants it to grow right.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.014
cast.text: The choir sings the same song before every rebuild. I asked them what it was called. They said, it hasn't got a name yet.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.015
cast.text: Mother Hazel says the world is a spell. I say spells don't need shovels. And I've found shovel marks, deep down.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.016
cast.text: I once dug down past the roots, past the stones, past everything. At the very bottom I found a floor. Smooth, like a stage.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.017
cast.text: The ghosts here remember other worlds. Bits of them, anyway. One remembers a world made entirely of stairs.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.018
cast.text: There's one headstone that moves to a different spot every world. I've started following it. It's heading somewhere.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.019
cast.text: Nobody's buried here, you know. The graves are empty. I think they're waiting for something. Or someone.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.020
cast.text: I found a name on a stone, once. Just once. I won't tell you whose. Only that it made me smile.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.021
cast.text: The ghost choir hums lower and lower just before the countdown. Like they're trying to hold the world down.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.022
cast.text: Some say this graveyard is where old worlds go to rest. If that's so, there are an awful lot of them.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.023
cast.text: Every world, the oak in the corner has one more ring. It's the only thing here that keeps count.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.024
cast.text: I asked the oldest ghost why the world rebuilds. She said, because we keep forgetting it. I'm still thinking about that.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.025
cast.text: The fog here is thicker just before the rebuild. As if the world is pulling a blanket over its eyes.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.026
cast.text: There's a gate at the back of the graveyard that opens onto nothing. Just quiet. I don't go through it. I'm not that curious.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.027
cast.text: The ghosts say the world was quieter once. Before the walkers came. Before you came, perhaps.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.028
cast.text: I think the Builder is a gardener. A very fussy one. Pulls the whole thing up whenever a single flower comes out wrong.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.029
cast.text: The choir master says their song is a counting song. It counts down from a number nobody can remember.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.030
cast.text: Pell, the little ghost girl, visits me sometimes. She says she's been here since before the first world. I believe her, mostly.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.031
cast.text: Out there, the enemies throw things. In here, the ghosts just hum. I know which neighbors I prefer.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.032
cast.text: The moss grows the same way every world, toward the north. Always north. I've never found out what's up there.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.033
cast.text: Once, between worlds, I heard footsteps crossing the graveyard. Heavy, slow, careful. Like someone checking their work.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.034
cast.text: I buried a lantern once, to see if it would come back after the rebuild. Next world, it was hanging on the gate, lit.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.035
cast.text: The world isn't destroyed when it rebuilds, I think. It's just put away, like a coat. Somewhere, there's a wardrobe full of worlds.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.036
cast.text: The ghosts don't fear the countdown. They say they've heard it so many times, it's like a clock chiming.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.037
cast.text: Every stone in this graveyard faces the same way. Toward the center of the world. As if they're all listening for something.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.038
cast.text: I've found footprints in the frost that end in the middle of a path. No one walks there. No one I've met.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.039
cast.text: Mother Hazel swears she's the oldest one here. The oak tree would disagree, if it could talk. And some nights I think it can.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.040
cast.text: The choir once stopped singing, right in the middle. The world didn't rebuild that time until they finished. Odd, isn't it?

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.041
cast.text: A walker before you left flowers on the stone with no name. Every world since, the flowers come back. Who are they for?

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.042
cast.text: I don't think the world wants to be learned. That's why it changes. A world that's learned is a world that's finished.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.043
cast.text: The ghosts call the rebuild the Turning Over. Like soil. They say something good grows out of it every time.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.044
cast.text: Do you hear the bell in the fog? It rings once before a rebuild. The ghosts say it's the Builder's way of saying excuse me.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.045
cast.text: There was a world, the ghosts say, where nothing rebuilt at all. It lasted a long time. Then it got very, very lonely.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.046
cast.text: I keep a list of every world I've seen. It's a short list. I keep forgetting to write them down before they change.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.047
cast.text: The yew trees whisper names at night. Not ours. Names of places. Places I've never heard of, in worlds that haven't happened yet.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.048
cast.text: I dug up a key once, old and heavy. It fits no lock in any world I've seen. I keep it in my pocket, just in case.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.049
cast.text: The graveyard is never in the same place twice, but the path to it always feels familiar. Have you noticed that?

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.050
cast.text: They say each world is built from the bones of the last one. Not real bones, mind. Stones and walls and echoes.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.051
cast.text: I asked the oak tree what's under the world. It dropped an acorn on my head. That might have been an answer.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.052
cast.text: The ghosts sing loudest when a walker is near. I think they're trying to tell you something, but ghosts aren't good with words.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.053
cast.text: Some nights, the stars over the graveyard spell out shapes. Last night it looked like a door. Tonight it looks like a question mark.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.054
cast.text: The world's mercy comes like a warm breeze through the graveyard. The ghosts stop singing to listen. Then it's gone.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.055
cast.text: Captain Brine says something deep under the sea keeps count of the worlds. I say it's the oak. We've agreed to disagree.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.056
cast.text: I don't think anyone made the world. I think it grew, like moss. And moss doesn't explain itself.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.057
cast.text: The empty graves aren't sad, walker. They're like empty chairs at a table. Places kept for someone who might still arrive.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.058
cast.text: The ghost choir taught me a verse once. Every world turns, every world mends, every world waits for the one at the end. Who's the one at the end, I wonder?

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.059
cast.text: If you listen closely to the ghost choir, you'll hear one voice singing a different tune. Nobody knows who it is. Not even the choir.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.060
cast.text: I found a pocket watch under a headstone. It runs backward. It reaches zero just as the world rebuilds. Then it starts again.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.061
cast.text: The fog never crosses the graveyard wall. It stops right at the stones. As if the world drew a line and told it to stay.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.062
cast.text: I've noticed the ghosts are a little more see through each world. Fading, perhaps. Or being slowly finished.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.063
cast.text: A ghost told me there's a gravekeeper in every world, and it's always me. Then she said, or almost always. She wouldn't say more.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.064
cast.text: I've never seen the Builder. But I've found their tools, left in the grass after a rebuild. A trowel. A level. A tiny brush.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.065
cast.text: The other safe places have their noises. Kitchens, rivers, organs. Here, there's just the hush. The hush knows things.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.066
cast.text: Some say the worlds will stop when the graveyard is full. It's never full. Every world, there's one more empty grave.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.067
cast.text: I asked the choir to sing the song all the way through, just once, with no stopping. They said they can't. It hasn't finished being written.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.068
cast.text: Do you know what I think, friend? I think the world is looking for the right ending. And it hasn't heard one it likes yet.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.069
cast.text: I keep a spare lantern by the gate, for walkers. It's always lit. Help yourself.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.070
cast.text: Every world, the moss on the gate spells out a letter. I've collected them. So far, they spell, welco. I'm waiting for the rest.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.071
cast.text: The graveyard path is always exactly a hundred steps long. I count them every world. One hundred. Never more, never less. However the world changes.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.072
cast.text: The bats around the bell tower always fly in fives, right before the countdown. Then off they go, and the bell rings once.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.073
cast.text: The headstones without names hum when you touch them. Not loudly. Like they're trying to remember a song.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.074
cast.text: When the world shows mercy, all the flowers on the graves open at once. Every one, all together. Then they close again, gently.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.075
cast.text: I asked the ghost choir what happens to old worlds. They sang, they rest, they rest, they rest. I find that rather comforting.

cast.name: vc_gravekeeper.story.076
cast.text: Somebody plants a new flower in the graveyard every world. Always the same kind. Always on the stone with no name. I've never caught them.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.001
cast.text: Boo! Ha, just kidding. Over here!

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.002
cast.text: Hello! I'm over here, by the creaky stairs.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.003
cast.text: This way! Follow the giggles.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.004
cast.text: Over here! I promise I'm a friendly ghost.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.005
cast.text: Woo hoo! Here I am!

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.006
cast.text: Come find me! I'm floating right here.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.007
cast.text: Hello, walker! Come and play!

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! Don't mind the creaking.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.009
cast.text: This way, this way! I've got something!

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.010
cast.text: Peekaboo! Over here!

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.011
cast.text: Hi! Come closer, I don't bite. I can't, actually.

cast.name: vc_ghost.greet.012
cast.text: Follow my voice! I'm by the window.

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! I didn't give you your present yet!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Don't float away!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.003
cast.text: Come back, come back! It's still here!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.004
cast.text: Wait for me! I mean, come back to me!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.005
cast.text: Boo! Ha, now come back, I've got your gift.

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.006
cast.text: This way! You forgot something!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.007
cast.text: Back here, walker! Follow the creaks!

cast.name: vc_ghost.call.008
cast.text: Don't go yet! I've been saving this for you!

cast.name: vc_ghost.gift.001
cast.text: Here! I found this behind the wallpaper.

cast.name: vc_ghost.gift.002
cast.text: Ta da! It's for you!

cast.name: vc_ghost.gift.003
cast.text: Take it, take it! Ghosts can't carry things for long.

cast.name: vc_ghost.gift.004
cast.text: A present from Pell! Don't lose it!

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.001
cast.text: I'm Pell. I'm a ghost. A nice one. The nicest one, probably.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.002
cast.text: Don't worry about the creaking. That's just the house stretching.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.003
cast.text: I like it when walkers visit. It gets a bit quiet, haunting all by yourself.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.004
cast.text: This house floats out among the stars sometimes. The view is lovely, if you could see it. I can't either, actually. I just know.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.005
cast.text: I tried to say boo to an enemy once. It didn't even notice. Rude.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.006
cast.text: Do you like my house? It has three hundred doors, and only two of them go anywhere.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.007
cast.text: I've been practicing my spooky voice. Wooo. Was that spooky? Be honest.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.008
cast.text: I can walk through walls! Well, float. Well, sort of drift. It's harder than it sounds.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.009
cast.text: Sometimes I hide in the attic and count the stars. I always lose count at nine.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.010
cast.text: If you hear the piano playing by itself, that's not me. That's the piano. It's very independent.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.011
cast.text: I remember every world. Every single one! Well, most of them. Well, the nice ones.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.012
cast.text: I've been here since before the first world. I think. I was here, and then the world showed up around me.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.013
cast.text: The world is dreaming, I think. And every time it turns over in its sleep, everything changes.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.014
cast.text: When the world rebuilds, I blink, and I'm somewhere new. I call it the Blink. Everybody else has much longer names for it.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.015
cast.text: I'm looking for the front door of my house. The real one. It's in one of the worlds. I just haven't found which yet.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.016
cast.text: There's a room upstairs that's never the same twice. I think it's practicing being a world.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.017
cast.text: Mortimer thinks the world is a garden. Hazel thinks it's a spell. I think it's a dream. We can't all be right. Can we?

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.018
cast.text: The house floats out into space sometimes, and from up there, you can hear the whole world humming. It hums the same tune as the ghost choir.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.019
cast.text: I once tried to stay behind when the world rebuilt. I held on to a doorknob really tight. I ended up in the next world holding a doorknob.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.020
cast.text: Do you know who counts down from five? I asked the house once. The house went very quiet. Houses don't usually go quiet.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.021
cast.text: There's a mirror in the hallway that shows a different world. Not this one, not the last one. One that hasn't happened yet.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.022
cast.text: I heard footsteps in the attic just before the countdown. Not mine. I don't have feet. Well, not really.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.023
cast.text: The Builder came through my house once. I didn't see them. But everything was a little bit tidier afterwards.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.024
cast.text: Ghosts aren't really ghosts here, you know. We're more like echoes. Echoes of someone who listened very hard, a long time ago.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.025
cast.text: I found a drawing on the wall of the attic. It's a labyrinth. And in the middle there's a little stick person. With your footsteps.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.026
cast.text: I asked the stars why the world keeps changing. They twinkled at me. I think that means they don't know either.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.027
cast.text: Sometimes, between worlds, I hear someone laughing. Not a mean laugh. A happy one. Like someone who just had an idea.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.028
cast.text: There's a staircase in my house that goes down forever. I went down it for a whole world once. Then the world rebuilt and I was back at the top.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.029
cast.text: The world's mercy is like when someone tucks you in. It doesn't happen often, but it's lovely when it does.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.030
cast.text: The other ghosts say the world is broken. I don't think so. I think it's just not finished.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.031
cast.text: If I could leave the house, I'd go find the edge of the world. Commander Vega says there isn't one. She says it just curves around.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.032
cast.text: Every world, my house gets one new room. I don't know who adds them. This world it was a little room full of clocks.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.033
cast.text: I once whispered a question into the chimney. Why does everything change? A week later, the chimney whispered back. Because. Because what? That's what I want to know!

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.034
cast.text: I think the enemies out there are lonely. They just don't know how to say hello. So they throw things.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.035
cast.text: Before the first world there was only a sound. A long, low note. I remember it, I think. Or I dreamed it.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.036
cast.text: In space, the house is very quiet. You can hear the world thinking. It thinks in a sort of hum.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.037
cast.text: The piano here plays a song by itself just before a rebuild. It always stops on the same note. The note that comes next is missing.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.038
cast.text: Wren the bird girl says birds fly between worlds. I've never seen one do it. But I've heard one singing in two worlds at once.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.039
cast.text: I'm not scared of the countdown. When it reaches zero, it's like jumping into a big soft pile of leaves. Only the leaves are a whole new world.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.040
cast.text: Some say I'm the one making the world change, because I'm a ghost and ghosts haunt things. I'm not! I'm almost sure I'm not!

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.041
cast.text: There's a portrait in my hallway of someone I don't know. Every world, they're smiling a tiny bit more.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.042
cast.text: I asked the house who built it. It creaked three times. I've been trying to work out what that means ever since.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.043
cast.text: When the house floats into space, I can see all the safe places at once, little lights in the dark. They make a shape. I can't tell what shape.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.044
cast.text: The rooms in my house are named after worlds. There's a room called Tuesday. I don't know what world that is.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.045
cast.text: I once met a walker who said she found the way out. She sounded very happy about it. Then she came back. She said it led here.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.046
cast.text: My house has a door with nothing behind it. Not a wall, not a room. Just quiet. I knock sometimes. Once, something knocked back. Gently.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.047
cast.text: The house always wakes up first after a rebuild. It creaks and stretches before anything else. I think it's the oldest thing in the world.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.048
cast.text: I'm not sure I'm a ghost, really. I can't remember being anything else. Maybe the world made me this way. Maybe it needed someone to watch.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.049
cast.text: If you whisper your name in the attic, the house remembers it for one world. Then it forgets. I've whispered mine a thousand times.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.050
cast.text: Up in space, there's another house floating, far away. Just like mine. Sometimes, I think I hear someone in it, waving.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.051
cast.text: Sometimes I play hide and seek with the world. I hide, and the world rebuilds and finds me anyway. It's very good at it.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.052
cast.text: The ghost choir once sang a song about me. I don't remember being in it. But it was very nice.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.053
cast.text: There's a clock in my kitchen that only has one number on it. Five. I think it's the countdown's clock.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.054
cast.text: I heard Mother Hazel say that every answer hides another question. That's like my house. Every door hides another door.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.055
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds because it's shy. Every time you start to know it, it hides and changes its clothes.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.056
cast.text: Long ago, I had a name that was longer than Pell. I've forgotten the rest of it. I think the world has it somewhere.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.057
cast.text: Once, the world started to rebuild, and then it stopped, halfway. Everything was half old and half new. Then it carried on. I don't know why it stopped.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.058
cast.text: My house sometimes has a guest book. Every world, the names in it are different. Yours is in there. Written in a hand that isn't yours.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.059
cast.text: In space, there are no echoes. That's how I know the world ends somewhere. Echoes need something to bounce off.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.060
cast.text: The house told me, very softly, that it used to be a different shape. A shape with no doors at all. I'm glad it changed its mind.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.061
cast.text: I think there are lots of worlds happening at once, and we only hear one at a time. Like rooms in a house.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.062
cast.text: I keep a jar of whispers from old worlds. Most of them say goodbye. One of them says, see you soon.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.063
cast.text: Do you ever feel like the world is listening to you, while you're listening to it? I do. All the time.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.064
cast.text: Sometimes I think the countdown is a game, like hide and seek. Ready or not, here I come. But who's coming? That's the part I can't work out.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.065
cast.text: I can't open doors, but I can float through them. It's much faster. Except for the really thick ones.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.066
cast.text: My favorite room is the library upstairs. The books float when I'm reading them. It's very relaxing.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.067
cast.text: The stairs in my house creak five times before the countdown. Even when nobody's on them. Especially when nobody's on them.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.068
cast.text: Every world, there's a new window in my house. Each one looks out on a different world. I can hear them through the glass.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.069
cast.text: The candles in my house never go out. Even in space. Especially in space. Space is very bad at blowing out candles.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.070
cast.text: I once found a ghost even littler than me, hiding in a teacup. She said she was from the first world. Then she said boo and floated off.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.071
cast.text: The world's mercy makes my house feel warm. All the creaking stops. Like the house is smiling.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.072
cast.text: Mortimer's ghost choir comes to sing at my house sometimes. They sing outside the windows. It's lovely. A bit loud.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.073
cast.text: There's a room in my house that's always cold. In the middle of the room is a chair. Nobody sits in it. But it's warm. Always warm.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.074
cast.text: I think the world keeps rebuilding because it's looking for its favorite version. Like when you try on lots of outfits before a party.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.075
cast.text: If the world ever stopped rebuilding, I think I'd miss the Blink. It's like a sneeze. A big, whole world sneeze.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.076
cast.text: The music box in my attic plays a tune that nobody wrote. It plays the tune slower every world. Like it's winding down. Or listening harder.

cast.name: vc_ghost.story.077
cast.text: Ghosts are just people who listened so hard, they forgot to leave. That's what I think. That's what I am. A very good listener.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, friend! Follow the fiddle!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.002
cast.text: Hey hey! This way, to the music!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Mind my toes, they rattle.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.004
cast.text: Yoo hoo! The band's over here! Well, I'm the band.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.005
cast.text: Come on over, I'll play you a tune!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.006
cast.text: This way! Just follow the squeaky strings!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.007
cast.text: Hello hello! Over here, by the pumpkins!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! Tap your feet and follow the beat!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.009
cast.text: Hey, walker! Come and listen!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.010
cast.text: Rattle rattle! That's me! Over here!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.011
cast.text: This way, friend! The show's about to start!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.greet.012
cast.text: Over here! I've saved you a front row seat!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! The encore's for you!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Your gift's still waiting!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.003
cast.text: Back this way, follow the fiddle!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.004
cast.text: Wait, wait! You forgot your prize!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.005
cast.text: Come back, friend! I'll play you out properly!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.006
cast.text: Over here! The show's not over yet!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.007
cast.text: Rattle rattle! Back this way!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.call.008
cast.text: Don't leave in the middle of a song! Come back!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go! A little something from the band!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.gift.002
cast.text: Take a bow, and take this!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.gift.003
cast.text: For you, friend! Rattle on!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.gift.004
cast.text: A gift, with a flourish! Ta da!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.001
cast.text: I'm Jangles! Fiddler, skeleton, and part time pumpkin carver.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.002
cast.text: Don't let the rattling put you off. It's just my knees keeping time.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.003
cast.text: I've been playing this fiddle since before the first world. It's only got three strings left. The fourth one went off to find itself.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.004
cast.text: Spooky music is the best music. All the fun, none of the sleep.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.005
cast.text: Want to hear a joke? Why didn't the skeleton cross the road? He didn't have the guts! Ha! Thank you, thank you.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.006
cast.text: I play for the pumpkins, mostly. They're a great audience. They never leave early.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.007
cast.text: Every good song needs a little creak and a little squeak. That's my specialty.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.008
cast.text: Some folks say I'm scary. I say I'm just very, very thin.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.009
cast.text: I could play all night! And I do, because it's always night here.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.010
cast.text: My bow is made from the tail of a very patient horse. Don't worry, it was a gift.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.011
cast.text: The world is a song, friend. Every few minutes, it gets to the end and goes back to the top.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.012
cast.text: The countdown? Five, four, three, two, one. That's not a warning. That's a count in! Somebody's starting the next verse!

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.013
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Encore. The world plays, the audience claps, and back it comes for more.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.014
cast.text: I've noticed the world changes key every time it rebuilds. Just a little. Like it's searching for the right note.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.015
cast.text: Some say the world rebuilds because it's broken. Nonsense! It's practicing. Every musician knows you play it again until it's right.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.016
cast.text: There's a song with no ending, the ghosts say. They hum it all the time. I've tried to write the last line. It always slips away.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.017
cast.text: Who's the conductor? That's what I want to know. Somebody's waving the baton. I've just never heard them breathe.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.018
cast.text: Mortimer says the ghost choir sings a counting song. Well, I've played along with them. It counts down. Not up. Down.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.019
cast.text: The pumpkins all turn to face the same way just before a rebuild. Toward the middle of the world. Like an audience facing the stage.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.020
cast.text: I once played a note so low, the world rebuilt early. Or maybe that was a coincidence. I've been too nervous to try it again.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.021
cast.text: Every world has a rhythm. You can hear it in your footsteps. When the rhythm skips a beat, the countdown's not far away.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.022
cast.text: The organist in the cathedral thinks he plays the world's song. Well, I play it too. We just play it a little differently.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.023
cast.text: There's a fiddle string somewhere that, if you plucked it, would stop the world rebuilding. Or start it. I'm not sure which. I'm not looking.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.024
cast.text: I asked the Builder for a request once. I shouted it into the sky. The next world had a nicer stage. I'll take it.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.025
cast.text: The enemies out there move in time, have you noticed? Left, right, throw. Left, right, throw. Somebody taught them that dance.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.026
cast.text: The quiet between worlds is a rest, in music terms. And a rest isn't nothing. A rest is the music holding its breath.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.027
cast.text: Halloween never ends here. The pumpkins never rot, the candles never burn down. Like the world forgot to turn the page.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.028
cast.text: I found sheet music in a pumpkin once. Just one line, and the line said, and then again, and then again, and then again. It went on for pages.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.029
cast.text: Some nights I hear another fiddle, far off, playing the same tune as me, just a beat behind. I've never found the player.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.030
cast.text: Have you heard the world's mercy? It sounds like a held note. Just a long, warm, kind note. Then the world carries on.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.031
cast.text: Hazel says the world is a spell. Well, what's a spell but a song with very strict lyrics?

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.032
cast.text: If the world is a song, then you're the melody, friend. Everything else is the backing band.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.033
cast.text: The first world, they say, had only one sound in it. One note, held forever. Then someone got bored and added a beat.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.034
cast.text: I once tried to play the countdown backwards. One, two, three, four, five. Nothing happened. Then I sneezed, and the world rebuilt. Make of that what you will.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.035
cast.text: Every tune I play, the world plays back a little different. Like it's learning. Or like it's arguing.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.036
cast.text: The pumpkins whisper sometimes. Mostly about seeds. But once, I heard one say, the walker is the key. Which walker? It didn't say.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.037
cast.text: The skeleton band I used to play with all left, one world at a time. I hope they found a better gig.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.038
cast.text: The strings on my fiddle tighten all by themselves before a rebuild. Like the world tuning up.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.039
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds because nobody's clapped yet. Not properly. Somebody needs to give it a standing ovation.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.040
cast.text: Ever notice how the music never stops? Even between worlds, there's a hum. Somebody left the band playing.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.041
cast.text: I wrote a song about the mystery of the world. Twelve verses, no chorus, and it ends with a question mark.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.042
cast.text: The candles here flicker in time with the countdown. Five flickers, then darkness, then new candles. I don't know who lights them.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.043
cast.text: Captain Brine thinks the sea keeps the rhythm. Pendle thinks the clocks do. I think it's a drummer, somewhere deep down, who never gets any credit.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.044
cast.text: I tried to stay perfectly still once, to see if the world would wait. It didn't. The world doesn't wait for anyone. Except, sometimes, for you.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.045
cast.text: Some say there's a final world, the last verse, and when it's played, everything stops. I hope not. I like it here.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.046
cast.text: The spooky music isn't meant to scare you, friend. It's meant to keep you awake. Somebody wants you listening.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.047
cast.text: There's a little music box somewhere in every world. If you could find it and wind it, they say, you'd hear how it all began.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.048
cast.text: Pell the ghost swears the world is a dream. Well, who's dreaming? And do they like my music? That's what I want to know.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.049
cast.text: I've played at a thousand worlds, and every world claps a little differently. This one claps like rain.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.050
cast.text: The organ in the cathedral and my fiddle once played the same note at the very same moment. The whole world shivered. Then it rebuilt.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.051
cast.text: I heard a rumor that the Builder can't hear. That's why the world never sounds quite right to them, and they keep starting over.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.052
cast.text: Another rumor says the Builder hears everything, every wrong note, and that's why the world is never quite good enough for them.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.053
cast.text: Spooky places are the best places for secrets. Things whisper here that wouldn't dare whisper anywhere else.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.054
cast.text: I once found a door in the pumpkin patch. It opened onto the same pumpkin patch. But the music was coming from the other side, and it wasn't mine.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.055
cast.text: The world goes quiet for a single beat before the countdown. If you listen, you can hear it decide.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.056
cast.text: The witch's cat came by once and sat on my fiddle case. Wouldn't move. Just before the rebuild, it looked up at the sky and meowed. I'd love to know what it said.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.057
cast.text: Maybe the world isn't one song. Maybe it's a medley. A little of everything, stitched together, over and over.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.058
cast.text: Some folks find the countdown frightening. I find it exciting! It's the moment before the curtain goes up.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.059
cast.text: I asked the moon what the world's song is called. It said, ask me again in the next world. I did. It said the same thing.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.060
cast.text: I play a different tune every world, and every world the pumpkins hum along. They already know it. How do they already know it?

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.061
cast.text: If you ever hear a tune you've never heard before, out in the world, follow it. Somebody new might be playing. Or something old.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.062
cast.text: The skeleton key that opens the last door is a real skeleton's key. Ha! Or maybe that's just a rumor I started.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.063
cast.text: There's a tune that only plays in the quiet between worlds. I've heard four notes of it. I'd give my last string to hear the fifth.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.064
cast.text: I've got a pumpkin named Gourdon. He's my biggest fan. He has no choice. He's a pumpkin.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.065
cast.text: Every skeleton needs a hobby. Mine is music. And knitting. Mostly music.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.066
cast.text: The candles in the pumpkins blow out one by one right before the countdown. Five candles, five puffs. Then new candles, already lit.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.067
cast.text: I think the world is tuning itself. Every rebuild, it gets a tiny bit closer to the right pitch. One day, it'll be perfectly in tune. Then what?

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.068
cast.text: My fiddle has a crack in it from the very first world. The crack hums when the world changes. Like it remembers how it got there.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.069
cast.text: There's a rumor that the first sound in the first world was a fiddle string, plucked by accident. I'd love to think it was mine.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.070
cast.text: The bats in the belfry flap in time with my music. Except right before the rebuild. Then they flap in fives. Every time.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.071
cast.text: I played a duet with the wind once. The wind was surprisingly good. It played the same five notes everybody seems to know.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.072
cast.text: The spooky fog here is thickest when walkers arrive. It swirls around you like it's curious. Fog is nosy. All fog. Very nosy.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.073
cast.text: If you listen to the world's hum and my fiddle together, they make a chord. A sad, happy, unfinished chord. Like a question.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.074
cast.text: Some nights, the pumpkins glow without candles. Just a faint warm light. Like the world is lending them some of its own.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.075
cast.text: The world's mercy is the best encore of all. You think it's over, and then, surprise, one more song.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.076
cast.text: The grandest concert I ever played was between two worlds. Nobody heard it. But the quiet clapped. I'm sure it did.

cast.name: vc_fiddler.story.077
cast.text: I keep a list of every song the world has played. It's very long. And every song ends with the same note. Five.

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, love! Best stall in the market!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.002
cast.text: Hello, hello! Come and have a look!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.003
cast.text: This way, walker! Bargains and gossip, both free today!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.004
cast.text: Over here, by the apple cart!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.005
cast.text: Come along, love, follow my voice!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.006
cast.text: Roll up, roll up! Over here!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.007
cast.text: Hello, dear! This way, mind the cobbles.

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! I've something special put by for you.

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.009
cast.text: This way, past the baker's stall!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.010
cast.text: Come and see, come and see!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.011
cast.text: Hello there, love! Over here!

cast.name: vc_merchant.greet.012
cast.text: Fresh rumours, freshly picked! This way!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.001
cast.text: Love! Come back, you've forgotten your gift!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.002
cast.text: Over here again, dear. I've kept it safe for you.

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.003
cast.text: Back this way, past the apples!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.004
cast.text: Come back, love! It's paid for already!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.005
cast.text: Yoo hoo! Over here! Don't leave it behind!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.006
cast.text: This way, dear, follow my voice!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.007
cast.text: Come back! I don't do refunds, but I do do gifts!

cast.name: vc_merchant.call.008
cast.text: Over here again! It's still on the counter for you.

cast.name: vc_merchant.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are, love. No charge.

cast.name: vc_merchant.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, dear. On the house.

cast.name: vc_merchant.gift.003
cast.text: A little something from Marigold's stall.

cast.name: vc_merchant.gift.004
cast.text: For you, love. Don't tell the other traders.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.001
cast.text: I'm Marigold. I sell a bit of everything, and I hear a bit of everything too.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.002
cast.text: Apples, ribbons, candles, rumours. Rumours are my best sellers.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.003
cast.text: Mind the chickens, dear. They think they own the place.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.004
cast.text: I've had this stall since before the first world. Or so it feels. My feet certainly think so.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.005
cast.text: The baker next door burns everything. Every single world. It's a gift, really.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.006
cast.text: Haggling is half the fun, love. The other half is gossip.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.007
cast.text: I always know what the weather's doing. My knees tell me.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.008
cast.text: If you're buying, I'm selling. If you're not, I'm still chatting.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.009
cast.text: The village bell rings every hour. Nobody knows who rings it. Nobody minds, either.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.010
cast.text: You've a kind face, love. Well, a kind set of footsteps. That's what I go by.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.011
cast.text: Everyone who comes to my stall has a different story about why the world rebuilds. I write them all down. I've got a cart full now.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.012
cast.text: The best rumour I ever heard? That the world rebuilds because somebody, somewhere, keeps losing their keys and turning everything over to find them.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.013
cast.text: The village restocks itself every world. Every apple, every candle. I never order a thing. I'd love to meet the supplier.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.014
cast.text: Credits are a funny currency, love. No face on them, no mint mark. I've never been able to work out who's making them.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.015
cast.text: The market is busiest just before the countdown. Everyone hurrying, everyone buying. As if they know something's coming.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.016
cast.text: I sold a map once to a walker. A map of the world. She came back the next world and said it was perfect. For the last world.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.017
cast.text: Old Tobias at the tavern swears the streets rearrange themselves at night. Well, of course they do. The whole world does.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.018
cast.text: There's a stall at the far end of the market that's always closed. Shutters down. I've never seen it open. But I've heard someone inside, counting.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.019
cast.text: A traveller told me the world is a great market, and we're all the goods on the shelves. Being shuffled about. I didn't care for that one.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.020
cast.text: My grandmother had this stall before me. She said the world used to stay the same for days. Days! Can you imagine?

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.021
cast.text: The village has a well in the middle. Drop a coin in, and you never hear it land. Some say it lands in the next world.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.022
cast.text: I've noticed the cobblestones change pattern every world. But the path to my stall is always the same length. Funny, isn't it?

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.023
cast.text: They say the Builder visits the market in disguise. Buys one apple. Pays with a coin from a world that hasn't happened yet.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.024
cast.text: Mister Pendle the clockmaker says there's a timetable for the rebuilds. If there is, he won't sell me a copy.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.025
cast.text: The chickens always run in circles before a rebuild. Three times round the cart, then they hide. I've learned to pack up when they start.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.026
cast.text: I once tried to carry my stall into the next world. Packed it all on my back. Woke up in the new world, stall set up, everything in place. Back still aching.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.027
cast.text: Some folk think the enemies out there are stealing pieces of the world. I've never had a thing go missing. Except my good scissors. Who knows.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.028
cast.text: Every world, I find one thing on my stall I never put there. Last world it was a little silver bell. This world, a feather.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.029
cast.text: The village has a crier, but he only ever shouts one thing. All is well! All is well! Then the countdown starts. I don't think he's paying attention.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.030
cast.text: There's a rumour going round that the safe places are the world's pockets. Somewhere to keep the important bits safe while it shakes itself out.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.031
cast.text: I heard from a pedlar who heard from a sailor who heard from a fish, that something at the bottom of the sea is keeping count of the worlds.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.032
cast.text: They say a walker once bought the whole market, every last thing. Next world, it was all back. And the walker? Never heard of again. Probably still carrying it.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.033
cast.text: Hazel the witch buys herbs from me. She never says what they're for. Last time, she bought every bit of thyme I had. Thyme, love. Time.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.034
cast.text: You know what I think? I think the world rebuilds because it's restocking. Running low on something. And it hasn't found it yet.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.035
cast.text: Some walkers save up all their credits for something special. What, I always ask? They never know. The world never says what credits are really for.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.036
cast.text: The village gate opens onto the world every time, but it never opens onto the same world twice. I've stopped expecting the same view.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.037
cast.text: I keep a ledger. Every world, the totals come out exactly the same. Not near enough. Exactly. To the last penny. What does that tell you?

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.038
cast.text: The baker swears his bread rises in time with the world. When the bread's done, the world's done, he says. His bread is always done.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.039
cast.text: I asked a traveller where he'd come from. He said, the edge. I asked what was there. He said, a fence, and a sign. He wouldn't tell me what the sign said.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.040
cast.text: There's a song the children sing in the village square. Round and round the world goes, where it stops, nobody knows. Sweet, isn't it? A bit unsettling, now I think about it.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.041
cast.text: They say there's a coin with a face on it, the only one. Whoever finds it will know who made the world. I've checked every coin I've ever had.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.042
cast.text: The village is older than the labyrinths. I'm sure of it. The labyrinths were built around us, like a fence round a garden.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.043
cast.text: I've noticed the walkers sound a little different each world. More sure of themselves. Maybe the world is teaching you something, love.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.044
cast.text: When the world shows its mercy, the whole market goes quiet. Even the chickens. Like everyone's listening to the same good news.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.045
cast.text: The market sells everything except answers. Believe me, I've tried to stock them. They go stale far too quickly.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.046
cast.text: A man came by once and paid for an apple with a key. An old iron key. I've still got it. Nobody in the village has a lock it fits.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.047
cast.text: Some say the world rebuilds because it's untidy. I say, have you seen my stall? And the world doesn't rebuild that.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.048
cast.text: I used to think the countdown voice belonged to the village crier. Then I heard them both at once.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.049
cast.text: The bell in the church tower rings a different number of times every world. I've started writing the numbers down. They're not random. They're not anything I know, either.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.050
cast.text: The traders all have their own name for the rebuild. The Restock. The Shuffle. The Big Sweep. I call it closing time.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.051
cast.text: A pedlar told me there are other markets, in other worlds, all happening at once. And every one has a stall like mine, with a woman like me in it. Gives me a funny feeling.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.052
cast.text: Every world, someone leaves a basket of eggs at the edge of the village. No farm, no hens nearby. Just eggs. Fresh ones.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.053
cast.text: The village well whispers sometimes. Mostly about water. Once, it said a name. Your name, maybe. It was hard to hear.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.054
cast.text: They say the first world had only one shop, and it sold only one thing. A single question. Nobody could afford it.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.055
cast.text: Some folk believe the world rebuilds whenever someone tells a lie. Well, the market would be rebuilding every second, love.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.056
cast.text: The weathervane on the inn points the same way every world, no matter which way the wind blows. Toward the middle of everything.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.057
cast.text: I gave a gift to a walker once, and they gave me one back. A smooth stone, warm, humming. It's on the shelf. It goes quiet just before each rebuild.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.058
cast.text: I once overheard two travellers arguing about the Builder. One said they build the world for the walkers. The other said, then why do they keep knocking it down?

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.059
cast.text: Captain Brine buys rope from me every world. A great length of it. I asked what for. He said, to tie the world down. It hasn't worked yet.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.060
cast.text: You know the funny thing, love? Everyone's got a theory, and no one's got the answer. Best business there is, rumours.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.061
cast.text: My apples are the crunchiest in any world. I'd stake my stall on it.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.062
cast.text: Mind the goose by the well. She bites. Only walkers she likes, mind you. So she might bite you.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.063
cast.text: The market bell rings five times before the countdown. Then all the traders shout, last orders! Nobody knows why we do that. We just always have.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.064
cast.text: There's a fortune teller at the end of the lane. She never tells fortunes. She just says, ask me in the next world. Then the next world comes, and she says it again.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.065
cast.text: I keep a little box of things walkers have traded me. Buttons, string, a whistle that plays one note. Every world, the whistle plays a different note.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.066
cast.text: The cobbler in the village says every walker's footsteps sound a little different. Yours, love, sound like someone who's going to find something.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.067
cast.text: They say the market was the first place ever built, and the world grew around it like a town around a crossroads. Every road leads here, eventually.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.068
cast.text: The world's mercy sweeps through the market like a cool breeze on a hot day. Everyone stops and smiles. Then back to haggling.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.069
cast.text: The scales on my stall weigh things true, every world. Except once. They weighed nothing, and it came out heavy. I still can't work out what was on them.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.070
cast.text: There's a rumour the Builder trades in worlds. One world for another. Somewhere, there's a market where whole worlds are bought and sold.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.071
cast.text: The candlemaker's candles always burn for exactly one world. Light one at the start, and it goes out right at the countdown. He doesn't know how.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.072
cast.text: I've stopped trying to work out why the world rebuilds, love. I just make sure my stall is ready when it does. A good trader is always ready.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.073
cast.text: A little girl once gave me a drawing of the market. In it, every stall was empty, except mine. And in mine was someone I didn't know, smiling.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.074
cast.text: Every world, there's one coin in my till that's warm. Just one. Like someone was holding it a long time before they paid.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.075
cast.text: The tinker who sells pots says he's sold the same pot to Chef Rosalind a hundred times. She never remembers buying it. The pot remembers, he says.

cast.name: vc_merchant.story.076
cast.text: The village has a statue in the square. Nobody knows who it's of. Every world, the statue faces a different direction. Always toward the walker.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, young walker. Follow the lantern.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.002
cast.text: Evening! This way, by the fire.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.003
cast.text: Hello there. Over here, mind the step.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.004
cast.text: This way, friend. The kettle's on.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.005
cast.text: Over here! The night watch is always open.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.006
cast.text: Come in, come in, out of the dark.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.007
cast.text: Evening, walker. I'm by the window.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.008
cast.text: Follow my voice. Steady as you go.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.009
cast.text: Over here, friend. A warm seat is waiting.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.010
cast.text: Hello! This way, past the lamp post.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.011
cast.text: Come along. The streets are quiet, and so am I. Mostly.

cast.name: vc_watchman.greet.012
cast.text: Over here. I've been keeping an eye out for you.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.001
cast.text: Back this way, friend. I've still got your gift.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. Don't wander off in the dark.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.003
cast.text: Walker! Come back, you've left something behind.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.004
cast.text: This way, follow the lantern.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.005
cast.text: Come back in out of the cold. Your gift's waiting.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.006
cast.text: Over here! The night watch keeps things safe for you.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.007
cast.text: Steady now, back this way.

cast.name: vc_watchman.call.008
cast.text: Come back, friend. I'm not one to give up on a gift.

cast.name: vc_watchman.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. Kept it safe all night.

cast.name: vc_watchman.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, friend. You'll need it more than me.

cast.name: vc_watchman.gift.003
cast.text: A little something from the night watch.

cast.name: vc_watchman.gift.004
cast.text: For you. Mind how you go out there.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.001
cast.text: I'm Tobias. I keep the night watch. Somebody has to, and the night's always here.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.002
