cast.text: Have a seat, friend. The cocoa's hot and the stew is better than it smells.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.003
cast.text: I walk the same streets every night. They're never the same streets. It keeps the job interesting.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.004
cast.text: My lantern's been lit since before the first world. Never needed new oil. Don't ask me how.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.005
cast.text: Mind the cat by the door. She belongs to nobody and everybody.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.006
cast.text: The tavern's warm, the streets are cold, and I'm somewhere in between. Always have been.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.007
cast.text: I've got a little book where I write down everything odd I see at night. It's a very thick book.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.008
cast.text: All quiet out there, mostly. The trick is knowing which quiet is the good kind.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.009
cast.text: Old habits. I check every door twice. Even in a world that'll be gone in a few minutes.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.010
cast.text: Pull up a stool, walker. I'm not much for talking, but I'm good at listening.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.011
cast.text: I've walked these streets every night for longer than I can say, and I'll tell you this. They rearrange themselves. Every single world.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.012
cast.text: Every world, the city has one more street. I count them. I've never found where the new one goes.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.013
cast.text: I keep a logbook of the rebuilds. Time, weather, anything odd. There's always something odd. Never the same odd thing twice.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.014
cast.text: The lamps go out one by one just before the countdown. Not all at once. One by one. As if someone's walking down the street, blowing them out.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.015
cast.text: Folk in the tavern argue about the rebuild every night. The Builder, the dream, the spell. I just listen and pour the cocoa.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.016
cast.text: I've seen a figure at the end of my street, just before a rebuild. Tall, still, holding something. By the time I got close, the world had changed. I'm sure it meant no harm. It was waiting, I think, like the rest of us.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.017
cast.text: The clock in the square stops at the same time every night. Then the world rebuilds, and it starts again. Pendle won't say why.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.018
cast.text: There's a door at the end of Lantern Lane that's painted a different colour every world. I knocked once. The door knocked back, very politely.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.019
cast.text: A walker in the tavern told me the city is the oldest part of the world. Built first, and everything else grew out from it. I like that idea.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.020
cast.text: On quiet nights, I hear a sound under the cobbles. Like gears turning. Like the whole city is sitting on a very large clock.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.021
cast.text: Marigold at the market says the world rebuilds to restock. Well, the tavern's never short of anything. So what's it restocking?

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.022
cast.text: I found a letter once, under the tavern door. It said, keep watching. Nothing else. No name. It was in my own handwriting. I don't remember writing it.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.023
cast.text: I think the watchman's job is the same as the walker's. Keep your ears open. Notice what's changed. And never stop asking why.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.024
cast.text: The city sounds different the moment after a rebuild. Like a room just after someone's left it. The air's still moving.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.025
cast.text: The cat by the door always knows when a rebuild's coming. She stretches, yawns, and goes under the table. Every time.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.026
cast.text: They say the city was once a single street. One street, one lamp, one watchman. I've a feeling that watchman was me.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.027
cast.text: Some nights I hear trains from the station, but there are no tracks out that way. Mister Pendle says those are trains from another world, passing close.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.028
cast.text: The enemies never come into the tavern. Never. I've seen them stop at the doorstep and turn around. Something keeps them out.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.029
cast.text: I asked the oldest regular in the tavern why the world rebuilds. She finished her cocoa, set down the cup, and said, it's practising. Then she left.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.030
cast.text: The rain out there always falls from the same direction. From the middle of the world, outward. Like something's breathing out.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.031
cast.text: There's a rumour among the watchmen that the city is a puzzle, and when the right walker solves it, the world will stop rebuilding.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.032
cast.text: I don't know if I want the world to stop rebuilding. It's the one thing I can count on.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.033
cast.text: If you walk to the end of every street in the city, you come back to the tavern. Every street. Every time. I've tried.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.034
cast.text: The world's mercy came through the city once while I was on watch. Every lamp burned a little brighter. Then back to normal. Lovely, it was.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.035
cast.text: I wrote down every rumour I heard in the tavern for a whole world. Forty three rumours. Not one of them agreed with another.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.036
cast.text: The fog rolls in from the river just before a rebuild. Captain Brine says it's the sea's breath. Willa says it's the river's. I say it's damp, and leave it at that.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.037
cast.text: There's an empty chair in the corner of the tavern no one sits in. Every world, there's a cup of cocoa on the table in front of it. Still warm.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.038
cast.text: The bells in the city ring at odd hours. Once, they rang five times, slow, and the countdown started right after. Coincidence, I tell myself.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.039
cast.text: A traveller told me there's a city in every world, and a watchman in every city. I asked if they all look like me. She just smiled.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.040
cast.text: Some say the city was built by the Builder as a place to rest. Some say the Builder lives here. I've checked every house. Not yet found them in.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.041
cast.text: I've noticed something on my rounds. The city is always laid out a bit like a labyrinth. The labyrinths out there are always laid out a bit like a city.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.042
cast.text: On the stroke of every rebuild, the tavern sign swings, though there's no wind. As if somebody's just walked in.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.043
cast.text: The cobblestones are warm at night, even in winter. Something underneath is keeping them warm. Or something underneath is awake.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.044
cast.text: I used to think the countdown came from the clock tower. Then I stood in the tower and heard it coming from outside.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.045
cast.text: The night never ends here. I've been on watch so long, I've forgotten what morning sounds like. Wren says it sounds like birds. I'll take her word for it.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.046
cast.text: I once followed a stranger through the streets for an hour. Every corner, they were just ahead. At the last corner, they were gone. Just a lantern, left lit.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.047
cast.text: In the tavern, they tell a story about the first walker. She asked the world a question, and the world has been rebuilding ever since, trying to answer.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.048
cast.text: Some in the tavern say the first walker gave the world an answer, and the world didn't like it. I prefer the story where she asked a question.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.049
cast.text: Every world, the tavern has a new song painted over the fireplace. The words are always nearly the same. One word changes. I've been keeping track.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.050
cast.text: The street names change every world. Lantern Lane, Quiet Row, Five Bell Street. Last world, there was one called Why. I didn't walk down it.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.051
cast.text: The sound of the city at night is the best map I know. Shutters, footsteps, a kettle somewhere. When the sounds go strange, I know a rebuild's near.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.052
cast.text: Hazel came into the tavern once and ordered a cup of nothing. I poured it. She drank it. She said it tasted of the world before this one.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.053
cast.text: A walker told me she heard her own footsteps behind her, out in the city. When she stopped, they kept going. Then they turned a corner and were gone.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.054
cast.text: I think the city remembers you. Doors you've walked past open a little easier. Lamps you've passed burn a little longer.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.055
cast.text: The night watch has one rule. Whatever happens, keep the lantern lit. Nobody told me why. I've a feeling it matters.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.056
cast.text: They say if every lamp in the city goes out at once, the world won't come back. I've never let that happen. I'm not about to find out.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.057
cast.text: Sprocket says the city runs on gears. Hazel says magic. The cat says nothing. Of the three, I trust the cat most.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.058
cast.text: I hear the tavern's old piano play the same tune every night at closing. The tune ends right as the countdown begins. Every time.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.059
cast.text: Somewhere in this city, they say, is a window that looks out onto the space between worlds. I've looked through a thousand windows. Not that one, yet.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.060
cast.text: Mind the puddle by the door. It's been there since the first world. I've grown fond of it.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.061
cast.text: The fire in the tavern never goes out. I keep it fed. It keeps me warm. Good partnership.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.062
cast.text: The tavern's old clock chimes once per world. Always at the same moment. Just before the countdown. Then it stops, and waits for the next world.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.063
cast.text: I found a map of the city scratched into the bottom of a tavern table. Every world, the map is different. And it's always right.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.064
cast.text: The bus drivers stop by the tavern sometimes. They never sit. They never drink. They just stand by the door, listening. Then they go.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.065
cast.text: There's a street in the city where your footsteps echo twice. Once for you, and once for someone just behind you. I've never seen who.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.066
cast.text: The world's mercy sometimes comes to the tavern as laughter. Out of nowhere. Everyone starts laughing, and nobody knows why. Then the world has a little more time.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.067
cast.text: The cobblestones are laid in a spiral, if you follow them. Round and round, all the way to the middle of the city. Then the spiral starts again.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.068
cast.text: I've noticed the enemies avoid lamp light. Every one. They never step into the glow. I keep the lamps lit for the walkers' sake.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.069
cast.text: There's a rumour that the night watch was started by the first walker. To keep the lamps lit, so the next walker could find their way.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.070
cast.text: A walker once told me the city is just one big safe place, and the labyrinths are its garden walls. I rather liked that.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.071
cast.text: I keep a list of every face I've seen in the tavern. Different faces, every world. But one seat is always taken by someone who never says a word.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.072
cast.text: The city fountain runs backward just before a rebuild. Water going up instead of down. Then it stops, and the new world starts the fountain fresh.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.073
cast.text: The stars over the city are always arranged the same. A wide circle, with one bright star in the middle. Like a clock face, with no hands.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.074
cast.text: Every lamp post in the city has a number. I've counted them. The last number is always one higher than the world before. The city's keeping count.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.075
cast.text: I've worn the same coat on my rounds for a thousand worlds. It's never worn out. It's got a pocket I never use. Every world, there's a note inside. It says, thank you.

cast.name: vc_watchman.story.076
cast.text: The tavern keeper before me said the world will stop rebuilding when every walker has had a warm meal and a kind word. I'm doing my part.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, over here! You're right on time!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.002
cast.text: This way, please! Platform one, by the big clock!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.003
cast.text: Hello! Follow the ticking!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.004
cast.text: Ah, there you are! Over here, quick as you like!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.005
cast.text: This way, walker! Mind the gap!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Tick tock, don't be late!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.007
cast.text: Hello hello! By the ticket office!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.008
cast.text: Follow the ticking, and you'll find me!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.009
cast.text: Over here, please! I've a moment to spare. Just one.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.010
cast.text: This way! The next train is a gift, and it's leaving now!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.011
cast.text: Hello! Over here, under the clock!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.greet.012
cast.text: Come along, come along! Punctuality, please!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.001
cast.text: Walker! Come back, you've missed your gift!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! It's not departed yet!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.003
cast.text: This way, back to the big clock!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.004
cast.text: Come back, please! The gift is still on the platform!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.005
cast.text: Tick tock! Back this way!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.006
cast.text: You'll want this before the countdown! Over here!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.007
cast.text: Over here, please! Follow the ticking!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.call.008
cast.text: Come back! I've held it for you, right on schedule!

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. Exactly on time.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, please. Delivered to the minute.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.gift.003
cast.text: A gift from the station. Mind the gap on your way out.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.gift.004
cast.text: For you, with my compliments, and my timetable.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.001
cast.text: I'm Mister Pendle. Clockmaker, station master, and keeper of very precise opinions.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.002
cast.text: Every clock in this station is right. They just don't agree with each other.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.003
cast.text: The trains here run perfectly to time. Where they go is another matter entirely.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.004
cast.text: I've repaired every clock in every world. Twice. Some of them three times.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.005
cast.text: A gentleman should always carry a pocket watch. I carry five. One for each second of the countdown.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.006
cast.text: Tick, tock. Do you hear that? That's the sound of everything being exactly where it should be.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.007
cast.text: The station tea room sells excellent tea. The tea is late, but excellent.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.008
cast.text: I do not like surprises. Which is unfortunate, given where we live.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.009
cast.text: The departures board says, next train, soon. It has said that for a very long time.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.010
cast.text: Mind the platform edge, please. I polished it this morning. Or this world, at least.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.011
cast.text: The world runs on a clock, I'm certain of it. A great clock, somewhere deep. Every few minutes, it chimes, and everything resets.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.012
cast.text: I've timed every rebuild I've ever seen. Two minutes, four minutes, three and a half. Never the same. And yet I'm convinced there's a pattern.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.013
cast.text: The countdown always takes exactly five seconds. Not four point nine. Not five point one. Exactly five. Somebody very careful is counting.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.014
cast.text: The trains leave on time, every time. But no one has ever seen one arrive anywhere. The passengers never come back to tell me.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.015
cast.text: I once rode a train to the end of the line. When the doors opened, I was back at this platform. One minute earlier than I'd left.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.016
cast.text: All my clocks stop for one second just before the countdown begins. One second, every clock, all at once. Then they start again as if nothing happened.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.017
cast.text: They say the great clock that runs the world is under the ice. Lady Rime says it's under the sea. Captain Brine says it's under the city. I say it's late.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.018
cast.text: I've noticed the world rebuilds a little sooner each time it shows mercy. As if it has to borrow the time from somewhere.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.019
cast.text: Hazel thinks the world is a spell. Spells don't keep time, madam! I've told her. Spells are notoriously unpunctual.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.020
cast.text: There's a clock in the station with no hands. It ticks louder than all the others. I believe it's counting something other than time.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.021
cast.text: I wound every clock in the station backward once, to see what would happen. The next world started at five, then six, then seven. I didn't do that again.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.022
cast.text: There's a platform here I've never been able to reach. Platform zero. You can hear the trains there, but there's no stair down to it.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.023
cast.text: Every world, the timetable has one train I don't recognise. It always says the same destination. Elsewhere. Departing, now.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.024
cast.text: The ticking in this station is the world's heartbeat. I'm sure of it. When it skips, a rebuild is coming. I've never been wrong. Well, rarely.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.025
cast.text: I took apart a pocket watch I found under a bench. Inside was a tiny labyrinth instead of gears. It was still ticking.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.026
cast.text: The trains are full of passengers I never see board. Their footsteps get on. Their voices chat. And then, off they go. To where, I wonder.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.027
cast.text: I believe the world rebuilds because something in it is running fast. Like a clock that gains a minute every hour. Every so often, someone has to set it back. But who's setting it? And whose clock are they going by?

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.028
cast.text: The bus drivers out there keep remarkable time. Never a second late. I've always wanted to ask where they learned it. They never stop long enough.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.029
cast.text: There's a rumour among the porters that the first train ever to leave this station is still travelling. Round and round the world. Waiting for its stop.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.030
cast.text: I keep a log of every chime. Every world, the station clock chimes once more than the world before. One day it'll chime and not stop. What then, I wonder?

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.031
cast.text: Mortimer at the graveyard says the dates on his headstones are always tomorrow. I'd like to see those dates. I'd like to know whose tomorrow.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.032
cast.text: The world's time and my clocks' time don't quite match. The world is always slightly ahead. As if it already knows what happens next.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.033
cast.text: Every station has a lost property office. Mine is full of things from worlds that are gone. Umbrellas, gloves, a single shoe. And one very old map.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.034
cast.text: The map in lost property shows a world with no labyrinths in it. Just one long railway, circling a single building. No one has ever claimed it.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.035
cast.text: They say the rebuild happens when the world's clock strikes thirteen. I've listened very carefully. I've only ever counted twelve. Then five more.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.036
cast.text: I once asked a passenger where she was travelling. She said, back. Back where, I asked. Back to the start, she said. Then the doors closed.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.037
cast.text: Precision is the key to everything. If I could time the rebuilds perfectly, I could tell you exactly when the next one comes. I can't. It's terribly annoying.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.038
cast.text: The pigeons in the station always settle on the clock just before a rebuild. All of them, at once. They know. Pigeons always know.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.039
cast.text: If time keeps starting over, then are we getting any older? I've checked. I have not found a single new grey hair. Make of that what you will.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.040
cast.text: The trains run under the labyrinths, you know. Deep down. If you put your ear to a wall out there, you can sometimes hear them pass.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.041
cast.text: The station has a waiting room nobody ever leaves. I've looked in. Everyone's sitting very patiently, with their tickets, listening for something.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.042
cast.text: Sprocket and I once argued for a whole world about whether the world is a clock or an engine. Then it rebuilt, and we had to start the argument again.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.043
cast.text: The clock tower in the city chimes with my clocks, but always half a second late. Half a second, every world. Something's dragging it behind.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.044
cast.text: I have a theory that every world lasts exactly as long as it needs to. Not a second more. The trouble is, I don't know what it needs to do.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.045
cast.text: The departure board flickered once, just before a rebuild. For a moment it read, thank you for travelling. Then it went back to saying soon.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.046
cast.text: I found a ticket on the platform with no destination printed on it. Just a date. A date so far ahead, there's no calendar for it yet.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.047
cast.text: The walkers who come through here are always in a hurry. Quite right. The world won't wait. Except, sometimes, it does. That's the mercy, I suppose.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.048
cast.text: Somewhere, I believe, there's a clockmaker who makes the world's clock. And somewhere, I suspect, there's a clockmaker who makes that clockmaker's clock.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.049
cast.text: The tunnels at the end of the platforms go on into darkness. I've walked one. It ended at a wall with a clock on it. Showing the time, five seconds from now.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.050
cast.text: Every train whistle in the station is in the same key as the ghost choir's song. I checked. It's a very strange key. It doesn't sound finished.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.051
cast.text: I've had the same cup of tea on my desk for a thousand worlds. It's never gone cold. I find that more troubling than the rebuilding, frankly.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.052
cast.text: There's a rumour the world will stop rebuilding when someone arrives exactly on time. On time for what, nobody knows. I'm trying anyway.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.053
cast.text: A porter told me the world isn't rebuilding. It's arriving. Again and again, at a station somewhere, and we're the passengers.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.054
cast.text: I measured the silence between worlds once. It lasted no time at all. And yet it felt like a long afternoon.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.055
cast.text: Each clock in my station shows a different time, and each one is correct. For a different world. I'm only sure which one is ours about half the time.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.056
cast.text: The great clock under the world must be wound. That's what I believe. And somebody has been winding it, faithfully, for a very long time.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.057
cast.text: Pell the ghost says the countdown is like a game of hide and seek. Well, if it is, I'd like the seeker to keep to a timetable.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.058
cast.text: The trains always slow down when they pass the safe places. As if the drivers know someone's listening.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.059
cast.text: One should always wind one's watch before breakfast. And after breakfast. And whenever one is nervous.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.060
cast.text: The station cat sleeps on the timetable. She is never late for anything. I respect her enormously.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.061
cast.text: The great clock under the world, I believe, has only one hand. And it points to now. Always now. That's the trouble.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.062
cast.text: Every world, I set my watch by the first train whistle. Every world, the whistle comes exactly five seconds after the rebuild. Never four. Never six.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.063
cast.text: I have found that the world's mercy always arrives at a quarter past something. Never on the hour. The world has a sense of style.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.064
cast.text: The station has a clock face on the floor, under the dust. I swept it once. The hands pointed to a time that doesn't exist. Thirteen minutes to nothing.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.065
cast.text: A passenger left a pocket watch on the bench. Inside the lid was engraved, for when the time comes. It doesn't say when that is.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.066
cast.text: The trains whistle a chord as they leave. Every world, the chord is one note closer to finished. Ambrose agrees. He's been listening too.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.067
cast.text: I am quite certain that time here runs in circles. Not straight lines. Circles. Which means we'll meet again, and again, and again.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.068
cast.text: Hazel once asked me to fix her clock. Inside, there were no gears at all. Just a tiny voice, counting very patiently.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.069
cast.text: Every clock I repair, I find the same mark scratched inside. A little door. Someone else has repaired these clocks before me. Many times.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.070
cast.text: The rails hum before a train arrives. Before a rebuild, the rails hum too. But no train ever comes. Just the world.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.071
cast.text: They say there's a clock in the middle of the world that's never been wound. It runs anyway. On what, nobody knows.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.072
cast.text: I asked the station cat what time it was. She yawned and went back to sleep. Possibly the wisest answer I've ever received.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.073
cast.text: I've noticed the countdown never interrupts a train mid departure. The world waits for the doors to close. Very considerate.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.074
cast.text: The timetable has a train at the very bottom, in tiny print. The last train. It has no time listed. Just a note. When you're ready.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.075
cast.text: Every tick is a little piece of the world going by. I like to think the world collects them all somewhere. A great jar of ticks.

cast.name: vc_clockmaker.story.076
cast.text: I believe each world is exactly as long as a good train journey. Long enough to look out of the window. Not long enough to get bored.

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, hon! Follow the sizzle!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.002
cast.text: This way! Kitchen's open!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.003
cast.text: Hey there! By the stove, come on in!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.004
cast.text: Over here! Mind the hot pans!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.005
cast.text: Yes chef! I mean, hello! This way!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.006
cast.text: Come on back, the kitchen's this way!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.007
cast.text: Over here, sweetie! Something smells good, right?

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.008
cast.text: Follow your nose, and your ears! Over here!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.009
cast.text: Hey! Come in, come in, out of the cold!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.010
cast.text: This way, by the big pot!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've got something cooking for you!

cast.name: vc_chef.greet.012
cast.text: Hello, hungry walker! Over here!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.001
cast.text: Hey, come back! Your order's up!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! It's still warm!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.003
cast.text: Don't walk out on the chef! Come back!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.004
cast.text: This way, follow the sizzle!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.005
cast.text: Order up! Back this way, hon!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.006
cast.text: Come back! I don't let anything go to waste!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.007
cast.text: Over here! Your gift's on the pass!

cast.name: vc_chef.call.008
cast.text: Back to the kitchen, sweetie! It's waiting for you!

cast.name: vc_chef.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go, hon. Fresh off the stove.

cast.name: vc_chef.gift.002
cast.text: Order up! This one's for you.

cast.name: vc_chef.gift.003
cast.text: Take it, sweetie. Chef's special.

cast.name: vc_chef.gift.004
cast.text: For you. Compliments of the kitchen.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.001
cast.text: I'm Chef Rosalind. Best kitchen in the whole world. Every world, actually.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.002
cast.text: Don't touch that pan. Or that one. Actually, just stand right there.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.003
cast.text: Hear that sizzle? That's the sound of happiness, hon.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.004
cast.text: I've cooked for walkers, ghosts, and one very hungry witch. The witch tips best.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.005
cast.text: Salt, pepper, patience. That's all a good cook needs. And a fire extinguisher.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.006
cast.text: My kitchen's never empty. The pots refill themselves. I'm not complaining.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.007
cast.text: I've been chopping onions since before the first world. Still makes me cry.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.008
cast.text: Everybody ends up in the kitchen eventually. It's the warmest room in any world.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.009
cast.text: Taste this. No, wait, it's still too hot. Okay, now. No. Wait.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.010
cast.text: A good kitchen is loud, hon. Pots clanging, oil popping. Quiet kitchens worry me.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.011
cast.text: You want my theory? The world is a recipe. And somebody keeps tasting it and saying, nope, not yet, start again.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.012
cast.text: Every world, my pantry restocks itself. Same ingredients. But every world they taste a little different. Like the world's adjusting the seasoning.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.013
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Big Stir. Everything goes in the pot, round and round, and out comes a brand new world.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.014
cast.text: The oil always pops five times right before the countdown. Pop, pop, pop, pop, pop. Then here we go again.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.015
cast.text: Hazel thinks the world is a spell. Honey, a spell is just a recipe with fancier words.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.016
cast.text: There's a cookbook on my shelf I've never been able to open. The cover just says, the world, serves everyone.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.017
cast.text: Somebody's cooking the world, I'm sure of it. I've smelled it. Just before a rebuild, the air smells like fresh bread.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.018
cast.text: The kitchen timers all go off together right before the countdown. I never set them. Somebody's timing something.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.019
cast.text: My grandmother said the first world was just one ingredient. Plain. And then someone added a pinch of something, and it's never stopped changing.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.020
cast.text: I've cooked a thousand meals, and I've never made the same dish twice. Not on purpose. The world just won't let me.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.021
cast.text: There's a back door in this kitchen that opens onto a different alley every world. Sometimes a different world, I think. I keep it shut.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.022
cast.text: Juniper at the coffee shop says the world refills like a coffee cup. Well, who's pouring? That's what I want to know.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.023
cast.text: Somebody leaves an empty plate on my counter every world. Licked clean. I never cooked anything for it. Who's eating, hon?

cast.name: vc_chef.story.024
cast.text: I tried to cook a dish that would last into the next world. Slow roasted. Started it right after a rebuild. The countdown came, and the oven was empty. Still warm.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.025
cast.text: The secret ingredient of the world, they say, is a sound. Something you can only hear when everything else goes quiet. I've never had a quiet kitchen long enough to hear it.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.026
cast.text: The enemies out there never come in the kitchen. I think they're scared of my rolling pin. Smart enemies.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.027
cast.text: I've got a theory about the world's mercy. It's like when you take a pot off the heat just in time. Somebody's watching the stove.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.028
cast.text: Every chef has a signature dish. Maybe the world's signature dish is the rebuild itself. Maybe it's showing off.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.029
cast.text: Sometimes the pots rattle on their own, and the sound is almost like a word. I've heard it say, again. Just that. Again.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.030
cast.text: They say the Builder eats one meal in every world, and that's how they decide if the world was any good. I'd love to cook for them. Just once.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.031
cast.text: I keep a little notebook of the walkers who come through. What they asked, what they said. They all ask the same question. Why does it all change?

cast.name: vc_chef.story.032
cast.text: When walkers ask me why the world keeps changing, my answer changes every world. Last world, I said the world is hungry. This world, I think the world is lonely. Next world, who knows.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.033
cast.text: The sizzling oil sounds just like rain. Or applause. Depends on my mood. Right before a rebuild, it always sounds like applause.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.034
cast.text: Did you know the world tastes different after it shows mercy? A little sweeter. I'm not making that up. Ask anyone in a kitchen.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.035
cast.text: There's a fridge in the back that's always cold inside, even when the power's out. Lady Rime says it's a piece of her ice cave. I never ordered ice.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.036
cast.text: I heard a rumor that every world is cooked in the same pot. A great big pot at the bottom of everything. And the soup never runs out.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.037
cast.text: I dropped a spoon down the drain once, and it came back up in the sink, next world. Shiny, and bent into a question mark.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.038
cast.text: Every kitchen I've ever worked in had a bell for when the food is ready. Mine rings by itself, right after every rebuild. Order up, world.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.039
cast.text: Here's what bugs me, hon. If the world keeps rebuilding, who washes up after? Somebody does. Every world, my kitchen is spotless.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.040
cast.text: Some cooks say the world rebuilds because it burned. Burnt worlds go in the bin. Fresh worlds come out. I don't buy it. My worlds never burn.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.041
cast.text: There's a little door under the stove I've never opened. It's warm. And sometimes, from behind it, I hear somebody humming my recipes.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.042
cast.text: The walkers out there carry ammo and potions. You know what nobody carries? A sandwich. Somebody should make that a gift.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.043
cast.text: The steam from the big pot makes shapes sometimes. Last world, it made a door. This world, it made a question mark. I'm not reading into it. Much.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.044
cast.text: Every time the world rebuilds, the knives on my rack are in a different order. Same knives. Different order. Like someone was looking for one in particular.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.045
cast.text: They tell a story in the kitchens. The world is a soup that somebody's trying to get just right for a guest who hasn't arrived yet. Every rebuild is another try. I think you might be the guest, hon. Don't let it go to your head.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.046
cast.text: The tastiest thing in the world is a question with no answer. You can chew on it forever.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.047
cast.text: There's a recipe card stuck to the back of my oven. It's in my handwriting. It says, step one, wait. Step two, listen. There's no step three.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.048
cast.text: Old Hollis by the fire says the world was cooked over a campfire, long ago, by someone telling stories. Sweet man. I don't believe a word.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.049
cast.text: I once burned a whole tray of biscuits, and the world rebuilt before I could throw them out. In the next world, they were perfect. I'm still suspicious.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.050
cast.text: Every pot in my kitchen boils at a slightly different speed. I've timed them. The last one always boils over right as the countdown starts.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.051
cast.text: Some nights I hear dishes clattering in an empty restaurant next door. There is no restaurant next door. There's just the world.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.052
cast.text: Mister Pendle says the world runs on a clock. Clocks are fine for eggs, hon. You can't run a whole world on an egg timer.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.053
cast.text: The world's like bread dough. You punch it down, and it rises again. Every time. I just want to know who's kneading it.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.054
cast.text: A walker once asked me for the recipe for the world. I said, sure, hon. Take everything, shake it up, and don't ever let it settle.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.055
cast.text: The fryer bubbles louder near walkers. I think the oil likes company. Or it's trying to warn me about something.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.056
cast.text: I asked the oven why everything keeps changing. It went ding. Not helpful, oven.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.057
cast.text: Some chefs say there's one last dish to be cooked, and when it's done, the world will finally sit down and eat. I hope I get to make it.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.058
cast.text: Wash your hands before you touch anything, hon. Even in a brand new world.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.059
cast.text: I've got a wooden spoon I've used since the first world. It's seen things. It's stirred things.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.060
cast.text: The salt in my kitchen always runs out right before the countdown. Every world. Somebody's using it. Somebody with a big appetite.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.061
cast.text: I've got a cast iron pan older than the world. Seasoned with a thousand worlds of cooking. If that pan could talk, it'd know everything.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.062
cast.text: The fridge hums the same note as the ghost choir. Low and steady. I didn't notice until Jangles pointed it out. Now I can't stop hearing it.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.063
cast.text: I tried cooking the world's mercy into a soup. I just added a pinch of hope and stirred slowly. It tasted wonderful. I'll never be able to make it again.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.064
cast.text: The ovens in the restaurant kitchen all preheat themselves right after a rebuild. Ready to cook. Somebody wants this kitchen busy.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.065
cast.text: There's a menu in the restaurant from a world long gone. Every dish on it is called a question. The first world question, the five second question.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.066
cast.text: The garbage disposal makes a sound like someone saying, more. Every time. More what? More worlds? More food? I don't know.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.067
cast.text: I keep a pinch of every spice I've ever found. One spice shows up only once every hundred worlds. It smells like the sea and tastes like the stars.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.068
cast.text: Every chef I know has a different theory. The pastry chef thinks the world is rising. The grill cook thinks it's charred. I think it's still simmering.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.069
cast.text: The kitchen door swings by itself right before the countdown. Five times. In, out, in, out, in. Like somebody checking on the food.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.070
cast.text: Somebody wrote a recipe on the kitchen wall in chalk. It says, take one world, add one walker, stir until curious. Serves everyone.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.071
cast.text: The sizzle of the oil gets faster and faster before a rebuild. Like a drum roll. Then the world changes, and the oil is fresh and quiet.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.072
cast.text: The walkers who come in here are always hungry for answers. I can't serve answers, hon. But I can give you something warm. That's a start.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.073
cast.text: There's an old cookbook with a chapter called, what to do when the world ends. The chapter is just one word. Eat.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.074
cast.text: I asked Hazel if her cauldron and my pots are related. She said, distant cousins. Then she wouldn't say anything else.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.075
cast.text: I baked a cake in the shape of the world once. It came out of the oven in a completely different shape. A labyrinth. I didn't bake a labyrinth.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.076
cast.text: Every world, there's a new knife in the drawer I don't recognize. Very sharp, very old. Engraved on the handle, a tiny door.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.077
cast.text: The kitchen is the heart of every home, they say. Maybe that's why the world always rebuilds one. It needs a heart.

cast.name: vc_chef.story.078
cast.text: I've got a feeling the world is cooking something big. Something slow. Something that takes a thousand worlds to get right.

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.001
cast.text: Hi! Over here, at the counter!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.002
cast.text: Hey there! This way, come on in!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.003
cast.text: Welcome! Over here, I'll take your order!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.004
cast.text: Hi hi! Follow the coffee smell!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.005
cast.text: Over here! No line today!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.006
cast.text: Hey! By the register! This way!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.007
cast.text: Come on in! Grab a seat, I'm over here!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.008
cast.text: Hi there! Over here, next to the fries!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.009
cast.text: This way! The coffee's fresh!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.010
cast.text: Hello! Over here, friend!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.011
cast.text: Next customer! That's you! Over here!

cast.name: vc_barista.greet.012
cast.text: Hey! I saved you a spot! Over here!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.001
cast.text: Hey, come back! You forgot your order!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.002
cast.text: Over here! It's still on the counter!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.003
cast.text: Wait! Your gift! Come back!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.004
cast.text: This way, back to the register!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.005
cast.text: Come back! I promise it's fresh!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.006
cast.text: Over here again! Order for the walker!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.007
cast.text: Hey! Don't leave it behind! This way!

cast.name: vc_barista.call.008
cast.text: Back to the counter! It's waiting for you!

cast.name: vc_barista.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go! Enjoy!

cast.name: vc_barista.gift.002
cast.text: One gift, to go!

cast.name: vc_barista.gift.003
cast.text: This one's on me!

cast.name: vc_barista.gift.004
cast.text: For you! Have a great world!

cast.name: vc_barista.story.001
cast.text: Hi! I'm Juniper. I make the coffee, I flip the burgers, and I hear everything.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.002
cast.text: Welcome! Sit anywhere. All the seats are the same. Well, except that one. It wobbles.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.003
cast.text: Our special today is the same as every day. It's very special.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.004
cast.text: Do you want fries with that? I always have to ask. It's the rule.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.005
cast.text: I've worked here since before the first world, I think. My name tag says so. It's a very old name tag.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.006
cast.text: The coffee machine makes a noise like a sleepy dragon. I named it Pancake.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.007
cast.text: It's never busy, but it's never empty either. There's always someone, somewhere, ordering something.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.008
cast.text: If you ever need a break from the labyrinths, the booth by the window is the comfiest.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.009
cast.text: The burger grill sounds like rain. I like listening to it on slow days.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.010
cast.text: I try to remember everyone's order. You haven't ordered yet. I'm still going to remember you.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.011
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Refill. The world empties out, and then it's poured fresh. Like coffee.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.012
cast.text: All my regulars have a theory about the world. The man with the hat thinks it's a dream. The lady with the scarf thinks it's a test. I think it's just really busy.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.013
cast.text: The milkshake machine starts whirring all by itself right before the countdown. Five whirs. Then everything changes.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.014
cast.text: Every world, someone orders the same thing. A cup of black coffee and a question. I bring the coffee. I've never figured out the question.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.015
cast.text: Somebody leaves a tip on table four every world. One credit. Nobody ever sits at table four.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.016
cast.text: I asked the coffee machine why the world keeps changing. It made a big gurgle. I think it was trying.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.017
cast.text: The receipts print things sometimes. Not orders. Words. Last world, a receipt just said, not yet. This world, it said, almost.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.018
cast.text: Chef Rosalind says the world is a recipe. I think it's more like a menu. There's a ton of options, and somebody keeps changing their mind.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.019
cast.text: The drive through speaker crackles sometimes when nobody's there. I hear somebody breathing. Then they say, never mind, and drive off.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.020
cast.text: The fast food place and the coffee shop are always next to each other, every world. Even when everything else moves. Isn't that weird?

cast.name: vc_barista.story.021
cast.text: I heard from a regular who heard from a bus driver, that the bus drivers know why the world rebuilds. The bus drivers don't talk, though.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.022
cast.text: Every world, the menu board has one new item on it. Nobody can order it. Last world, it was called The Answer. Sold out.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.023
cast.text: The ice in the soda machine never melts. Not even after the rebuild. Lady Rime brought it once. She never said where from.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.024
cast.text: I've noticed the walkers who come in are a bit braver every world. Like the world is making you stronger on purpose.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.025
cast.text: Do you ever think the world is a game, and we're all in it? My manager says don't think that on the clock.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.026
cast.text: My manager is a voice on the phone. I've never met him. He always calls right after the rebuild to ask if everything's okay.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.027
cast.text: The burger flipper beeps when it's done. It beeps five times. Then the countdown starts. I've started flipping really fast.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.028
cast.text: There's a door marked staff only that I've never opened. I am staff. It still won't open for me.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.029
cast.text: I left a note on the counter for the Builder once. It said, thanks for the nice coffee shop. Next world, the note said, you're welcome. Pretty sure that was the Builder. Or a very polite customer.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.030
cast.text: The world's mercy is like a free refill. You didn't ask for it, but there it is, and it's warm.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.031
cast.text: Sometimes the jukebox plays a song nobody chose. A slow, humming song. It's the same song the ghost choir sings, Jangles told me.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.032
cast.text: Hazel comes in for a cup of hot water and nothing else. She says she brings her own magic. She tips in feathers.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.033
cast.text: A customer told me the world is a giant vending machine. You put something in, and something random comes out. I didn't love that theory.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.034
cast.text: The register counts the credits perfectly every world. Except it's always one credit over. Every world. Where does that one come from?

cast.name: vc_barista.story.035
cast.text: The fryer sizzles a bit like a whisper. I swear it said my name once. Then again, maybe it said fries.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.036
cast.text: Every world, there's a lost and found box behind the counter, and it's full of stuff I've never seen. Keys, gloves, and a compass that points down. Like whatever it wants you to find is underneath everything.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.037
cast.text: They say there was a coffee shop in the very first world. Just one. And the first walker sat in it and wondered why. And that's when it all began.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.038
cast.text: I love the moment after the rebuild. Everything smells new. The coffee's fresh, the floor's clean, the world's wide open.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.039
cast.text: The regulars argue about whether the enemies are part of the world or visitors like you. I think they're the world's way of keeping you moving.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.040
cast.text: Some nights, the neon sign outside flickers in a pattern. Long, short, short, long. I've been trying to decode it. So far it spells nothing. Or maybe it spells nothing on purpose.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.041
cast.text: I wrote down every regular's theory on napkins. I've got a whole drawer of napkins. If you read them all together, they almost make sense. Almost.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.042
cast.text: The fast food bags rustle by themselves sometimes, all at the same time. Like the whole world just shivered.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.043
cast.text: A walker once asked me if I ever get tired of the world changing. Honestly? No. It means every shift is my first shift.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.044
cast.text: There's a rumor the world will stop rebuilding when someone orders the perfect meal. Nobody knows what the perfect meal is. People keep trying.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.045
cast.text: The coffee cups have a tiny drawing at the bottom. A labyrinth. In every world, the path through it is different.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.046
cast.text: I think the coffee shop is the world's favorite place. It always keeps it. It always puts it back nice.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.047
cast.text: Mister Pendle comes in for tea and checks his watch the whole time. He says the world is running slow today. Then fast. Then slow.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.048
cast.text: Somebody once ordered five of everything. Right before a rebuild. Then the world changed, and their order vanished. I still wonder who they were.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.049
cast.text: The tables wobble just before the countdown. All of them. Not just the wobbly one. That's how I know.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.050
cast.text: Some people say the safe places are like the world's break room. Where the world rests, between shifts. I like that one.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.051
cast.text: My regulars say I should ask the Builder for a raise. I would, if I knew where to find them. I'd also ask about the wobbly table.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.052
cast.text: There's a cup on the top shelf that's always full. Hot chocolate. I never made it. I never drink it. Every world, it's still warm.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.053
cast.text: The music in the burger place loops. Same playlist, every world. But the last song is always a little different. Like it's still being written.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.054
cast.text: If the world rebuilds because it's looking for something, I hope it's looking for a good cup of coffee. Because I've got that covered.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.055
cast.text: Pro tip, the muffins are best right after a rebuild. Fresh from the oven. Every time.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.056
cast.text: I love the sound of the milk steamer. It sounds like a tiny train. Pendle doesn't agree.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.057
cast.text: Table four is reserved. For who? Nobody knows. It just is.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.058
cast.text: The coffee beans are always fresh, every world. I've never had a delivery. The bags are just there, full, every morning.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.059
cast.text: I asked the bus drivers if they want a coffee. They nodded. That's the most any of them has ever said. They didn't drink it.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.060
cast.text: The world's best kept secret is the back booth. Sit there long enough, and you can hear the whole world whispering through the vent.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.061
cast.text: Somebody carved a tiny question mark under every table. Every world. New tables, same question marks. I never catch who does it.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.062
cast.text: I tried to write the rebuild times on the chalkboard. The chalk ran out at exactly five every time. Weird chalk.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.063
cast.text: The espresso machine hisses five times before every countdown. Pancake knows something. That dragon always knows something.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.064
cast.text: A man in a long coat comes in right after every rebuild. He orders a cup of tea and asks, how was the last one? Then he leaves. I never know what to say.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.065
cast.text: Regulars say the coffee tastes like whatever world you need. Strong in a hard world, sweet in a nice one. I think the beans are magic. Don't tell Hazel.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.066
cast.text: There's a rumor that the coffee shop is the one place the Builder takes a break. I've watched every customer. They all look like they need a break.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.067
cast.text: My name tag has a different name on it every world. It always says Juniper. But underneath, in tiny letters, a different name. I've never recognized any of them.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.068
cast.text: The ice machine drops ice at exactly the moment of the rebuild. Clunk. Like the world's last word.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.069
cast.text: Some walkers sit in the coffee shop for a whole world, just listening. I don't blame them. It's the best place to hear the world change.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.070
cast.text: I had a dream I served coffee to the whole world at once. Everyone at one long table. And somebody at the end stood up and said, now I'll tell you why. Then I woke up.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.071
cast.text: Rosalind says the world is a recipe. Well, every coffee is a recipe too. And no two cups are ever the same. Maybe that's the point.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.072
cast.text: I keep a jar for tips. Every world, there's a strange coin in it. No face, no name, just a little drawing of a door.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.073
cast.text: The fry cook here before me left a note. It said, the fries know. Know what? I've asked the fries. They just sizzle.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.074
cast.text: The jukebox has a song called, the last world. Nobody's ever been able to play it. The button's stuck.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.075
cast.text: Sometimes the coffee shop is full of whispers, but there's nobody here. Just conversations from other worlds, leaking through.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.076
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds because it gets bored, like a kid. And honestly, if I had to be the same world every day, I'd get bored too.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.077
cast.text: The coffee cup on table four is always half full when I come in. Never empty, never full. Halfway. Like someone is still thinking.

cast.name: vc_barista.story.078
cast.text: I always say, have a great world, instead of have a great day. A walker told me it's the nicest thing anyone's said to them. Here, it really means something.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.001
cast.text: Ho ho! Over here, by the fire!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.002
cast.text: Come and warm your hands, young one! This way!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Pull up a log!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.004
cast.text: Hello, hello! Follow the crackle!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.005
cast.text: Ho ho ho! There you are! Come closer!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.006
cast.text: This way, little walker! The fire's lovely tonight!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.007
cast.text: Over here, by the warm glow!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.008
cast.text: Come sit with old Hollis a while!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.009
cast.text: Hello there! Mind the sparks, and come on over!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.010
cast.text: Over here! I've a story and a present!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.011
cast.text: This way! Follow the crackling!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.greet.012
cast.text: Ho ho! Come in from the cold!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.001
cast.text: Ho ho! Come back, young one! I've still got your present!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! By the fire!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.003
cast.text: Come back and get warm! Your gift's waiting!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.004
cast.text: This way, follow the crackle!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.005
cast.text: Don't run off! Old Hollis has something for you!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.006
cast.text: Back by the fire, little walker!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.007
cast.text: Ho ho! You forgot your present! Over here!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.call.008
cast.text: Come back now! The fire's still going!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.gift.001
cast.text: Ho ho! Here you are, young one!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, with an old man's blessing.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.gift.003
cast.text: A present from Grandpa Hollis! Use it well!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.gift.004
cast.text: For you! Now off you go, and come back with a story!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.001
cast.text: I'm Hollis. Grandpa Hollis, everybody calls me. I tell stories, and I keep the fire going.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.002
cast.text: Ho ho! Sit down, sit down. The log's a bit lumpy, but it's warm.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.003
cast.text: Nothing better than a crackling fire and a good story. Except maybe a mug of cocoa. I've got that too.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.004
cast.text: I've told stories by this fire for longer than I can remember. Which, at my age, isn't saying much! Ho ho!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.005
cast.text: Toast a marshmallow? Careful now, they catch fast.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.006
cast.text: My beard's been singed eleven times. Fire and I are old friends. We tease each other.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.007
cast.text: The stars are out tonight. They're always out tonight. Ho ho!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.008
cast.text: Listen to that crackle. Every fire tells its own story, if you're patient.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.009
cast.text: I'm not a wizard, young one. I'm just old. It's very similar, but with more naps.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.010
cast.text: The fireplace in the cottage and the campfire in the woods are the same fire, you know. It just likes a change of scenery.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.011
cast.text: Let me tell you the oldest story I know. Once, there was a world that stayed the same forever. And it was so lonely, it wished to be new. And its wish came true. Again and again.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.012
cast.text: There's a story where the world never wished to change at all. Someone else wished it for the world. And they never told anyone who.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.013
cast.text: The fire always flares up just before the countdown. A big whoosh of sparks. Like it's waving goodbye.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.014
cast.text: I tell a different story every world, and here's the funny thing. The stories come true, a little bit, in the next world. Just a little.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.015
cast.text: My grandfather told me the world rebuilds because it's a book being read aloud, and every time someone turns the page, there's a whole new chapter. Who's reading it, I asked him. He just winked. Ho ho!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.016
cast.text: The fire sings sometimes. A little hissing tune. It's the same tune the ghost choir sings, slower. I think the whole world knows that song.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.017
cast.text: There's a legend about the first walker. She sat by a fire like this one and asked, why does it all change? And the fire said, so you'll never stop listening.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.018
cast.text: Some say the Builder is a kind old soul who just loves building. Can't stop. Every time they finish, they get excited and start again.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.019
cast.text: Some say the Builder is a child, playing with blocks. Building, knocking down, building again. Children are like that. Ho ho!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.020
cast.text: The sparks fly up and never come down. Where do they go? Up to the next world, I think, to light the new fires.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.021
cast.text: I once kept the fire going right through a rebuild. Fed it a log at four, three, two, one. Next world, the same log was burning. I'll never forget it.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.022
cast.text: The ashes in this fireplace never pile up. I've never once swept them. Somebody's tidying up between worlds.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.023
cast.text: Hazel and I have argued about the world for a hundred worlds. She says spell. I say story. We agree on one thing. Nobody knows the ending.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.024
cast.text: Here's a riddle for you. What's always new, but older than anything? The world, young one. The world.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.025
cast.text: There's a story the woodcutters tell. Deep in the forest, there's a tree that never changes when the world rebuilds. And under it, there's a door.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.026
cast.text: I asked a woodcutter what was behind the door under the oldest tree. He said, another forest. And in that forest, another tree. And under it, another door.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.027
cast.text: The world's mercy is like a second helping of pudding. You don't expect it. You don't deserve it, maybe. But oh, it's lovely.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.028
cast.text: They say the countdown voice is the voice of the storyteller who tells the world. Five, four, three, two, one. Once upon a time, again.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.029
cast.text: I've noticed every world has one fire burning in it somewhere. Always one. Like a candle left in a window, so somebody can find the way home.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.030
cast.text: The smoke from my fire always drifts the same way. Toward the middle of the world. I've followed it. It goes up, and up, and then it simply stops.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.031
cast.text: There was a walker once who sat by this fire for a whole world, just listening. When the countdown came, she smiled and said, now I understand. Then she was gone. I've been telling stories ever since, hoping one of them is the right one.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.032
cast.text: My stories never end, you know. They just stop for a bit. Same as the world.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.033
cast.text: In the old days, they say, there were no safe places. Then someone lit the first fire, and the world made a safe place around it, so the fire wouldn't go out.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.034
cast.text: I heard a story about a land beyond the labyrinths where it's always morning. Wren says she's flown there. I've never been sure if she's teasing.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.035
cast.text: The logs in my pile are never the same wood twice. Oak, pine, birch, and once, a wood I'd never seen, that smelled like rain.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.036
cast.text: Every story has a beginning, a middle and an end. The world only has the first two. It keeps forgetting the third.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.037
cast.text: I sometimes think the world rebuilds because somebody's telling it wrong. Not badly, mind you. Just not quite the way it really went.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.038
cast.text: There's a story the children used to tell. The world is a snow globe, and every so often someone picks it up and gives it a good shake. I liked that one.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.039
cast.text: Cinder, by the lava, says the world is forged in fire. Well, I've sat by a fire a long time, and it's never forged me anything but warm toes.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.040
cast.text: If you could catch a spark from the countdown, they say, you'd see the next world in it, tiny and glowing. I've tried. My hands aren't quick enough anymore.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.041
cast.text: The fire knows when a walker's near. It crackles a little brighter. I think it likes you.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.042
cast.text: There's an old saying round the campfires. The world turns over for those who listen. I've never been quite sure what it means.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.043
cast.text: One night the fire burned blue for an entire world. Nobody knew why. The next world, everyone had a different theory. The fire never said.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.044
cast.text: Some say the enemies out there were once walkers, who stopped listening and started throwing things. It's only a story. I hope.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.045
cast.text: Every story by every fire, in every world, starts the same way. Once, long ago. Have you ever wondered when long ago actually was?

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.046
cast.text: I once tried to tell a story with no ending, to see if the world would wait. It didn't. It rebuilt right in the middle. I finished the story in the next world, for a different listener.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.047
cast.text: The marshmallows taste a little different every world. Toasty one world, smoky the next. I take it as a sign the world is still deciding.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.048
cast.text: Here's something I've never told anyone. Every world, there's a set of footprints in the ash that go into the fire, and never come out. Small ones. Gentle ones. The Builder, warming their hands before the next world, I think. Even builders get cold.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.049
cast.text: They say the world is a great big campfire story, and we're all the characters. If that's true, I hope the storyteller likes us.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.050
cast.text: The fire's smoke spells out shapes sometimes. A door, a key, a question mark. Last world, it spelled out a word. Soon.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.051
cast.text: Sit by any fire in any world, and you'll hear the same thing if you're quiet enough. A tiny voice, deep in the flames, counting.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.052
cast.text: The best stories don't answer the question, young one. They make you ask a better one. That's what the world's doing, I think.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.053
cast.text: Let me throw another log on. There. Lovely. Nothing like the sound of a fresh log catching.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.054
cast.text: I knit when I'm not telling stories. Scarves, mostly. I've made a scarf for every safe place in the world.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.055
cast.text: Hot cocoa? Careful, it's hot. Ho ho! Of course it's hot. It's hot cocoa.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.056
cast.text: Here's a story. Once there was a walker who asked every safe place the same question. And every answer was different. And all of them were true.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.057
cast.text: The fire tells me things, if I listen long enough. Last night it told me the world is still learning to be a world. Ho ho! Aren't we all?

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.058
cast.text: There's a story about a lantern that was lit in the first world and never went out. It's still burning, somewhere. In every world. Waiting to be found.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.059
cast.text: In one story I know, the world rebuilds because it's dancing. And every rebuild is just a new step. One, two, three, four, five, turn.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.060
cast.text: In another story, there's a great tree at the heart of the world, and every world is one of its leaves. The rebuild is the wind turning the leaves.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.061
cast.text: The best story I know has no ending. I start it every world. And every world, the world rebuilds before I get to the end. Ho ho!

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.062
cast.text: The fire burns a little lower when a sad story is told. And a little higher for a happy one. It's very sensitive, my fire.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.063
cast.text: The world's mercy comes like a new log on the fire. Sudden warmth, a crackle, a glow. And a little more time to finish the story.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.064
cast.text: Once, a child asked me, Grandpa Hollis, will the world ever stop changing? I said, not while there are stories left to tell. And there always are.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.065
cast.text: There's a story the old fire keepers tell. Every flame in every world is lit from one first flame. Somewhere, that flame is still burning, very small and very bright.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.066
cast.text: The chimney whistles a tune when the wind blows. Five notes. Rising, then falling. Everyone in the world seems to know that tune.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.067
cast.text: I've heard a hundred theories by this fire. Spells, clocks, dreams, machines. My favorite is the simplest. The world just loves to start fresh.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.068
cast.text: Mother Hazel and I once tried to tell the same story together. She told it one way, I told it another. By the end, we'd made a whole new world.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.069
cast.text: There's an old rocking chair by my fireplace that rocks on its own, just before the countdown. Gently. Like someone's settling in for a story.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.070
cast.text: The stories I tell come back to me, changed, from other people. A walker once told me my own story, and it had a better ending. I've used it ever since.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.071
cast.text: Some say the safe places are the world's campfires. Places to rest, to warm up, to hear a story before the long walk. I think that's just right.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.072
cast.text: Every fire has a heart. The very middle, where it's hottest and brightest. I think the world has a heart too. And it's still glowing.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.073
cast.text: I tell stories so the world won't forget them. When the world rebuilds, I like to think the stories go with it. Tucked away. Safe.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.074
cast.text: When I was young, I asked my grandmother why the world keeps changing. She said, so you'll always have something new to tell. She was right.

cast.name: vc_storyteller.story.075
cast.text: The fire makes the same sound, every world, at the very end. A soft pop. Like a full stop. Then a new story begins.

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Follow the bangs!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.002
cast.text: Hey! This way, and keep clear of the hot stuff!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.003
cast.text: Over here, walker! I'm by the rockets!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.004
cast.text: Hey you! Yeah, you! Over here!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.005
cast.text: This way! Mind the lava, it's grumpy today!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Something's about to go off, and it's your gift!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.007
cast.text: Follow the whistle and the pop! I'm right here!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.008
cast.text: Hey! Come over! I won't light anything while you walk!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.009
cast.text: Over here, by the glow!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.010
cast.text: This way, walker! Watch your step!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've got something with your name on it!

cast.name: vc_cinder.greet.012
cast.text: Hey! Come and see! Well, hear!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! Your gift's still here!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Don't make me launch it at you!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.003
cast.text: Walker! Back this way!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.004
cast.text: Come back! Follow the pops!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.005
cast.text: Hey! You forgot something! This way!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.006
cast.text: Over here! It's not going anywhere, and neither am I!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.007
cast.text: Back this way, walker! Mind the lava!

cast.name: vc_cinder.call.008
cast.text: Come on back! I've kept it cool for you!

cast.name: vc_cinder.gift.001
cast.text: Here. Caught it before it went off.

cast.name: vc_cinder.gift.002
cast.text: Take it. Careful, it's still warm.

cast.name: vc_cinder.gift.003
cast.text: For you, walker. Forged it myself.

cast.name: vc_cinder.gift.004
cast.text: Here you go. Light up the next world with it.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.001
cast.text: Name's Cinder. I make fireworks. Big ones. Loud ones. The best ones.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.002
cast.text: Keep back from the edge. The lava doesn't bite, but it does burn.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.003
cast.text: Every rocket I make, I name. That one's Thunder. That one's Gerald. Don't ask.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.004
cast.text: I get my fire straight from the lava. Saves on matches.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.005
cast.text: Love that smell. Smoke and sulfur. Smells like progress.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.006
cast.text: My eyebrows grew back eleven times. That's a personal record.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.007
cast.text: Fireworks aren't about the bang. Well, mostly they're about the bang. But the fizz matters too.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.008
cast.text: You've got good ears, walker. In my line of work, you need them. And spare eyebrows.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.009
cast.text: I don't do quiet. Quiet makes me nervous.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.010
cast.text: The lava keeps me warm, the rockets keep me busy, and the walkers keep me company.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.011
cast.text: The world gets forged, walker. That's what I reckon. Melted down and poured fresh into a new shape, every few minutes.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Reforging. Everything goes in the fire, everything comes out new. That's how it works with metal. Why not worlds?

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.013
cast.text: The lava rises a little just before the countdown. Every time. Like something down there is breathing in.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.014
cast.text: I lit a firework right as the world rebuilt, once. It went up in one world and came down in the next. Exploded in a color I'd never seen before.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.015
cast.text: Deep under the lava, there's something glowing that isn't lava. I've seen the light. Steady, like a lamp. Somebody's down there working.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.016
cast.text: They say the Builder keeps a forge at the bottom of the world. Every world, they hammer out a new one. The sparks are what we call stars.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.017
cast.text: Hazel says spell, Rosalind says recipe, Pendle says clock. They're all wrong. It's a forge. I can hear the hammer.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.018
cast.text: Every world, I find new powder in my shed. Different colors, different bangs. I never ordered it. Someone wants me to keep making fireworks. Maybe the world needs the noise. Maybe fireworks keep something away, or wake something up.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.019
cast.text: The biggest firework I ever made, I called the Question. It went up, burst into a great big shape, and the whole world went quiet. Then it rebuilt.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.020
cast.text: Fireworks always fizz before they pop. Five fizzes. Just like the countdown. I didn't plan that. I don't think I did, anyway.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.021
cast.text: The lava here never cools. Not once in all the worlds. Something underneath must be keeping the fire going. Something that never sleeps.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.022
cast.text: I heard the enemies out there are made in the same forge as the world. Leftover sparks, still looking for a shape.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.023
cast.text: Sometimes, the lava bubbles in a rhythm. Pop, pause, pop pop. Like someone knocking. Who knocks from inside a volcano?

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.024
cast.text: The sky here is always lit up. Not by my fireworks, mostly. There's a glow over the whole world, just before the rebuild. Like a kiln about to open.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.025
cast.text: Old Hollis says the world is a story. Stories don't need fire. Worlds do. That's how I know he's wrong. Lovely fellow, though.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.026
cast.text: There's a rock by the lava I can't melt. I've tried every fire I've got. It just sits there, cool to the touch. Older than the world, I reckon.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.027
cast.text: Every world, the world's mercy smells a bit like a firework that didn't go off. Sweet. Smoky. Like something saved for later.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.028
cast.text: I made a rocket that would go all the way up. Past the sky. To see what's above the world. It never came down. I'm still listening for it.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.029
