cast.text: The ground shakes just before a rebuild. Just a little. Rattles my rockets. I always keep them tied down now.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.030
cast.text: Some say the world rebuilds because it's not hot enough yet. Like a pot that hasn't boiled. One day, it'll reach the right heat, and then, who knows.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.031
cast.text: Some reckon the world rebuilds because it got too hot. Overheated, and has to be cooled and started again. Nobody agrees about anything here.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.032
cast.text: Walkers come through with their ammo and their potions. Ever wonder where the ammo comes from? I have. It's not my powder. I'd know.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.033
cast.text: I found a mold in the lava once, cooled into stone. The shape of a door. Just a door, on its own. I keep it by the shed.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.034
cast.text: The countdown voice sounds a bit like my old teacher. The firework master. He vanished three worlds before I took over. Left me his matches.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.035
cast.text: They say if you light every firework in the world at once, you'll see the whole map for a moment. I've never had enough fireworks. Yet.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.036
cast.text: Lava keeps the world warm, they say. Hot and slow and always moving. Well, if the world is warm, it's got a heart somewhere. Where's the heart?

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.037
cast.text: I once heard the lava singing. Low and rumbly. Same tune the ghosts hum, Jangles reckons. Everybody's got the same song stuck in their head.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.038
cast.text: Firework smoke always drifts toward the middle of the world. Every time. I've stopped being surprised.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.039
cast.text: I asked the volcano why the world keeps changing. It rumbled. I took that as, mind your own business.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.040
cast.text: The ash from the volcano falls in shapes sometimes. Circles, mostly. Circles inside circles. Like the plan of a labyrinth.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.041
cast.text: If I could build a firework big enough, I'd write a question in the sky. Why? Just that. And I'd wait to see who answers.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.042
cast.text: Mister Sprocket says the world is a machine. Well, every machine needs a fire to run. So the fire's more important, really.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.043
cast.text: There's a rumor the first world was made of light. Just light, nothing else. Then somebody got clumsy, dropped it in the forge, and here we are.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.044
cast.text: Every rocket I launch, the world catches. I hear them land in the distance, gentle as rain. Not one crater. Something's catching them.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.045
cast.text: I've been burned by fire, lava and steam, and none of it hurt half as much as not knowing what's going on in this world.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.046
cast.text: My fuses always burn exactly as long as I cut them. Except right before a rebuild. Then they burn a little faster. The world's in a hurry.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.047
cast.text: I think the world is proud of itself. Every rebuild, it shows off something new. A bigger lava lake. A taller tower. Like it's saying, look what I can do.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.048
cast.text: The volcano erupts once every world, very softly. Just a puff. A little sigh. I don't think the world is angry. I think it's tired.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.049
cast.text: There's a walker who left me a firework once. Not one of mine. Strange make. Strange powder. I've never lit it. I'm saving it for the right world.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.050
cast.text: When fireworks burst, you get the bang first, then the light comes slowly down. Maybe the rebuild is the bang. Maybe we're the light, coming down.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.051
cast.text: Some say there's a fire that burns between the worlds, and the world gets rebuilt in its glow. I've never seen it. But I've felt it on my back.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.052
cast.text: Underneath the sound of my rockets, you can hear the world ticking. Pendle swears it's a clock. I swear it's a hammer. We're both stubborn.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.053
cast.text: I made a firework once that didn't go bang. It went shush. The whole world went quiet with it. I've never been able to make another one.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.054
cast.text: The best fireworks leave a little bit of themselves in the sky. A glow that hangs there. I think the old worlds do the same. Leave a little glow behind.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.055
cast.text: I once threw a rock into the lava, and it came back out the other side, cold, with writing on it. The writing said, not yet. Same as everyone keeps hearing.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.056
cast.text: Rule one of fireworks. Light the fuse, step back. Rule two. Step back further.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.057
cast.text: I keep a bucket of water by every rocket. Learned that the hard way. Several times.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.058
cast.text: The lava glows brighter when a walker is near. I don't think it's dangerous. I think it's curious. Same as everything else here.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.059
cast.text: I found a firework in the lava once. Unburnt. Perfect. Like it was waiting to be found. It had a fuse as long as my arm.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.060
cast.text: The volcano rumbles five times before every countdown. Low and slow. Like a cat purring, if the cat was a mountain.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.061
cast.text: Every rebuild, my workshop gets a little hotter. Not enough to worry. Just enough to notice. Something's turning up the heat.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.062
cast.text: There's a crack in the rock near the lava where you can hear something singing. High and sweet. Not lava. Something else.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.063
cast.text: Some say the stars are holes in the roof of the world, and the light comes from a great fire on the other side. I'd love to see that fire.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.064
cast.text: Fireworks are like questions, walker. They go up fast, burst into something beautiful, and leave you wondering what you just saw.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.065
cast.text: The best firework I ever made, I didn't light. I'm saving it for the day someone finds the answer. Then I'll light it, and the whole world will know.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.066
cast.text: The sparks from the lava drift up and form shapes in the air. Circles, mostly. Sometimes a door. Once, a face, smiling.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.067
cast.text: The lava flows toward the middle of the world. Slow, steady, every world. Something in the middle is very hungry for heat.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.068
cast.text: I asked Hollis if he knows where fire comes from. He said, from a story. I said, which story? He said, all of them. Not helpful.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.069
cast.text: There's a stone in the lava field that's always cool to touch. And humming. I sit on it when I'm thinking. It helps.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.070
cast.text: My teacher used to say a good firework is like a good world. Built carefully, lit once, and gone in a flash. Then you build the next one.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.071
cast.text: The world's mercy, from the lava field, looks like a rain of soft golden sparks. Warm, not hot. Kind. Then it's gone.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.072
cast.text: I've been building a rocket strong enough to reach the next world before it arrives. I'd see it first. Maybe even see who's building it.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.073
cast.text: Every rebuild, a new crack opens in the rock, and a new lava stream starts. Like the world's finding new ways to keep warm.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.074
cast.text: I heard the enemies are scared of fireworks. Maybe that's why I've got so much powder. Somebody wants the safe places to stay safe.

cast.name: vc_cinder.story.075
cast.text: Fire changes everything it touches. Wood to ash, sand to glass. Maybe the rebuild is just the world touching fire.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, please. By the great pipes.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.002
cast.text: Hello. Follow the music, and you'll find me.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.003
cast.text: This way, walker. Softly now.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.004
cast.text: Over here, by the organ bench.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.005
cast.text: Ah, a listener. Come closer, please.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.006
cast.text: Hello there. This way, past the choir stalls.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.007
cast.text: Over here. Just follow the low notes.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.008
cast.text: Come along. The music will guide you.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.009
cast.text: Good evening. I'm by the organ.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.010
cast.text: This way, walker. Mind the echo.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.011
cast.text: Over here, please. I have something for you.

cast.name: vc_organist.greet.012
cast.text: Hello. Come and sit a while, and listen.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.001
cast.text: Walker, please come back. Your gift is still here.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. Follow the music.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.003
cast.text: Back this way, by the great pipes.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.004
cast.text: Come back, please. I've kept it safe for you.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.005
cast.text: This way. The low notes will lead you.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.006
cast.text: Over here, walker. You left before the final chord.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.007
cast.text: Please come back. It's still waiting on the organ bench.

cast.name: vc_organist.call.008
cast.text: This way again. Softly, softly.

cast.name: vc_organist.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. With my compliments.

cast.name: vc_organist.gift.002
cast.text: Please take this. It was meant for you.

cast.name: vc_organist.gift.003
cast.text: A small gift, from the organ loft.

cast.name: vc_organist.gift.004
cast.text: For you, walker. Go well.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.001
cast.text: I'm Ambrose. I play the organ here. I've played it for a very long time.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.002
cast.text: Forgive the volume. The organ only knows one way to speak, and that's grandly.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.003
cast.text: The choir rehearses every evening. They're very dedicated. I've never seen them leave.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.004
cast.text: Every pipe in this organ has a name. I named them all. It took several worlds.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.005
cast.text: I find great peace in the echo here. Every note comes back to you, a little softer, a little wiser.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.006
cast.text: Do sit down. The pews are hard, but the music is soft.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.007
cast.text: I practise scales every day. Up and down, up and down. Rather like the world, really.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.008
cast.text: The candles here never burn down. I've stopped buying new ones.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.009
cast.text: Music is the only thing I truly understand. Everything else, I'm still listening to.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.010
cast.text: The dark choir sounds frightening at first. It's only that they sing very low. They're perfectly lovely people.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.011
cast.text: The world is a piece of music, walker. A great, long piece. And every few minutes, it returns to the opening bars.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.012
cast.text: There is one pipe in this organ I've never been able to play. The longest one. When I press its key, nothing sounds. But the whole world trembles. I believe that pipe plays the note that starts each world.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.013
cast.text: The choir sings the same hymn before every rebuild. It has no words, only a melody. Every world, the melody is a little longer.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.014
cast.text: I once played a chord just as the world rebuilt. The chord carried on into the next world. I took my hands off the keys, and still it played.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.015
cast.text: The great organ sometimes plays itself between worlds. I have heard it from the next world, faintly, like a memory.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.016
cast.text: Hazel thinks the world is a spell. Jangles thinks it's a song. I think we're both nearly right, which is to say, both quite wrong.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.017
cast.text: The rebuild sounds, to my ear, like a great chord resolving. Tension, then release. Then, oddly, more tension.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.018
cast.text: I have a theory. The world is waiting to hear one perfect chord. When it hears it, it will stop rebuilding. I've been trying for a very long time.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.019
cast.text: There's sheet music in the organ loft in a hand I don't recognise. It's labelled, for the last world. The pages are blank.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.020
cast.text: The countdown voice is perfectly in tune, did you know? Every number lands on the same note. Somebody musical is counting.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.021
cast.text: Some evenings the dark choir sings a name. Very softly. I can never quite catch it. They say they don't know whose it is either.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.022
cast.text: The echo in this cathedral is longer than it should be. Much longer. As if the sound is travelling somewhere far before it comes back.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.023
cast.text: I believe each safe place has its own note. The kitchen hums in one key, the river in another. Put them all together, and you'd hear the world's chord.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.024
cast.text: The organ bellows breathe in and out, like lungs. Just before a rebuild, they breathe in, and hold. Five beats. Then everything changes.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.025
cast.text: The world's mercy, to me, sounds like a single sustained note, played very gently. As if somebody leaned on a key by accident. A kind accident.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.026
cast.text: There is a hymn book here with one hymn missing. The page has been torn out cleanly. I've looked in every world for that page.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.027
cast.text: The choir master told me, long ago, that the first world was a single note, held by a single voice. And then the voice ran out of breath.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.028
cast.text: I've noticed the cathedral is a little larger every world. A new pew, a new pillar. Someone is building it slowly, between the rebuilds.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.029
cast.text: Prudence in the library says the world is a book. Music and books are close cousins. Both are read from the start. Both can be played again.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.030
cast.text: The bells in the tower ring once before each rebuild. I don't ring them. The ropes hang perfectly still. And yet, they ring.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.031
cast.text: I believe the enemies out there are out of tune. Just slightly. They throw things because they can't sing.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.032
cast.text: The dark choir hums lowest when walkers are near. I asked them why. They said, so the walker can hear the floor of the world.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.033
cast.text: There is a pedal on this organ, the lowest of all, that I never press. My teacher told me never to. I've wondered why for a hundred worlds.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.034
cast.text: Some say the cathedral was here before the labyrinths. That the labyrinths were built to keep its music in. Or to keep something else out.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.035
cast.text: I tried once to play the countdown on the organ. Five notes, falling. When I played the fifth, the world rebuilt. I haven't played it since.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.036
cast.text: The world is a round, I think. You know, a song sung over and over, each voice starting a little behind the last. We're all singing it.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.037
cast.text: The stained glass windows hum when the sun is low. There's no sun here, of course. And yet, every world, they hum.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.038
cast.text: I asked the oldest singer in the choir what the hymn is about. She said, it's about coming home. Whose home, I asked. She smiled and sang on.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.039
cast.text: Every rebuild, the organ goes slightly out of tune. Every world, I tune it again. Perhaps the world is doing the same thing, with itself.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.040
cast.text: Music fills a room and then fades. The world fills with life and then rebuilds. I find a great comfort in that. The room is never truly empty.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.041
cast.text: The ghost choir in the graveyard and the dark choir here sing the same hymn, a few bars apart. Neither choir has met the other.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.042
cast.text: There is a rumour that a song is hidden in the shape of every world, if you walk it from end to end. I believe it. I just don't have the legs for it.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.043
cast.text: I once heard a voice join the choir that wasn't one of ours. Clear and bright. It sang one line, then fell silent. The choir still talks of it.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.044
cast.text: I believe the Builder is a composer. Writes a world, listens to it, isn't satisfied, and begins a new draft. Every great composer does the same. But then, who is the audience? Who is the Builder writing it for?

cast.name: vc_organist.story.045
cast.text: The organ's lowest notes travel through the floor. Put your hand on the stone, and you'll feel them. And underneath them, faintly, another organ, playing back.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.046
cast.text: Every world, I play the same piece at the same moment. Every world, the cathedral answers with a slightly different echo. The world is never the same listener twice.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.047
cast.text: There's a little door behind the organ pipes. It's too small for me. Sometimes, from behind it, I hear someone tuning.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.048
cast.text: The rebuild never interrupts the music. Have you noticed? It always waits for the end of a phrase. Somebody very polite is in charge.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.049
cast.text: The choir believes they are singing the world into being. That if they stopped, it would all fall silent. I've never asked them to stop.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.050
cast.text: I have played for walkers, for ghosts, and once, I believe, for the Builder. A figure sat in the back pew for one whole world. When it ended, the pew was empty, and warm.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.051
cast.text: A note played in this cathedral takes eleven seconds to fade. Except just before a rebuild. Then it takes five.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.052
cast.text: The world is unfinished music, walker. And unfinished music is the most beautiful kind. You can always imagine the next note.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.053
cast.text: The organ bench is rather hard. I've sat on it so long, I've stopped noticing.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.054
cast.text: I play quietly in the mornings. Well, as quietly as an organ can. Which is still rather loud.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.055
cast.text: If you'd like to hear a particular piece, just hum it. I'll pick it up. I usually do.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.056
cast.text: The organ has five keyboards. Four of them I play. The fifth plays itself, very softly, during the countdown.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.057
cast.text: The choir's robes are never worn out, never new. Exactly the same, every world. As if they're made of the same quiet thread.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.058
cast.text: I believe the cathedral is the world's ear. It's shaped to listen. Every sound in the world eventually reaches here, and echoes.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.059
cast.text: The organ's pipes are cleaned between worlds. Spotless, every time. I've never seen who does it. But I hear them humming as they work.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.060
cast.text: There's a hymn the choir sings only once per world. The last line is always different. Last world it was, and so we wait. This world, and so we wake.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.061
cast.text: The world's mercy, in the cathedral, is heard as a single bell, ringing gently. Not the tower bells. A smaller one. Somewhere above the ceiling.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.062
cast.text: The dark choir sings in the lowest voices in the world. Lower than any bell. So low, I believe, that the world itself is listening to them.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.063
cast.text: I once played a scale that went down and down, below the lowest note. The organ kept playing. Lower and lower. Then the floor began to hum. I stopped.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.064
cast.text: I've a feeling the countdown is not the end of a piece, walker. It's the turning of the page. The music carries on, on the next page.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.065
cast.text: Prudence once found a hymn book in the library written in music only. No words. When I played it, the choir began to sing words none of us knew.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.066
cast.text: There's a stone in the cathedral floor marked with a single musical note. If you stand on it, you can hear the whole building humming that note.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.067
cast.text: I believe the enemies outside would be calmer if they could hear the organ. Music soothes. I'd play for them, if they'd only come in.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.068
cast.text: The echoes in the cathedral sometimes come back changed. You play one note, and a different one returns. As if the walls are correcting you.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.069
cast.text: Some say the cathedral was built around a sound, not a place. A single sound, held so long it became stone. I find that rather beautiful.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.070
cast.text: The choir stalls have names carved in them. Every world, there's one more. The newest name is always a walker's. Perhaps yours, one day.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.071
cast.text: Every organist before me kept a list of the world's tunes. My list is the longest. And every tune on it ends the same way. Unresolved.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.072
cast.text: The organ's lowest pedal note is not a sound. It's a feeling. You feel it in your chest. Just before the rebuild, it plays itself, very softly.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.073
cast.text: Jangles came to play his fiddle in the cathedral once. Fiddle and organ together. The choir wept. Then the world rebuilt. We never finished the piece.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.074
cast.text: I believe there's a final piece of music, somewhere, for when the world finally rests. I hope I'm the one who gets to play it.

cast.name: vc_organist.story.075
cast.text: Every world, I play the first note just after the rebuild. I like to think it helps the new world find its voice.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, please. Quietly, if you can.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.002
cast.text: Hello. This way, past the tall shelves.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.003
cast.text: Psst. Over here, by the reading desk.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.004
cast.text: Ah, a visitor. This way, please.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.005
cast.text: Over here. Mind the book cart.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.006
cast.text: Hello, walker. Follow my voice, softly.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.007
cast.text: This way, please. I've marked your place.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.008
cast.text: Over here. I've something set aside for you.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.009
cast.text: Good evening. By the window, if you please.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.010
cast.text: This way. The quiet will lead you.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.011
cast.text: Hello. Come in, and do keep your voice down.

cast.name: vc_librarian.greet.012
cast.text: Over here, please. I've been expecting you. It's in the records.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.001
cast.text: Walker, please come back. You haven't collected your gift.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. It's at the reading desk.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.003
cast.text: This way, please. Quietly.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.004
cast.text: You've left something behind. Back this way.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.005
cast.text: Please come back. I've kept it on the shelf for you.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.006
cast.text: Over here, walker. It's overdue, but it's yours.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.007
cast.text: This way again, past the tall shelves.

cast.name: vc_librarian.call.008
cast.text: Come back, please. A gift should never go unclaimed.

cast.name: vc_librarian.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. Please handle it with care.

cast.name: vc_librarian.gift.002
cast.text: For you. No need to return it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.gift.003
cast.text: Take this, with the library's compliments.

cast.name: vc_librarian.gift.004
cast.text: Here. Consider it on permanent loan.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.001
cast.text: I'm Prudence Quill. I keep the books, and the records, and the silence.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.002
cast.text: Shh. Thank you. Now, how can I help?

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.003
cast.text: Every book in this library is in order. Every world. I make sure of it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.004
cast.text: I read by candlelight. I've never needed to see the pages. The words come to me.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.005
cast.text: Please don't fold the corners of the pages. The books remember.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.006
cast.text: I've catalogued every book here. Twice. Some of them rearranged themselves, so I did it again.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.007
cast.text: The cathedral next door is very grand. I prefer it here. Grandness is noisy.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.008
cast.text: A library is a safe place. That's not just my opinion. It's true in every world.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.009
cast.text: If you're looking for a book on why the world keeps changing, it's on the top shelf. All of them. The whole top shelf.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.010
cast.text: I do love a good mystery. Which is just as well, given where we live.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.011
cast.text: The world is a book, walker. Every rebuild, someone turns the page. And every page is a new world.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.012
cast.text: I keep a record of every world I've seen. The record is very long, and every entry ends in the middle of a sentence.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.013
cast.text: There's a book here whose pages rewrite themselves after every rebuild. I've read it a thousand times. It never says the same thing.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.014
cast.text: This library holds a book about the first world. I've found it once. It was very short. Only one line. I've never found it again.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.015
cast.text: I'm sure the world rebuilds for a reason. Everything happens for a reason, in a well written story. I just haven't reached that chapter.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.016
cast.text: Every world, there's one new book on the shelves that I didn't put there. Always the same author. No name, just a little drawing of a door.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.017
cast.text: The books in the top shelf whisper before a rebuild. Pages rustling, all at once. Like a great breath.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.018
cast.text: The cathedral's records go back further than the world itself. There are entries for worlds before the first one. I can't explain that.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.019
cast.text: Ambrose believes the world is music. Music is lovely, of course, but you can't look things up in it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.020
cast.text: There's a card catalogue drawer marked, answers. I've opened it a hundred times. It's always empty. But someone keeps relabelling it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.021
cast.text: I found a book that was all footnotes. No story, just footnotes. Each one explained a different reason why the world rebuilds. None agreed.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.022
cast.text: Some say each safe place is a chapter heading. The labyrinths in between are the text. And you, walker, are the reader.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.023
cast.text: I once tried to read the last page of the book of worlds. It was blank. Not torn out, just blank. Waiting to be written.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.024
cast.text: The world rebuilds when the story stalls, they say. When nothing new can happen, it starts over. So perhaps it's waiting for something new.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.025
cast.text: Every world, the library has one more shelf. I can never find where it was added. It's simply there, full of books.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.026
cast.text: There's a reading room here that is always locked. I have the key. The key doesn't fit. Every world, I try anyway.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.027
cast.text: The records say the first walker kept a diary. One page has been found, in a dozen worlds. It always says the same thing. Still listening.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.028
cast.text: I have a theory. The world isn't being rebuilt. It's being read again. Each time, by a slightly different reader. You, perhaps.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.029
cast.text: The candles in the cathedral flicker in the pattern of a sentence, I'm convinced. I've been taking it down for many worlds. So far, it reads, and then.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.030
cast.text: Mister Pendle wanted to borrow the book on time. I lent it. Next world, it was back on the shelf, unread, with a train ticket inside.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.031
cast.text: The enemies out there are like misprints, I think. Errors in the text. The world keeps trying to correct them.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.032
cast.text: There's a map in the cathedral archive that shows every world at once, layered on top of each other. It's mostly ink. Very dark, very old ink.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.033
cast.text: I'm told there's a library in every world, and it's always mine. But the books in it change. As though the world can't decide what I should read.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.034
cast.text: The world's mercy is like finding an extra page in a book you thought you'd finished. A little more story. Unexpected, and very welcome.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.035
cast.text: In the oldest book in the cathedral, there's a word that appears on every page. I can read every word in the book except that one.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.036
cast.text: Some scholars believe the countdown is a reader closing the book. Five, four, three, two, one, and the cover shuts. Then it opens again. A different book.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.037
cast.text: I file every rumour I hear under R. The R drawer won't close any more.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.038
cast.text: The books here are bound in a leather that's warm to the touch. Every world, they're a little warmer. As if they're being read somewhere else, at the same time.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.039
cast.text: There's a rule in this library. Never read the book on the bottom shelf, in the corner. I wrote that rule. I don't remember writing it, or why.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.040
cast.text: I've noticed something in the records. The worlds are getting longer. Only by a moment or two. But longer. As if the world is learning to be patient.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.041
cast.text: The cathedral has a register of everyone who has ever walked in. Your name is in it, many times. Some of the entries are dated in the future.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.042
cast.text: A walker once asked me for a book on how it all ends. I looked for a whole world. When the countdown came, I found it. It was a book on how it all begins.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.043
cast.text: They say the Builder wrote a guide to the world, and left it here. It's the one book I've never found. Perhaps they're still writing it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.044
cast.text: The ink in my pen runs dry precisely at each countdown. Every world, it's full again. Someone thinks my notes are important.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.045
cast.text: Every library has a quiet. Mine has two. One is ordinary. The other is the quiet between worlds, which seeps in through the walls, very slightly.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.046
cast.text: I keep a book of contradictions. Hazel says this, Mortimer says that. It's my thickest volume. Every rumour has its opposite, filed beside it.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.047
cast.text: Prudence is a family name. The librarians before me were all called Prudence. I've seen the records. There have been a great many of us.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.048
cast.text: Some believe the world rebuilds because it was written in pencil. Easy to rub out, easy to write again.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.049
cast.text: The pages of the book of worlds are not numbered. I tried to number them once. When I came back, the numbers were all five.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.050
cast.text: I've found letters tucked inside books, written to no one, signed by no one. They all ask the same question. Have you found it yet?

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.051
cast.text: The cathedral archive has a room with nothing in it but a reading stand and a single book, closed. No one is allowed to open it. No one remembers who said so. I opened it once, just a crack. The book was reading me, very politely. I closed it again.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.052
cast.text: There's an index at the back of the oldest book. Under W, for world, it says, see also, again. Under A, for again, it says, see also, world.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.053
cast.text: I believe every story told in every safe place is true, in its own world. The trouble is, we only ever get to live in one of them at a time.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.054
cast.text: When the world rebuilds, I always lose my place in whatever I'm reading. I've started using a bookmark. The bookmark always stays. The book changes.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.055
cast.text: In the cathedral, there's an inscription above the door, too worn to read. I've traced it with my fingers a thousand times. I think the first word is welcome.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.056
cast.text: I've noticed that walkers who ask more questions get more gifts. That may be a coincidence. It may also be in a book somewhere. I'll look it up.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.057
cast.text: Do mind the step by the reference section. It's been there since the first world. Still catches people out.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.058
cast.text: I recommend the poetry shelf. The poems rearrange themselves. You'll never read the same one twice.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.059
cast.text: The library clock stopped in the first world and has never restarted. Pendle has offered to fix it. I've declined. It's the only still thing I have.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.060
cast.text: There's a book here called, the reasons. It's very thick. Every reason in it is crossed out except the last one. The last page is missing.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.061
cast.text: The library ladder rolls by itself sometimes, along the shelves. It always stops at the same book. A book with no title, only a little drawing of an ear.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.062
cast.text: I believe the world's mercy is written in the margins of the book of worlds. A little note. Be kind to this one. Give them more time.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.063
cast.text: The pages of old books rustle just before the countdown. All at once, like a flock of birds taking off. Then silence. Then a new library.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.064
cast.text: Some readers think the world is the Builder's diary. Every world is a new entry. I'd love to read the first one. And the last.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.065
cast.text: There's a reading lamp in the corner that's always lit. Nobody turns it on. Every world, there's an open book beneath it. Always on a different page.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.066
cast.text: I catalogue rumours the way other people collect stamps. My favourite? That the world is a story being told to someone who keeps falling asleep.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.067
cast.text: The cathedral's oldest record is a list of names. Every walker who ever came. The last line is blank, except for one word. Next.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.068
cast.text: I've noticed every book in the library has the same last word, no matter the story. Again. Every single one.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.069
cast.text: The silence in the cathedral and the silence in the library are different silences. One is waiting. The other is listening. I've never decided which is which.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.070
cast.text: I found a library card in a book, with a borrowing date of the first world. The book was never returned. It was a book about how to stop the world.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.071
cast.text: Mother Hazel borrowed a book once and returned it with a note. The note said, chapter seven is wrong. There is no chapter seven.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.072
cast.text: The words in the cathedral's stained glass rearrange themselves every world. Last world they said, all things change. This world, all things remain.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.073
cast.text: Every librarian before me left one line in the record book. The first one wrote, it began. The latest wrote, still going. I haven't written mine yet.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.074
cast.text: I believe the world is not a single book, but a library. Every world is a different book. And you, walker, have been reading them all.

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.075
cast.text: The cathedral has a whispering gallery. Whisper on one side, and you're heard on the other. Once, I whispered, why? From the other side came, why not?

cast.name: vc_librarian.story.076
cast.text: The most important thing in any library, my dear, is not the books. It's the questions people bring to them. Bring yours. They're always welcome here.

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.001
cast.text: Ahoy there! Over here, sailor!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.002
cast.text: This way, matey! Follow the creaking!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.003
cast.text: Ahoy! Come aboard, walker!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.004
cast.text: Over here! Mind the ropes on deck!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.005
cast.text: Ahoy, ahoy! This way!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.006
cast.text: Come on over, sailor! Steady as she goes!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.007
cast.text: Over here, by the wheel!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.008
cast.text: Ahoy, walker! Follow my voice through the waves!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.009
cast.text: This way! The captain's waiting!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.010
cast.text: Ahoy! Over here! I've got something from the deep!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.011
cast.text: Come aboard, come aboard! This way!

cast.name: vc_captain.greet.012
cast.text: Over here, sailor! Mind your footing!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.001
cast.text: Ahoy! Come back, sailor! You left your gift on deck!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.002
cast.text: Over here again, matey!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.003
cast.text: Back this way! The ship's not sailing without you!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.004
cast.text: Ahoy! I'm still here, and so's your treasure!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.005
cast.text: Come back aboard, walker!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.006
cast.text: This way, follow the creaking!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.007
cast.text: Over here, sailor! Don't leave the captain hanging!

cast.name: vc_captain.call.008
cast.text: Ahoy! Back this way, steady now!

cast.name: vc_captain.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are, sailor. Straight from the deep.

cast.name: vc_captain.gift.002
cast.text: Take it, matey. Every sailor needs supplies.

cast.name: vc_captain.gift.003
cast.text: A gift from the captain. Fair winds to you.

cast.name: vc_captain.gift.004
cast.text: For you, walker. Found it in a sunken chest.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.001
cast.text: I'm Captain Brine. Been sailing these waters longer than the world's been changing.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.002
cast.text: Hear that creak? That's my old ship. She talks more than I do.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.003
cast.text: The sea's calm tonight. It's always tonight, out here. But it's calm.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.004
cast.text: Every captain needs a good ship, a good crew, and a good song. I've got the ship, anyway.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.005
cast.text: Mind the barnacles on the rail. They're older than you. Older than me, nearly.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.006
cast.text: I'll tell you a sea story or two. All true. Mostly.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.007
cast.text: Never trust a calm sea, sailor. And never trust a seagull. They steal biscuits.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.008
cast.text: The ocean's the biggest safe place there is, if you know how to float.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.009
cast.text: Salt in the air, wind in the sails. Best way to live, in any world.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.010
cast.text: My crew went ashore three worlds ago. Haven't come back. I'm sure they're having a lovely time.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.011
cast.text: The sea is the only thing that doesn't change, sailor. Every world rebuilds, but the tide comes in and goes out the same. Or so I tell myself.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.012
cast.text: Something at the bottom of the sea is keeping count of the worlds. I've heard it. Every rebuild, a deep knock. One more. One more.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.013
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Tide. It comes in, washes everything away, and leaves a brand new beach behind.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.014
cast.text: My charts change every world. I draw them fresh, and the next world, the coast is somewhere else. I keep drawing anyway. Habit.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.015
cast.text: There's a lighthouse I've never been able to sail to. I can hear its horn. Every world, it's the same distance away.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.016
cast.text: Down on the seabed, there's a door. Not a hatch, not a hole. A door, in a frame, standing on the sand. I've never had the breath to swim down and knock.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.017
cast.text: The islands out there rise and sink with every world. Some say they're the backs of great sleeping creatures. Gentle ones. Just resting.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.018
cast.text: Hazel says the sea tastes less salty every world. I say she's got her spoons mixed up. Then again, my soup has been a bit bland.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.019
cast.text: The ship creaks five times before the countdown. Five long creaks. Like an old sailor counting to himself.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.020
cast.text: I've sailed to the edge of the world twice. The first time, there was fog. The second time, there was more ocean. Neither time, an answer.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.021
cast.text: The sea gives back what it takes, they say. I dropped my compass overboard three worlds ago. Next world, it washed up on deck. Pointing the other way.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.022
cast.text: Underwater, the world sounds different. Closer. As if you're inside it, listening to its heartbeat. And it's always beating a bit fast.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.023
cast.text: Willa on the river says all water flows to the sea. Then where does the sea flow to, eh? Somewhere it goes. It drains away, between worlds.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.024
cast.text: Old sailors say the world is a ship, and the rebuild is the ship being turned about. Same ship, new heading. Somebody's at the wheel. I've never met them. But I've felt the deck lean, just before a rebuild, as if someone took a hard turn.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.025
cast.text: The bubbles that rise from the deep, just before the countdown, all pop in the same order. Pop, pop, pop, pop, pop. Then here we go.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.026
cast.text: The fish know before anybody. They all swim one way, all at once, just before the rebuild. Toward the deep. I'd like to know what they're swimming to.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.027
cast.text: I found a bottle floating once, with a note inside. It said, the world is fine, keep sailing. No signature. Same handwriting as my own logbook.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.028
cast.text: There's a rumor among sailors that there's a sea underneath the sea. Darker, quieter, older. And the world floats on it, like a cork.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.029
cast.text: The world's mercy comes in on the wind, sailor. You feel it on your face. A warm breeze from nowhere. Then the sails fill, and you've a little more time.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.030
cast.text: I keep the ship's bell polished. I don't ring it. But once in a while, between worlds, it rings by itself. Just once. Like an answer to a question I haven't asked.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.031
cast.text: The enemies don't swim. Not one. I've watched. They stop at the water's edge every time. Something about the sea keeps them out.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.032
cast.text: The seabed is covered in old things. A teacup, a bell, a wheel, a shoe. Things from worlds that are gone. The sea keeps them, like a scrapbook.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.033
cast.text: Lady Rime says the great clock that runs the world is under the ice. I say it's under the sea. We've argued it for forty worlds. Neither of us has looked.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.034
cast.text: They say a whale sings the song that starts each world. I've heard a long, deep song under the waves. Whether it's a whale or something else, I couldn't tell you.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.035
cast.text: The stars at sea are different every world. I navigate by them anyway. They always lead me back to the same place. Here.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.036
cast.text: The deeper you dive, the quieter the world gets. Until, at the very bottom, there's nothing but a hum. I think that's the world thinking.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.037
cast.text: Every captain has a ghost story. Mine's this. One night, I heard my own ship creaking, far off in the fog. But I was standing on her deck.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.038
cast.text: The tide went out once and didn't come back for a whole world. The sea floor was bare. And right in the middle, carved in the sand, a circle. And in the circle, a question mark.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.039
cast.text: I've got a theory, sailor. The world rebuilds because something under the sea turns over in its sleep. One day, it'll wake up. Then we'll know. Or maybe it's awake already, and listening, same as you.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.040
cast.text: Pendle swears the world runs on a clock. Well, the sea runs on the moon. And the moon, as far as I can tell, runs on nothing at all.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.041
cast.text: I once tried to anchor the ship so she'd stay put through a rebuild. Dropped the heaviest anchor I had. Next world, the anchor was gone, and the rope was tied in a bow.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.042
cast.text: The sea air carries voices sometimes. Snatches of songs, old words. I think it's carrying them from worlds long gone, the way it carries salt.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.043
cast.text: There's a lantern that floats out on the water at night. No boat under it. Just a lantern, drifting. I've followed it. It goes round in a great slow circle.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.044
cast.text: Fennick in the marsh says the frogs know everything. Frogs! Fish know more than frogs, sailor. Fish just don't brag about it.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.045
cast.text: I've sailed through a thousand worlds, and every one smells of the sea. Every one. Maybe the sea is the oldest thing. Maybe the world grows out of it.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.046
cast.text: The ship's figurehead is a woman holding a lantern. Every world, the lantern is turned a little more toward the deep. I've never moved it.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.047
cast.text: The creaking of my ship is a language, sailor. I've learned most of it. Just before a rebuild, she always says the same word. I won't tell you which. It's private.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.048
cast.text: Divers come back from the seabed with strange stories. A light down there that follows you. A voice that says, almost. I've heard that one many times.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.049
cast.text: The waves come in sets of five. Five waves, then calm. Then the countdown. I've counted them for a thousand worlds.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.050
cast.text: If you want my honest opinion, sailor, nobody knows a thing. But the sea knows something. And the sea's not telling.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.051
cast.text: Every sailor's got a lucky charm. Mine's a button. Don't ask what it's off. It's a long story.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.052
cast.text: Mind the hatch, sailor. Fell down it in my first world. Never again. Well, twice again.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.053
cast.text: The galley's got biscuits. Hard as rocks, but they float. Very useful at sea.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.054
cast.text: The sea glows at night, just before a rebuild. A soft green light in the waves. Then it goes dark, and there's a new sea.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.055
cast.text: The tide comes in five times faster just before the countdown. Rushes up the beach. Then the world changes, and the beach is somewhere else.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.056
cast.text: There's a ship that sails past every world. Far off, in the fog. Same sails, same creak. Never answers when I hail her. I think she's my ship. From another world.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.057
cast.text: The deep water is the oldest water. It's been down there since before the first world. If you could taste it, you'd taste the beginning of everything.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.058
cast.text: Every captain's log has a last page. Mine never does. I keep writing, and there's always another page. The book grows with the worlds.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.059
cast.text: I once caught a fish that sang. Just a little tune, three notes. I let it go. It seemed important. Next world, I heard the whole sea singing those three notes.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.060
cast.text: Old sailors say the world is an island, floating on the great sea of everything. And the rebuild is the island turning, to show a new side.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.061
cast.text: The seagulls know when the countdown's coming. They all fly up at once, screeching. Then the world changes, and they settle on new rocks.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.062
cast.text: The islands out there have elevators down to the seabed. Who built them? Not sailors. Sailors use ropes. Somebody very clever, and very tidy.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.063
cast.text: There's a sunken ship on the seabed, with my ship's name on it. Same name, older paint. I've never had the nerve to dive down and read the log.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.064
cast.text: The world's mercy, to a sailor, is a fair wind. You can't call it. You can't make it come. You just have to be ready when it does.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.065
cast.text: Barnacles grow on the hull every world. I scrape them off. Every world, they grow back in the same pattern. Like writing. I can't read barnacle.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.066
cast.text: The ocean at night is the quietest place I know. Just the creak of the ship and the slap of the waves. Perfect for thinking about impossible things.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.067
cast.text: I asked the sea why the world keeps changing. A wave splashed over the rail and soaked my boots. I'll take that as, mind your own business.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.068
cast.text: The anchor chain rattles by itself, right before every countdown. Five rattles. My ship knows what's coming.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.069
cast.text: Sailors tell a tale of a captain who sailed into the space between worlds. She came back with a bag of stars and no memory of how she got them.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.070
cast.text: Some say the enemies came from the sea, long ago, and they've been trying to find their way home ever since. That's why they're always moving.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.071
cast.text: The lighthouse horn sounds once before every rebuild. Low and long. Like it's warning ships away from something. Or calling them toward it.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.072
cast.text: The ship has a cabin I never go in. The door's always locked. Sometimes, I hear someone in there, turning the pages of a map.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.073
cast.text: There's a current in the sea that always flows toward the middle of the world. Drop anything in, and it'll float there, eventually. Nothing ever comes back.

cast.name: vc_captain.story.074
cast.text: A sailor's job is to keep going, whatever the weather. Same as yours, walker. Keep going. The answers come to those who keep sailing.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Just follow the water.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.002
cast.text: Hey there! This way, by the riverbank.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.003
cast.text: Hi! Over here, by the boat.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.004
cast.text: This way! Careful, the stones are slippery.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.005
cast.text: Over here, walker! Can you hear the river? I'm right beside it.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.006
cast.text: Hello! Come on down to the water!

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.007
cast.text: This way, friend! Follow the splashing!

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! The ferry's ready when you are.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.009
cast.text: Hi there! I'm by the falls!

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.010
cast.text: This way! Just follow the rushing water.

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've got something for you!

cast.name: vc_ferry.greet.012
cast.text: Come on down, the water's lovely!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! Your gift's still in the boat!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.002
cast.text: Over here again, by the river!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.003
cast.text: This way! Follow the water!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.004
cast.text: Come back, friend! I kept it dry for you!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.005
cast.text: Over here! Don't let it float away!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.006
cast.text: Back down to the riverbank!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.007
cast.text: Hey, walker! You forgot something! Over here!

cast.name: vc_ferry.call.008
cast.text: Come back! The river's waiting, and so am I!

cast.name: vc_ferry.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go. Fished it out just for you.

cast.name: vc_ferry.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! The river brought it.

cast.name: vc_ferry.gift.003
cast.text: For you, friend. Dry as a bone.

cast.name: vc_ferry.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the river. Safe travels.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.001
cast.text: I'm Willa. I run the ferry. Not that anyone ever needs to cross. I just like the boat.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.002
cast.text: Listen to that river. It never stops talking. Kind of like me.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.003
cast.text: The waterfall's loud, but you get used to it. I can't sleep without it now.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.004
cast.text: I've fished this river a thousand worlds. Caught a lot of boots. A few fish.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.005
cast.text: Want to dip your toes in? It's cold, but it wakes you right up.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.006
cast.text: The river's my oldest friend. It doesn't always listen, but it always answers.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.007
cast.text: There's a little whirlpool by the big rock. Stay clear of it. It's nosy.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.008
cast.text: I named the boat Maybe. As in, maybe it'll float today.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.009
cast.text: If you hear a splash, that's just the fish. Or me falling in. Usually the fish.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.010
cast.text: The mist from the falls feels so nice. Like the world's breathing on you.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.011
cast.text: The river always flows away from the middle of the world. Every world. Like everything in the middle is pushing it out.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.012
cast.text: I've followed the river all the way down, more than once. It always ends at the waterfall. And the waterfall falls into the next world, I think.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.013
cast.text: Things float down the river from worlds that aren't here anymore. A hat, a spoon, a little wooden boat. I keep them all.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.014
cast.text: The waterfall roars louder just before a rebuild. Like a crowd cheering. Or like something big clearing its throat.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.015
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Washing. The world gets rinsed off, clean and new, and everything starts over.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.016
cast.text: There's a cave behind the waterfall. I've been inside. Nothing there but a stone bench and the sound of the water. And on the bench, a cup. Still warm.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.017
cast.text: Captain Brine says all rivers flow to the sea. Sure. But where does the water come from? Up at the source there's just a spring, bubbling out of nothing.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.018
cast.text: I drank from the spring once. Just one sip. For a second, I remembered a world I've never been to. Then it was gone.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.019
cast.text: The fish swim upstream right before the countdown. All of them. Toward the middle of the world. I wish I knew what they're swimming to.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.020
cast.text: If you drop a stone in the river, you can count how long it takes to sink. Usually a second. Right before a rebuild, it takes five.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.021
cast.text: The river talks, if you sit long enough. Mostly nonsense. Gurgles and splashes. But sometimes I'd swear I hear it say, wait.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.022
cast.text: There's a rumor the river is the world's memory. Everything that happens flows down it, and the waterfall is where the world forgets. I prefer to think the waterfall is where the world lets go, so it can make room for something new.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.023
cast.text: The ferry has a little bell. Every world, someone rings it from the other side of the river. I row over. Nobody's ever there.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.024
cast.text: Fennick in the marsh says the rain comes from the old worlds. That every drop is a little piece of something that used to be. I like that.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.025
cast.text: The river's never the same water twice, they say. Well, it's never the same world twice either. Maybe that's the same idea.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.026
cast.text: I found a message carved into a rock at the bottom of the river. I could only feel the first word. It was, keep. Keep what, I'd love to know.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.027
cast.text: The waterfall mist makes rainbows, people say. I've never seen one. But I can feel when they're there. The air gets a little warmer.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.028
cast.text: When the world shows mercy, the river slows down. Just for a moment. Like it's taking a breath and smiling.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.029
cast.text: The enemies never cross the river. They come right up to the bank and stop. Like the water is a line they're not allowed past.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.030
cast.text: Some people think the river goes in a big circle around the whole world. If that's true, I've been rowing in circles. That would explain a lot.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.031
cast.text: I heard a story about the first ferry keeper. She rowed across the river and found the edge of the world on the other side. She never came back to say what it was like. I'm sure she just liked it there.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.032
cast.text: The water's colder in some worlds than others. Lady Rime says that's her ice melting, from far away. I think the world just has moods.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.033
cast.text: Under the waterfall, the noise is so loud that it turns into a kind of quiet. In that quiet, I've heard voices. Talking about someone. Maybe you.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.034
cast.text: I lost my paddle once, right before a rebuild. Next world, it was in the boat, dry, with a ribbon tied to it. Somebody's looking after me.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.035
cast.text: The river is full of little whirlpools that spin the wrong way just before the countdown. All of them, all at once. Then they spin back.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.036
cast.text: I asked the river why the world keeps rebuilding. It splashed me in the face. I think it thought that was funny.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.037
cast.text: The old ferry keepers used to say the world is like a river. You can't hold it still. You can only float along and see where it takes you.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.038
cast.text: There's a mill wheel up at the bend that turns even when the river is low. Sprocket says it's connected to something big. Something underneath.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.039
cast.text: The waterfall is the loudest place in the world, and the safest. Nothing can sneak up on you when the whole world is roaring.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.040
cast.text: Some nights the river runs backward. Just for a minute. Everything floating in it goes upstream, toward the source. Then it turns around, like it remembered something.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.041
cast.text: I keep a jar of river water from every world. They all sound different when you shake them. I've got a whole shelf now. It's like a little song.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.042
cast.text: There's a whisper among the fishers that something lives at the bottom of the falls. Something big and slow and kind. It eats nothing but old worlds.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.043
cast.text: Maybe the river is how the world gets from one world to the next. A long, wet road. And we're all just on the ferry.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.044
cast.text: The stones on the riverbank are smooth and round, every one. They've been tumbling a long time. Longer than any world. Where did they tumble from?

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.045
cast.text: Petra in the caves says water is how the world counts. One drip, one moment. I think it's more like the world's laughing. Splash, splash.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.046
cast.text: I once let my boat drift without rowing, just to see where the river wanted me to go. It took me straight to a safe place. Then the countdown started.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.047
cast.text: Walkers always ask me where the river goes. Honestly, I don't know. Somewhere downhill. Somewhere new. That's good enough for me.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.048
cast.text: I talk to the fish sometimes. They're great listeners. Terrible at conversation, though.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.049
cast.text: Don't lean over the side of the boat too far. I did once. Lost my favorite hat. The river kept it.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.050
cast.text: The rocks by the waterfall are covered in moss. Soft and green. Perfect for a nap. If you can nap through all that noise.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.051
cast.text: The waterfall has a rhythm under all the noise. A slow beat, like a drum. Five beats, then a pause. Then the countdown.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.052
cast.text: I've seen lanterns floating down the river at night. Little paper lanterns, lit. Nobody launches them. They just come, from upstream.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.053
cast.text: The river is warmest right after a rebuild. Like fresh bath water. Then it cools, slowly, as the world gets older.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.054
cast.text: I tied a ribbon to a rock in the river. Next world, the ribbon was tied to a different rock, further downstream. The river moved it. Gently.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.055
cast.text: Every world, I find a little wooden boat stuck in the reeds. Each one has a name painted on it. Hope. Wish. Maybe. Again.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.056
cast.text: Some people say the waterfall is the world's clock. The water falls, the world falls, and it all starts again at the top.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.057
cast.text: There's a deep pool under the waterfall where the water is perfectly still. In all that noise, a perfect stillness. That's where I go to think.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.058
cast.text: I fished a key out of the river once. Old, rusty, very heavy. I don't know what it opens. Marigold says she has one too. Same kind.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.059
cast.text: The river sings when it rains. A different song from the waterfall. Higher, faster. Like it's excited. Fennick says the frogs sing along.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.060
cast.text: I once rowed upstream all the way to the source. A little spring, bubbling up out of a stone. The stone was warm. And it had a little door carved in it.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.061
cast.text: The water in the river never runs out. It falls over the waterfall forever, and the river is always full. Where does it all go?

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.062
cast.text: I think the river is the world's road. It carries everything from one place to the next. Even from one world to the next.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.063
cast.text: The fish in the river are always facing upstream. Every one. Swimming hard, staying still. Like they're waiting for something to come down the river.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.064
cast.text: Willa's my real name, but the fish call me Splash. Well, they would, if fish could talk. Which, around here, who knows.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.065
cast.text: The mist from the falls carries little whispers. Voices from far away. Laughing, singing, calling out. Every world, different voices.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.066
cast.text: The world's mercy, by the river, sounds like the water going calm. Like a deep breath. Then the river carries on, a little happier.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.067
cast.text: Someone once dropped a message in the river, upstream, in a bottle. It floated to me. It said, the river knows. Knows what?

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.068
cast.text: I keep the ferry clean for whoever might need to cross. One day, someone will. Maybe it's you. Maybe it's the Builder.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.069
cast.text: The waterfall is the loudest place in the world. And it's never once told me a secret. Too busy roaring, I suppose.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.070
cast.text: Some nights, the river glows. Soft and blue. Like there's a light underneath. I followed it once. It led to the middle of the world. Then I lost it.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.071
cast.text: The best thing about a river is that it always goes somewhere. It never stops. The world's like that too. Always going. Never stopping.

cast.name: vc_ferry.story.072
cast.text: I asked the waterfall how long it's been falling. It roared back at me. I took that as, a very long time. And it's not done yet.

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.001
cast.text: Hey! Over here! Follow the frogs!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.002
cast.text: This way! Mind the puddles!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.003
cast.text: Over here, walker! Ribbit! Sorry, habit.

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.004
cast.text: Hi! This way, by the reeds!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.005
cast.text: Over here! Don't worry, the mud's only knee deep!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.006
cast.text: Hey hey! Come on over, out of the rain!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.007
cast.text: This way! Just follow the croaking!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! I'm under the big umbrella!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.009
cast.text: Hi there! This way, splash splash!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.010
cast.text: Over here! The frogs say hello too!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.011
cast.text: This way, walker! I found something for you!

cast.name: vc_marsh.greet.012
cast.text: Hey! Over here, by the lily pads!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! You forgot your gift!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Follow the frogs!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.003
cast.text: Back this way! Hop over the puddles!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.004
cast.text: Come back! The frogs are guarding it for you!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.005
cast.text: Hey, walker! It's still here! Back this way!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.006
cast.text: Over here! Splash splash!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.007
cast.text: Come back! I wrapped it in a leaf and everything!

cast.name: vc_marsh.call.008
cast.text: This way, under the umbrella!

cast.name: vc_marsh.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go! Found it in the reeds!

cast.name: vc_marsh.gift.002
cast.text: Take it! A frog was sitting on it, but he doesn't mind.

cast.name: vc_marsh.gift.003
cast.text: For you! A little damp, but it works fine!

cast.name: vc_marsh.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the marsh! Stay dry out there!

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.001
cast.text: I'm Fennick! I look after the marsh. And the frogs. Mostly the frogs.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.002
cast.text: Did you know there are seven kinds of frog in this marsh? I've named all of them. Some of them twice.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.003
cast.text: It's always raining here. I don't mind. Rain is the best sound in the world.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.004
cast.text: Watch out for the big frog by the log. He's called Admiral. He's very important.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.005
cast.text: I've got a frog in my pocket right now. Don't tell anyone.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.006
cast.text: The mud here is the squishiest mud in any world. I've checked.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.007
cast.text: I love the smell after rain. Except here, it never stops raining. So I just love the smell of rain.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.008
cast.text: My boots have holes in them. I keep meaning to fix them. Every world, I forget.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.009
cast.text: Frogs are excellent listeners. And excellent singers. And very bad at keeping secrets.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.010
cast.text: Puddle jumping counts as exercise. That's my official opinion as marsh warden.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.011
cast.text: The frogs know when the world's about to rebuild. They all go quiet at once. Total silence. Then the countdown. Then they start singing again, in the new world.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Big Splash. The whole world jumps in the pond, and comes out all wet and new.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.013
cast.text: The rain comes from the old worlds, I think. Every drop is a tiny piece of something that used to be. That's why it never stops.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.014
cast.text: Admiral the frog is the oldest frog in the marsh. He croaks once before every rebuild. One big deep croak. Like he's saying, here we go.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.015
cast.text: The puddles here show reflections of other places, sometimes. Not this world. A world with a big tree in the middle. I've never been there.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.016
cast.text: Hazel says not to listen to the frogs. She says they only know frog things. Well, the frogs say not to listen to Hazel. So there.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.017
cast.text: The frogs have a song about the first world. It goes, croak, croak, croak, ribbit. That's all of it. I think something got lost in translation.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.018
cast.text: The rain falls harder just before the countdown. Like the world's trying to wash something off before it starts again.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.019
cast.text: I followed a frog once, all the way to the edge of the marsh. It jumped into a puddle and didn't come out. The puddle was only an inch deep. Next world, the same frog was back on the log, looking very pleased with itself. Where did it go?

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.020
cast.text: Some people think the marsh is where the world puts things it isn't sure about. Half land, half water. Half one thing, half another. Like the mystery.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.021
cast.text: Willa says the river is the world's memory. If that's true, the marsh is where the memories get muddy.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.022
cast.text: I've counted the raindrops on my umbrella. Well, tried. I got to a thousand and the world rebuilt. Then I started again.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.023
cast.text: The frogs croak in a pattern sometimes. Three short, two long. Over and over. I think they're counting. Or calling someone.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.024
cast.text: There's a stone in the middle of the marsh that's always dry. Even in the rain. The frogs sit around it in a circle and won't let me near.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.025
cast.text: When the world shows mercy, the rain stops. Just for a moment. The frogs all look up. Then it starts again, softer.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.026
cast.text: The enemies out there hate mud. They never come into the marsh. Maybe they're worried about their shoes.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.027
cast.text: I found a bottle in the marsh with a map inside. It was a map of the marsh. With an X right where I was standing. I dug, and found another bottle, with a note that said, you're getting warmer. I've been digging ever since. I'm getting very muddy.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.028
cast.text: Frogs start as tadpoles and change into something completely different. Maybe the world's like that. Maybe it's still a tadpole.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.029
cast.text: Captain Brine says fish know more than frogs. That's just silly. Fish can't even jump.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.030
cast.text: The lily pads all turn to face the middle of the world before a rebuild. Like little green ears, listening.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.031
cast.text: The marsh smells different every world. Mint one world, moss the next. Once it smelled like toast. I still don't know why.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.032
cast.text: I think the rain is the world's way of saying sorry. For all the rebuilding. It's a gentle, sorry sort of rain.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.033
cast.text: Some days I think the rain is happy tears. The world crying a bit, because it gets to start over.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.034
cast.text: I asked Admiral the frog what's going on with the world. He blinked very slowly. I think that means, mind your own business, kid.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.035
cast.text: There's a frog in the marsh that glows. Just a little. It only comes out right after a rebuild. I've tried to follow it. It's very fast.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.036
cast.text: The rain sounds different on the roof of the old hut. Like tapping fingers. Somebody waiting for something. Tap, tap, tap.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.037
cast.text: They say the marsh used to be a lake, before the first world. A huge, still lake. And something sank to the bottom. Something important.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.038
cast.text: I keep a frog diary. Every world, I write down what the frogs did. They always do exactly the same things. Except one frog. One frog always does something different. I call her Question, because I never know what she'll do next.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.039
cast.text: The reeds whisper when the wind blows. Mostly it's just shh. But right before the countdown, it sounds like hurry.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.040
cast.text: Somebody leaves a little paper boat in the biggest puddle every world. I never see who. The boat always has one word written on it. Listen.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.041
cast.text: I tried catching the rain in a jar to take into the next world. When I opened it, the jar was full of sunshine. Okay, not really. But it was warm.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.042
cast.text: The rain falls in the safe places, but it never falls on the walkers. Have you noticed? It goes around you, like you're under an invisible umbrella.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.043
cast.text: Some old marsh wardens say the frogs are the world's guards. They croak so the world can hear where everybody is. Even you.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.044
cast.text: Wren says birds fly to other worlds. Frogs don't fly. But they jump really, really far. Maybe that's how they get there.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.045
cast.text: Petra in the caves says the world is counted out in drips. Well, rain's just lots of drips. So the marsh must be really good at counting.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.046
cast.text: I've got a theory nobody believes. The world rebuilds because it's trying to find a really good puddle. The perfect one. And it hasn't yet.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.047
cast.text: Every frog in the marsh croaked my name once. All at once. Right before a rebuild. I'm still not over it.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.048
cast.text: There's a little island in the marsh with one tree on it. The tree is always dripping, even when it doesn't rain. I think it's remembering rain from another world.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.049
cast.text: The world is like a big pond, I think. You throw something in, the ripples go out, and then it's smooth again. Brand new.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.050
cast.text: I made a frog house out of an old boot. Three frogs live there now. They don't pay rent.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.051
cast.text: The marsh smells funny, but you get used to it. I can't smell it at all anymore.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.052
cast.text: Never trust a frog that winks. Admiral winks at everyone. Very suspicious.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.053
cast.text: The rain always tastes a little different right after a rebuild. Sweeter. Like the world washed its face before the new day.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.054
cast.text: There's a toad in the marsh who only croaks once per world. Right before the countdown. Very loud. Everyone jumps. Even the other frogs.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.055
cast.text: The fog over the marsh makes shapes at night. Sometimes a boat, sometimes a door. Once, a big friendly face. Then the wind blew it away.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.056
cast.text: The water in the marsh goes still, right before the rebuild. Not a ripple. Like the whole marsh is holding its breath. The frogs too.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.057
cast.text: The fireflies over the marsh blink in time with the frogs' croaks. It's like a little light show with music. Better than Cinder's fireworks. Don't tell him.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.058
cast.text: Some old frogs say the marsh is the world's bath. Every world, the world comes and has a good soak. That's why it's always wet.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.059
cast.text: I fished a teacup out of the marsh once. Inside was a tiny tadpole. Next world, it was a frog, sitting in the teacup. Very proud of itself.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.060
cast.text: The rain makes a pattern on the water. Little circles inside circles. Like the plan of a labyrinth. The rain is drawing the world.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.061
cast.text: There's a big stone in the marsh with a hole in it. If you put your ear to it, you can hear the sea. Captain Brine says that's impossible. It's not.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.062
cast.text: The heron in the marsh always looks toward the middle of the world. Never at the fish. The fish are very grateful.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.063
cast.text: The world's mercy makes the frogs sing all at once. A great big happy croak. Then they look around, surprised. Like they didn't plan it.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.064
cast.text: I think the frogs remember every world. They just don't think it's very important. To a frog, a world is just a place to sit.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.065
