cast.text: There's an old hut on stilts in the middle of the marsh. Nobody lives there. But every world, there's a fresh cup of tea on the table.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.066
cast.text: The puddles are deepest right after a rebuild. Like the world filled them fresh. I always jump in the first one I find. It's a tradition.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.067
cast.text: Clover says bees always find their way home. Frogs too! Every frog in the marsh finds its own lily pad, every world. Same pad, same frog.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.068
cast.text: I think the marsh is where the world puts its rough drafts. Muddy, messy, unfinished. Then it takes them out and makes them into proper worlds.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.069
cast.text: The rain sometimes falls in a rhythm. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter, stop. Five drops, a pause. Petra says the drips in her cave do the same thing.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.070
cast.text: Frogs croak to find each other in the dark. Maybe the world rebuilds to find something too. Calling out, every few minutes. Are you there?

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.071
cast.text: There's a family of ducks that paddles in a circle every world. Always the same circle. They're either very organized, or very lost.

cast.name: vc_marsh.story.072
cast.text: I tried staying awake for a whole rebuild once. I blinked. Just once. And the whole marsh was different. You can't watch it happen. Not even frogs can.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Follow the drips.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.002
cast.text: Hello! This way, deeper in.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.003
cast.text: Over here, walker. Watch your head, the ceiling's low.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.004
cast.text: This way! It echoes, so just keep coming.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.005
cast.text: Hi there! I'm by the big stalagmite.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Drip, drip, that's me.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.007
cast.text: This way, walker. Careful, it's slippery.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.008
cast.text: Hello! Come on in, the cave is cool and quiet.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.009
cast.text: Over here, by the underground pool!

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.010
cast.text: This way. Just follow my voice and the echoes.

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've found something for you down here!

cast.name: vc_caver.greet.012
cast.text: Hi! Come in, I don't get many visitors down here.

cast.name: vc_caver.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! Your gift's still down here!

cast.name: vc_caver.call.002
cast.text: Over here again, by the drips.

cast.name: vc_caver.call.003
cast.text: This way, back into the cave.

cast.name: vc_caver.call.004
cast.text: Come back! I've kept it safe and dry, well, mostly dry.

cast.name: vc_caver.call.005
cast.text: Over here, walker! Follow the echoes!

cast.name: vc_caver.call.006
cast.text: Back this way! Mind the puddles!

cast.name: vc_caver.call.007
cast.text: Hey! Don't leave yet! I've got something for you!

cast.name: vc_caver.call.008
cast.text: This way again! Drip, drip!

cast.name: vc_caver.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go. Found it in a crack in the rock.

cast.name: vc_caver.gift.002
cast.text: Take this. Every caver needs supplies.

cast.name: vc_caver.gift.003
cast.text: For you. Straight from the deep.

cast.name: vc_caver.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the cave. Mind your head on the way out.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.001
cast.text: I'm Petra. I explore caves. And then I explore the caves inside the caves.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.002
cast.text: Listen to the drips. Every one is a tiny bell. I find it very peaceful.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.003
cast.text: Stalactites hang down, stalagmites stand up. I always remember because the tights hang down. Sort of.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.004
cast.text: I've mapped this cave a thousand times. It's never quite the same cave.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.005
cast.text: Don't worry about the echo. It just likes repeating things. Repeating things. See?

cast.name: vc_caver.story.006
cast.text: I like it underground. It's quiet, it's cool, and the rocks don't argue.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.007
cast.text: Every rock tells a story. Most of them are very slow stories.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.008
cast.text: Mind the low bit. I've bumped my head there in every world.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.009
cast.text: The pool here is so still, you can hear a single drop land from across the cave.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.010
cast.text: I keep a notebook full of drip counts. My friends think it's strange. I don't have many friends down here, except the drips.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.011
cast.text: The drips count the world, I'm sure of it. One drip, one moment. If I could count them all, I'd know exactly when the next rebuild comes.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.012
cast.text: I've noticed the drips speed up just before the countdown. Drip, drip, drip, faster and faster. Then five big drips, and the world changes.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.013
cast.text: Stalactites take thousands of years to grow. Yet here, every world, they're a tiny bit longer. Which means the cave remembers. Even when the world doesn't.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.014
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Shudder. The whole cave shivers, every rock and pebble, and then it settles into a new shape.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.015
cast.text: Deep under the cave, there's a layer of rock that never changes. Smooth, dark, and old. I think the whole world is built on top of it, again and again.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.016
cast.text: I put my ear to that old rock once. I heard a ticking. Slow and steady. Pendle would love to hear it.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.017
cast.text: The underground pool has no bottom. I've dropped a stone in and listened for a whole world. Never heard it land.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.018
cast.text: There are marks on the cave wall. Scratches in rows of five. Somebody was counting. Somebody was down here before me, counting worlds.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.019
cast.text: I've been finding crystals in new places every world. They hum when I tap them. Every crystal hums the same note. The note of the ghost choir.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.020
cast.text: Some cavers say the caves are the world's roots. Everything above ground is just leaves and branches. Change the leaves, the roots stay.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.021
cast.text: The echo in this cave lasts longer than it should. If you shout, it comes back five seconds later. Exactly five. Same as the countdown.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.022
cast.text: The water here is the oldest water in the world. It's been dripping since before the first rebuild. It tastes of stone, and something sweet.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.023
cast.text: I followed an underground stream once. It led deeper and deeper. At the end, there was a wall. And on the other side of the wall, I could hear the sea.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.024
cast.text: Captain Brine says something at the bottom of the sea keeps count. I think it's down here, under the caves, and the sea is just above it.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.025
cast.text: Every world, there's a new tunnel in the cave I've never explored. I always explore it. It always leads back to here. Every single time.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.026
cast.text: Some people think the world is built from the top down. I think it's built from the bottom up. Starting down here, in the dark, where it's quiet.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.027
cast.text: I found a lantern deep in the cave, still lit. No footprints anywhere near it. Just the lantern, on a ledge, waiting.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.028
cast.text: The bats in the cave all fly out together just before the countdown. A big rush of wings. Then the world changes, and they all fly back in.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.029
cast.text: When the world shows mercy, the drips stop for a moment. Total silence. Then they start again, a little slower. Like the world is giving itself time.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.030
cast.text: I made a map of the cave and pinned it to the wall. Every world, someone adds a new tunnel to it. In pencil. I never draw in pencil.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.031
cast.text: The enemies never come into the cave. Too dark, maybe. Or maybe they know there's something down here that's older than them.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.032
cast.text: Hazel says there's a smooth old floor under every world. She's right. I've stood on it. It's warm. Like something underneath is breathing.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.033
cast.text: Every rock in the cave has layers. Like pages. I think every layer is a world that came before. If that's true, there have been millions.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.034
cast.text: I asked the cave why the world keeps changing. The echo just asked me back. Why does the world keep changing. Changing. Changing.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.035
cast.text: Stalagmites grow up from the floor toward the stalactites. In a few worlds, they'll touch. I want to be here when they do. Something might happen.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.036
cast.text: I've heard voices down here. Not scary ones. Soft, far away. Like people in another cave, in another world, wondering the same things as me.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.037
cast.text: There's a rumor that the deepest cave goes all the way through the world, and comes out the other side. Into what, nobody knows.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.038
cast.text: The drips have a rhythm. Most of the time, it's random. But once every world, they play a little tune. Five notes. Always the same five.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.039
cast.text: Fennick says the rain is pieces of old worlds. Well, all the rain sinks down here eventually. So this cave is full of old worlds. Drip by drip.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.040
cast.text: I carved my name in the rock once. Next world, it was still there. And underneath, in different handwriting, someone had carved, me too.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.041
cast.text: The cave is the quietest safe place, I think. Quiet enough to hear the world think. It thinks in drips.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.042
cast.text: I've been all the way down to where the water stops dripping and starts rising. Up from below. Like the world is filling itself from underneath.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.043
cast.text: Rocks don't change much. That's why I like them. But every world, the cave floor tilts a tiny bit more toward the middle of the world.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.044
cast.text: Some cavers believe the world is a giant geode. Rough outside, full of crystals inside. And the rebuild is somebody cracking it open to look.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.045
cast.text: I once fell asleep in the cave during a rebuild. I didn't feel anything. I just woke up in a slightly different cave, with my notebook open to a new page.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.046
cast.text: There's a pool in the deepest part of the cave where the water is warm. Warm water, deep underground. Something is keeping it warm.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.047
cast.text: The crystals glow faintly right after a rebuild. Just for a moment. Like they've just been switched on. Somebody flipped a switch.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.048
cast.text: Count the drips between rebuilds, and you'll get a different number every time. But it's always a number that ends in five. Always.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.049
cast.text: I think the world is patient, like a cave. It doesn't rush. It just keeps dripping, and growing, and changing, very slowly. Well, slowly for a cave.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.050
cast.text: I carry three torches, two ropes, and one sandwich. The sandwich is the most important.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.051
cast.text: Watch out for the bats. They're friendly, but they're very bad at sharing the ceiling.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.052
cast.text: I love the smell of caves. Cold stone and wet moss. Better than any flower.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.053
cast.text: Every drip in this cave lands in exactly the same spot, every world. Even when the cave changes shape. The drips have a map.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.054
cast.text: There's a crystal deep down that rings when the world shows mercy. One clear note. I've heard it three times. Each time, I cried a little. Happy crying.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.055
cast.text: The cave goes down further every world. I've never reached the bottom. I think the world is digging itself deeper, so it has more room for secrets.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.056
cast.text: I found a staircase carved into the rock, going down. Very old, very worn. Every step has a number. They count down. Five, four, three, two, one. At the bottom is a wall. Smooth as glass. When I put my hand on it, it was warm, and I could feel it ticking.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.057
cast.text: The underground lake has fish with no eyes. They don't need them. They listen, like you. They always swim toward the walkers.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.058
cast.text: Some cavers say the caves are where the world keeps its memories. Every tunnel is a memory. Every drip is a thought.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.059
cast.text: I once found a candle burning on a ledge, deep in the cave. Nobody had been down there in a thousand worlds. The wax was still soft.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.060
cast.text: The rocks in the cave hum when the countdown starts. Only a little. You have to put your ear right against them. They hum the world's song.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.061
cast.text: The deepest drip in the cave falls once per world. Just once. Right as the rebuild happens. I've waited for it. It's a very big drip.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.062
cast.text: There's a rumor that if you follow the drips down far enough, you'll find where all the water comes from. A spring with no bottom, in the middle of the world.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.063
cast.text: The bats always hang facing the same way. Toward the middle of the world. Upside down, of course. They'd find it confusing otherwise.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.064
cast.text: The cave is the world's basement, I think. Where it keeps old things it doesn't need anymore, but can't bear to throw away.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.065
cast.text: I left a rope in the cave once, tied to a rock, going down into a hole. Next world, someone had tied a knot at the bottom. A very neat one.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.066
cast.text: The echo in this cave sometimes answers a question you didn't ask. I said hello once. It said, hello. Then, a moment later, it said, almost.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.067
cast.text: Captain Brine says the sea is the oldest thing in the world. I say rock is older. The sea sits on rock. Rock sits on, well, that's the question.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.068
cast.text: I keep a pebble from every world in my pocket. They clack together when I walk. Like a little drum, keeping time. My own countdown.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.069
cast.text: Every world, the stalactites drip in a slightly different rhythm. I write them all down. One day, I'll play them all at once and hear the answer.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.070
cast.text: The safest place in the world is underground. Nothing changes much down here. Even the rebuild is gentle in a cave. Just a little shiver.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.071
cast.text: There's a hole in the deepest cave that breathes. In and out, slow and cool. Corbin says the wind is the world breathing. I think I've found its nose.

cast.name: vc_caver.story.072
cast.text: I asked a stalagmite how old it was. It didn't answer, of course. But I counted the rings. It's older than every world I know. Older than the first.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, friend. Follow the crickets.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.002
cast.text: Hey there. This way, through the trees.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.003
cast.text: Over here. Mind the roots.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.004
cast.text: Evening, walker. I'm by the old pine.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.005
cast.text: This way. Quiet steps, the owls are listening.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.006
cast.text: Over here, friend. I've got a little fire going.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.007
cast.text: Hello. Just follow my voice through the woods.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.008
cast.text: This way, walker. Watch for low branches.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.009
cast.text: Over here. Safe and sound, under the trees.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.010
cast.text: Hey. This way, by the big stump.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.011
cast.text: Over here, friend. Got something for you.

cast.name: vc_ranger.greet.012
cast.text: Evening. Come on over, the crickets won't mind.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.001
cast.text: Hey, friend. Come on back. Your gift's still here.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. Follow the crickets.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.003
cast.text: This way, back through the trees.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.004
cast.text: Come back, walker. I kept it for you.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.005
cast.text: Over here. Mind the roots on the way.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.006
cast.text: Back this way, friend. The forest will wait.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.007
cast.text: Hey. You left something. Over here.

cast.name: vc_ranger.call.008
cast.text: This way again, by the old pine.

cast.name: vc_ranger.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go, friend. Found it under the pine needles.

cast.name: vc_ranger.gift.002
cast.text: Take this. The forest provides.

cast.name: vc_ranger.gift.003
cast.text: For you. Stay safe out there.

cast.name: vc_ranger.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the woods. Go easy, walker.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.001
cast.text: I'm Rowan. Forest ranger. I look after the trees, and the trees look after me.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.002
cast.text: Listen to those crickets. Best orchestra in any world.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.003
cast.text: Owls are hooting tonight. They're always hooting tonight. It's always night in this forest.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.004
cast.text: Leave no trace, friend. That's the first rule of the forest.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.005
cast.text: I've walked every path in these woods. Every world, there are new ones to walk.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.006
cast.text: If you're ever lost in a forest, sit down and listen. The forest will tell you where to go.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.007
cast.text: The crickets get louder when it's warm, and slower when it's cool. Nature's thermometer.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.008
cast.text: I sleep under the stars most nights. Well, every night. There's no day here.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.009
cast.text: That rustling's just a hedgehog. He visits most worlds. I call him Pinecone.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.010
cast.text: Good boots, a warm coat, and a quiet mind. That's all a ranger needs.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.011
cast.text: The forest regrows every world. Different trees, different paths. But the oldest pine is always here. Same bark, same rings. I've counted.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Regrowing. Like a forest after a long winter. Everything comes back, fresh and green and a little bit different.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.013
cast.text: The crickets stop chirping right before the countdown. All of them, all at once. In all my years, I've never heard crickets do that anywhere else.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.014
cast.text: There's an owl in the old pine who only hoots once per world. Right before the rebuild. One long hoot. Like she's saying, time.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.015
cast.text: Some folks think the world is a garden. Mortimer does. I think it's more like a wild forest. Nobody planted it. It just keeps growing.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.016
cast.text: The roots of the trees go deeper than the labyrinths. Way deeper. Dig down far enough, and you'll find them, all tangled together, all connected.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.017
cast.text: I've followed the roots down once, as far as I could. They all lead the same way. Toward the middle of the world. To something they're drinking from.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.018
cast.text: Every tree has rings. One ring for every year. The old pine has more rings than there have been worlds. How can that be?

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.019
cast.text: There's a path in the forest that's always there, every world. Narrow, mossy, quiet. I've walked it to the end. It ends at a gate in the middle of nowhere. No fence on either side. You could walk around it. I never have. It feels rude.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.020
cast.text: The crickets chirp in a pattern if you listen long enough. Slow, slow, quick quick slow. It's the same rhythm the drips make in Petra's cave.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.021
cast.text: The world's mercy comes through the forest like a warm wind. The leaves rustle, the crickets get louder, and for a moment, everything feels right.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.022
cast.text: Some rangers say the forest is where the world rests. The trees are its thoughts, slow and green. And the rebuild is just the world changing its mind.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.023
cast.text: I've found tracks in the mud I can't name. Not deer, not fox. Something with soft round feet, walking slowly, stopping often. Like it's listening too.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.024
cast.text: Every world, there's a new tree in the clearing. A sapling. It never grows up. The next world, there's another one. Somebody's planting them.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.025
cast.text: The enemies stay out of the forest. Too many trees to throw around, maybe. Or maybe the forest doesn't let them in.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.026
cast.text: Hazel says the world is a spell. Well, if it is, the forest is the oldest part of it. These trees remember the first words.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.027
cast.text: I asked the old pine why the world keeps changing. A pine cone fell on my head. Mortimer says the oak does the same to him. Trees have a sense of humor.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.028
cast.text: Fireflies show up just before the countdown. Hundreds of them. They all fly up, toward the sky. Then the world changes, and they're gone.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.029
cast.text: The forest smells like rain and pine and something sweet I can't name. Every world, that sweet smell gets a little stronger.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.030
cast.text: I've seen the Builder's tools in the forest. An axe stuck in a stump. A saw hung on a branch. Never seen the Builder, though.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.031
cast.text: Some rangers think the Builder is a woodcutter. Cuts the world down, plants a new one. I hope not. I like these trees.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.032
cast.text: There's a stream in the forest that only flows at night. Since it's always night here, it always flows. But I've heard it stop, just before a rebuild.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.033
cast.text: The moss grows on the north side of every tree, in every world. Mortimer says his moss does the same. What's in the north? Nobody knows.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.034
cast.text: I carved a mark into a tree once, to see if it'd still be there next world. It was. But on a different tree. In a different forest.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.035
cast.text: Old rangers say the forest is the world's lungs. Every rebuild is one long breath out, then in. Fresh air for a fresh world.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.036
cast.text: Wren says the birds know the answer, but they sing it too fast for us to catch. I believe it. Birds are always in a hurry.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.037
cast.text: The crickets here have been chirping since before the first world, they say. Same crickets, same song. They're older than the trees.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.038
cast.text: I found a ranger's hat on a branch once. Not mine. Older, faded, very well worn. Inside, a note. Keep the paths clear. Someone's coming.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.039
cast.text: Some nights the forest goes quiet, and I can hear something far off, walking. Big, slow, steady steps. Not scary. Patient. Like a gardener checking on things.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.040
cast.text: The rebuild never knocks down the old pine. Every other tree changes, but not that one. I think the world built around it. Not the other way around.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.041
cast.text: I've got a theory, friend. The world rebuilds because it's growing. And when you grow, you change shape. Simple as that. Of course, then you have to ask, what's it growing into?

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.042
cast.text: The night sky in the forest has one star that never moves. Every world, same place. Commander Vega says it's a planet. I think it's a lantern.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.043
cast.text: The pine needles make a soft carpet. Walk on them quietly, and you can hear the forest floor humming. Very low, very slow. The world's own tune.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.044
cast.text: Squirrels hide nuts all over the forest, every world. And every world, they forget where. I sometimes think the world does the same thing with its answers.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.045
cast.text: There's a stone circle deep in the woods. Moss covered, very old. In the middle, the grass never grows. It's the only place in the forest where the crickets won't go.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.046
cast.text: Walkers like you come through the forest every world. You always stop and listen. That's good. The forest likes a good listener. So does the world.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.047
cast.text: The trees lean a little toward you as you pass. Haven't you felt it? They're curious. They've never met anyone who stays through every world but you.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.048
cast.text: Hungry? I've got trail mix. Mostly raisins. Somebody ate all the nuts. I suspect Pinecone.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.049
cast.text: Mind the nettles on the left. They sting. Nature's way of saying, keep to the path.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.050
cast.text: I carve walking sticks in my spare time. Got a whole pile. Take one if you like.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.051
cast.text: The owls in the forest call to each other across the trees. Right before a rebuild, they all call at once. One big chorus. Then silence.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.052
cast.text: The forest floor is covered in acorns that never sprout. Every world, new acorns. Same spots. Like the forest is waiting for permission to grow.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.053
cast.text: I found a trail of pebbles through the woods once, each one a little bigger than the last. It led to a stream. And in the stream, a very large pebble. Humming.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.054
cast.text: The bark on the old pine has lines on it, like writing. I've traced them with my fingers. They spell nothing I know. But they feel like a name.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.055
cast.text: The world's mercy smells like pine and rain and a fresh fire. It rolls through the forest, and every creature stops and sniffs the air.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.056
cast.text: There's a hollow tree in the forest you can climb inside. It's warm in there, and quiet. If you sit still, you can hear the forest thinking.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.057
cast.text: Some say the trees talk to each other through their roots. Slow conversations, one word per world. I wonder what they're saying. I wonder how far they've got.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.058
cast.text: The deer in the forest walk in circles around the old pine, every world. Slow, careful circles. Like they're guarding it.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.059
cast.text: I've walked every trail in this forest, and every trail has the same last tree. A birch with a heart carved in it. Two letters. Neither one mine.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.060
cast.text: The wind through the trees sounds like the sea. Close your eyes, and you'd think you're at the beach. Brine says the sea sounds like the forest. We laughed about that.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.061
cast.text: The crickets know a song that's older than the world. Every night, they sing a little more of it. One day they'll get to the end.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.062
cast.text: The forest goes on forever in one direction. North. Every other direction, you hit the edge. North, it just keeps going.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.063
cast.text: I once found a lost walker in the woods. She said she'd been walking for a hundred worlds. I gave her my map. It was the wrong map. She thanked me anyway.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.064
cast.text: Every ranger before me kept a journal. Mine has every rebuild in it. Every one starts with the same line. The crickets went quiet.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.065
cast.text: The mushrooms in the forest glow a little after a rebuild. Pale green. They light a path. If you follow it, you end up at a safe place. Every time.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.066
cast.text: I think the forest is the world's way of remembering what it was like before the labyrinths. Wild, and green, and free.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.067
cast.text: Rowan trees are said to keep away bad luck. I'm named after one. I hope it's working. For all of us.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.068
cast.text: The forest is never silent. Even between worlds. There's always a cricket, somewhere, keeping the song going.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.069
cast.text: I asked a hedgehog why the world keeps changing. He rolled into a ball. Fair enough. Sometimes, that's the right answer.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.070
cast.text: The walkers who come through here always find their way out. The forest makes sure of it. It doesn't want anyone lost for long.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.071
cast.text: The fallen leaves in the forest make the same pattern every world. I've studied it. It's a map. I just don't know of where.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.072
cast.text: Some old rangers say the Builder sleeps in the forest between worlds, under the old pine. Resting before the next one.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.073
cast.text: I've slept under the old pine. I didn't see anyone. But the next morning, my blanket was tucked in. And there was a leaf on my pillow.

cast.name: vc_ranger.story.074
cast.text: Every night, a new star appears over the forest. Just one. Every world, one more. Like someone is lighting candles in the sky, one at a time.

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Follow the buzzing!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.002
cast.text: Hello, explorer! This way, through the vines!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Mind the hanging branches!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.004
cast.text: This way! I've cleared a path for you!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.005
cast.text: Hey there! By the big fern, over here!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Don't worry about the cicadas, they're just loud!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.007
cast.text: This way, walker! Adventure awaits! Well, I await.

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! Come and see what I found!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.009
cast.text: Hello! Just follow my voice through the jungle!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.010
cast.text: This way! Watch your step, there are roots everywhere!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I found something for you on the trail!

cast.name: vc_explorer.greet.012
cast.text: Hi! Come on in, it's warm and wild in here!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.001
cast.text: Hey, explorer! Come back! You forgot your gift!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Through the vines!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.003
cast.text: This way! Follow the buzzing!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.004
cast.text: Come back, explorer! It's still here!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.005
cast.text: Over here! I've marked the trail for you!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.006
cast.text: Back this way! Mind the roots!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.007
cast.text: Hey, walker! Don't leave without it!

cast.name: vc_explorer.call.008
cast.text: This way again! By the big fern!

cast.name: vc_explorer.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go! A real jungle treasure!

cast.name: vc_explorer.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! Every explorer needs supplies!

cast.name: vc_explorer.gift.003
cast.text: For you! Found it under a giant leaf!

cast.name: vc_explorer.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the jungle! Go explore!

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.001
cast.text: I'm Ivy! Explorer, map maker, and finder of things that don't want to be found.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.002
cast.text: Hear the cicadas? They're the loudest bugs in any world. I love them.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.003
cast.text: I've got a compass, a notebook, and three snacks. Every good expedition starts with snacks.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.004
cast.text: The jungle is never quiet. Not for a second. It's the best place to think.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.005
cast.text: Watch out for the parrot. He repeats everything. Especially secrets.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.006
cast.text: Every leaf in this jungle is bigger than my head. Some of them are bigger than my tent.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.007
cast.text: I've mapped this jungle a hundred times. The map is never right. That's what I love about it.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.008
cast.text: It's hot, it's sticky, and it's wonderful. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.009
cast.text: I named a river after myself once. Next world, it was gone. Rivers are like that here.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.010
cast.text: Explorers never get lost. We just discover new places to be.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.011
cast.text: The jungle rearranges itself every world. Every vine, every tree. But the cicadas always sing from the same direction. Toward the middle of the world.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Shuffle. Like a deck of cards. Same cards, new order. And I've been trying to work out who's dealing.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.013
cast.text: I've been on a hundred expeditions to find the edge of the world. I've found the edge of the jungle, the edge of the map, and the edge of my patience. Never the edge of the world.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.014
cast.text: The cicadas buzz louder and louder right before the countdown. Then they stop. Five seconds of total silence. You could hear a leaf fall.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.015
cast.text: There's a temple deep in the jungle, overgrown and very old. Every world, it's in a different spot. But inside, it's always the same. One room, one door, one question carved on the wall. I can't read it. The letters are worn away. But it ends with a question mark. Of course it does.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.016
cast.text: The old maps in the temple show a world with no labyrinths. Just jungle, as far as you could walk. Then something changed, and nobody wrote down what.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.017
cast.text: Some explorers say the labyrinths were built to keep something in. Others say to keep something out. I think they were built to keep us busy.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.018
cast.text: Hazel thinks the world is a spell. Mortimer thinks it's a garden. I think it's an expedition. The world is exploring itself, and we're along for the ride.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.019
cast.text: I've found footprints in the jungle mud that go in circles. Big, slow, careful footprints. Somebody's looking for something. Maybe the same thing as me.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.020
cast.text: The parrot in the big tree once said a word I'd never heard before. He said it right before the countdown. I wrote it down. I still can't pronounce it.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.021
cast.text: Cicadas live underground for years before they come out to sing. Maybe the world is like that. Hiding underground, waiting for its turn to sing.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.022
cast.text: Every expedition I go on, I come back to the same clearing. No matter which way I walk. It's like the jungle wants me here, specifically.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.023
cast.text: The enemies never come into the jungle. Too many vines, I think. They'd get all tangled up.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.024
cast.text: I asked the cicadas why the world keeps changing. They buzzed so loudly, I couldn't hear myself think. Which might have been the point.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.025
cast.text: The world's mercy is like finding a shady spot in the heat. Sudden, cool, and you don't know where it came from. But you're very grateful.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.026
cast.text: There's a rumor among explorers that if you walk in a straight line long enough, you'll walk right out of the world. Nobody has ever walked straight long enough. The world won't let you.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.027
cast.text: Every world, I find a new plant I've never seen before. I name each one. I've got hundreds of names now. Ivy's Wonder, Ivy's Surprise, Ivy's Oops.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.028
cast.text: The jungle grows back so fast, you can almost hear it. That's what the rebuild sounds like to me. Growing, really fast, all at once.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.029
cast.text: There's a waterfall deep in the jungle that falls upward. Okay, I haven't seen it. But three different explorers told me about it. That's basically proof.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.030
cast.text: The vines all twist the same direction. Clockwise. Every vine, every world. Pendle says that means something. He wouldn't say what.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.031
cast.text: Sol the wanderer says the desert has no end. Well, the jungle has no beginning. I've looked. You just keep finding more jungle.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.032
cast.text: I found a compass in the temple that points to the nearest safe place. Just like yours! Someone built the first compass to help walkers find safety. Someone who cared. I'd love to say thank you, if I ever find them.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.033
cast.text: There's a tree in the jungle so tall, nobody's ever climbed to the top. I tried. I got halfway, and the world rebuilt. Now it's in a different spot. Typical.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.034
cast.text: The frogs in the jungle are louder than the marsh frogs. Fennick doesn't believe me. I'll prove it one day. If the worlds hold still long enough.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.035
cast.text: I've been keeping an expedition journal for a thousand worlds. Every entry ends with, more questions. I should really change it up.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.036
cast.text: The cicadas sing in waves, louder and softer, louder and softer. Like the world is breathing. In through the trees, out through the leaves.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.037
cast.text: Deep in the jungle there's a stone with a handprint on it. Small, smooth, worn by touching. Every walker who finds it puts their hand on it. I did. It was warm.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.038
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds because it's curious. It wants to see what happens if things are arranged differently. Like a scientist. A very messy scientist.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.039
cast.text: The monkeys in the jungle chatter about something every night. If I could understand them, I bet I'd know everything. They seem very well informed.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.040
cast.text: Some explorers believe the Builder left a map behind, hidden in the jungle. The map to everything. I've been searching for it for many worlds. I'll find it. Probably.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.041
cast.text: The heat in the jungle gets stronger right before a rebuild. Like the world is warming up for something. Stretching, before a run.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.042
cast.text: I found a tent in the jungle once, left behind by another explorer. Inside was a notebook. The last page said, I think I've worked it out. The rest was blank.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.043
cast.text: Every world, the cicadas sing one note higher. Just one. One day they'll be too high to hear. I wonder what happens then.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.044
cast.text: The jungle is full of hidden things. Temples, caves, old bridges. Things from older worlds that got left behind. Like the world forgot to tidy up.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.045
cast.text: Some explorers say the jungle is the world's dream. Wild and tangled and full of surprises. When the world wakes, the jungle fades. When it sleeps, it grows.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.046
cast.text: Mother Hazel gave me a potion once that let me understand the parrot for one world. He just complained about the weather. The whole time. Waste of a potion.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.047
cast.text: Ivy grows everywhere, they say. On walls, on trees, on old ruins. Maybe I'm named after it. Maybe the jungle named me. I'm not sure anymore.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.048
cast.text: I've always believed in one thing. If you keep exploring, you'll find something. Maybe not the answer. But something. That's good enough for me.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.049
cast.text: Always pack a spare rope. And a spare snack. And a spare spare snack.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.050
cast.text: I tried to befriend a monkey once. He stole my hat. We're still friends. He still has my hat.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.051
cast.text: Every explorer needs a motto. Mine is, what's over there? It's gotten me into a lot of trouble.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.052
cast.text: The jungle path always leads somewhere new, every world. But every path, if you follow it long enough, leads back to the temple.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.053
cast.text: I found a carving on a tree trunk. An arrow, pointing to the middle of the world. And under it, very small, the words, not yet.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.054
cast.text: The cicadas come up from underground every world. Millions of them. I think they're digging up from somewhere very deep. Somewhere old.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.055
cast.text: The jungle floor is warm, even at night. Something under there is breathing. Slow and steady. I think the whole world has a heartbeat.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.056
cast.text: There's a stone bridge in the jungle that crosses nothing. No river, no gap. Just a bridge, in the middle of the trees. Who built a bridge to nowhere?

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.057
cast.text: Every expedition journal I find in the jungle ends the same way. With a drawing of a door. Everyone who comes here draws that door. Including me.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.058
cast.text: The world's mercy sounds like the jungle going quiet, and a single bird singing. Just for a moment. Then everything starts buzzing again.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.059
cast.text: The orchids bloom only right after a rebuild. They open all at once, like they've been waiting for the new world. Beautiful, and gone so fast.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.060
cast.text: I've found ruins of other explorers' camps. Some of them are from worlds that are long gone. Same tent, same pot, same notebook. Same questions.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.061
cast.text: Maybe the world is an expedition. And we're all explorers. And the map is never finished, because the world keeps drawing new edges.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.062
cast.text: I asked a tortoise in the jungle why the world keeps changing. He was very slow to answer. The world rebuilt before he opened his mouth.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.063
cast.text: The jungle has a smell just before the countdown. Like rain about to fall. Fresh and green and a little electric.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.064
cast.text: There's a cave in the jungle with paintings on the walls. Paintings of walkers, walking. Every world, there's one more walker in the paintings.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.065
cast.text: Some explorers think the answer is in the jungle, because it's the wildest place. Wild places keep secrets better.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.066
cast.text: The vines are always a little longer every world. Reaching. Toward the middle of the world. Everything here reaches for the middle, eventually.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.067
cast.text: I keep a compass, a map, and a list of questions. The list is the longest thing I own. It gets longer every world. I love it.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.068
cast.text: The temple bell rings once every world, by itself. Deep and low. The jungle goes quiet to listen. Then the cicadas start up again, louder than ever.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.069
cast.text: I found a hammock strung between two trees, deep in the jungle. Still swinging. Nobody in it. Somebody was just here, resting. Somebody always seems to be just here.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.070
cast.text: The rain in the jungle falls warm. Right before a rebuild, it falls upward. Just for a second. I've felt it on my chin.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.071
cast.text: The parrot says one word every world. Last world it was, door. This world it was, open. I'm waiting to hear what comes next.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.072
cast.text: The deeper into the jungle you go, the older the trees get. At the very middle, there's said to be a tree as old as the world. I'm still looking.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.073
cast.text: Every explorer leaves a mark on the trail, so the next one can follow. The oldest mark in the jungle isn't a word. It's a little drawing of an ear.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.074
cast.text: Somebody wants us to listen. That's what I've decided. Everything in this world, every clue, every rumor, says the same thing. Listen.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.075
cast.text: The fireflies in the jungle blink in patterns, right before the countdown. I think they're passing a message along. From one end of the world to the other.

cast.name: vc_explorer.story.076
cast.text: I asked Mother Hazel what's at the middle of the jungle. She said, the middle of the world. I asked what's at the middle of the world. She said, the middle of the jungle.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Follow the birdsong!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.002
cast.text: Hello! This way, by the hedge!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Shh, quietly, the robins are nesting.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.004
cast.text: Good morning! It's always morning here! This way!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.005
cast.text: Hi! Come and listen to the birds with me!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.006
cast.text: Over here, by the blossom tree!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.007
cast.text: This way! Tweet tweet! That's me, not a bird.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.008
cast.text: Hello, walker! Over here!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.009
cast.text: Over here! Mind the nest on the gate!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.010
cast.text: This way! Follow the blackbird, then follow me!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've got something lovely for you!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.greet.012
cast.text: Hello hello! By the bird bath!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.001
cast.text: Hello! Come back! You've forgotten your present!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Follow the birdsong!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.003
cast.text: This way! It's still here, I promise!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.004
cast.text: Come back! The robins are guarding it!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.005
cast.text: Over here, walker! By the blossom tree!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.006
cast.text: Back this way! Quietly, don't scare the birds!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.007
cast.text: Wait! Come back! It's for you!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.call.008
cast.text: This way again! Tweet tweet!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are! A present from the garden!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! A little bird left it for you. Well, I did.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.gift.003
cast.text: For you! Isn't it lovely?

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.gift.004
cast.text: A gift, with love from Wren and the robins!

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.001
cast.text: I'm Wren! I watch birds. And listen to them. Mostly listen.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.002
cast.text: That's a blackbird. That one's a thrush. And that one's a robin, and he's showing off.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.003
cast.text: It's always morning here. The best time for birds. And for breakfast.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.004
cast.text: I've got a little book of birdsong. I write down every new one I hear.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.005
cast.text: The blossom smells lovely today. It smells lovely every day, actually.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.006
cast.text: Birds are the cleverest creatures. Don't tell the frogs I said so.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.007
cast.text: I made a bird bath out of an old bowl. The sparrows love it. They splash everywhere.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.008
cast.text: Do you hear the woodpecker? Tap tap tap. He never stops. I think he's building something.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.009
cast.text: My favourite bird is the wren. Obviously. Tiny, but very loud.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.010
cast.text: Spring always feels like a new beginning. Here, it's always spring. So it's always a new beginning.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.011
cast.text: The birds fly between worlds, I'm sure of it. I've heard the same blackbird sing in two different worlds. Same song, same little wobble at the end.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Flight. Everything takes off, all at once, and lands somewhere new.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.013
cast.text: The birds all go quiet just before the countdown. Every single one. Then, the moment the new world arrives, they sing the loudest dawn chorus you've ever heard.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.014
cast.text: The birds know the answer, I think. They sing it every morning. They just sing it too fast for us to catch.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.015
cast.text: There's a bird I've only heard once. Right before a rebuild. A long, sweet, falling song. I've never found it in any book.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.016
cast.text: Every world, the birds build their nests in exactly the same places. Even when the trees are different. As if they have a map we don't.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.017
cast.text: The swallows fly in circles before a rebuild. Big, wide circles. Round and round the middle of the world. Then they're gone.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.018
cast.text: Old Hollis says there's a land where it's always morning, beyond the labyrinths. He thinks I've been there. I haven't. But the birds have, I'm sure.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.019
cast.text: I put out crumbs every world, and every world, the same robin comes. He knows me. I think he remembers every world. Lucky robin.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.020
cast.text: Some people say the world rebuilds because it's spring cleaning. Clearing out the old, making room for the new. I quite like that idea.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.021
cast.text: The cuckoo calls five times before every countdown. Cuckoo, cuckoo, cuckoo, cuckoo, cuckoo. I asked Pendle if his clocks do that. He looked very worried.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.022
cast.text: I found a feather once that wasn't from any bird I know. Silver and light, and it hums when you hold it. Hazel wanted to buy it. I said no.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.023
cast.text: The birds migrate somewhere, every so often. They all fly away together. They're always back by the next world. Where do they go in between?

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.024
cast.text: When the world shows mercy, the birds burst into song. All at once. Like they're cheering. Then they settle down, very pleased with themselves.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.025
cast.text: The enemies don't bother the birds, and the birds don't bother the enemies. I think they've got an agreement. I'd love to know what it says.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.026
cast.text: The eggs in the nests never hatch. Every world, they're new eggs. Same colour, same speckles. The world keeps starting the spring over.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.027
cast.text: I think one day the eggs will hatch, and that's when the world will stop rebuilding. Or start doing something new. Either would be exciting.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.028
cast.text: The owls in Rowan's forest and the birds in my garden have never met. But they sing the same notes, just at different times of day.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.029
cast.text: The dawn chorus has a pattern. Every bird takes a turn, and there's always one gap. One bird that's missing.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.030
cast.text: I've been trying to work out which bird is missing from the dawn chorus. I think it might be the one that knows the answer.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.031
cast.text: The blossom falls before every rebuild. Just a few petals. They float down, slowly, like snow. Then the world changes, and the tree is full again.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.032
cast.text: The magpies collect shiny things. Every world, I find their stash. Credits, buttons, a little silver key. They always have a little silver key.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.033
cast.text: Wren is such a small name for such a big mystery, isn't it? I sometimes think I'm too small to work it all out. But wrens are very clever.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.034
cast.text: The woodpecker taps in rhythm. Tap, tap, tap, tap, tap, pause. I've counted it in every world. It's always five, before the pause.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.035
cast.text: I once whistled a tune back to the blackbird. He sang it back to me, changed a little. I sang it back changed again. We did that till the world rebuilt. In the next world, the blackbird was still singing our tune. Birds remember. I'm sure of it.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.036
cast.text: Some say the birds were here before the first world. They were singing in the dark, and the world grew up around the song.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.037
cast.text: Clover the beekeeper says bees always find their way home, even after a rebuild. Birds do too. Maybe home is something that doesn't change.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.038
cast.text: I've heard a bird that sings in a voice like someone counting. One, two, three. Really. Fennick thinks I'm making it up. I'm not.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.039
cast.text: The sparrows chatter about everything, all day. I think they're gossiping about the walkers. They definitely talk about you.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.040
cast.text: A bird landed on my shoulder once, right before the countdown. It sang one note in my ear. Very quietly. I still don't know what it meant.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.041
cast.text: Every spring needs a reason, my mum says. The world must have a reason too. It can't just be spring forever for nothing.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.042
cast.text: I keep a list of every bird that visits. The list is different every world, but the first name is always the same. Robin. Always Robin.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.043
cast.text: The nests are woven with bits of things from old worlds. Ribbon, string, a strip of paper. I found a nest with a word written in it. Almost.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.044
cast.text: Swallows fly south, geese fly in a V, and starlings fly all together in a great big swirl. Right before the rebuild, they all fly toward the middle of the world.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.045
cast.text: I wonder if the birds can see the Builder. They fly so high. Maybe that's what they're singing about every morning. Good morning, Builder.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.046
cast.text: The morning sun is always just rising here. It never quite gets up. As if the world is waiting for something before the day can start.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.047
cast.text: Spring always smells of new grass and hope. I think the world rebuilds because it loves the smell of spring so much, it can't stop.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.048
cast.text: Every walker that visits, the robin sings a new verse. I think he's writing a song about all of you. It's a very long song by now.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.049
cast.text: Did you hear that? That's a chiffchaff. It says its own name. Chiff chaff, chiff chaff. Clever thing.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.050
cast.text: I've got a pair of binoculars. I can't use them, really. But they make me feel very official.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.051
cast.text: The ducks in the pond are very rude. They quack at everyone. Don't take it personally.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.052
cast.text: The robin's song has five notes at the end. Every world. Five little notes, falling. I think he learned them from the countdown.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.053
cast.text: I think the birds are keeping watch over the world. They see everything from up high. If anything's out of place, they'd be the first to know.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.054
cast.text: I left a little bird box out for the owl. Every world, there's a feather inside. A different feather. From a bird I've never heard.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.055
cast.text: The swallows always arrive right after a rebuild, all at once, out of nowhere. Swooping and chattering. Like they've just come back from a long trip.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.056
cast.text: Some people say birdsong is just birds saying, this is my tree. I think it's more than that. I think they're telling stories. About the old worlds.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.057
cast.text: There's a heron in the pond who stands perfectly still for a whole world. Then, just before the countdown, she takes one step. Just one. Toward the middle of the world. She'll get there one day.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.058
cast.text: The geese fly over in a V shape every world. But once, they made a different shape. A circle. Then a question mark. Then the world rebuilt.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.059
cast.text: I collect eggshells that the birds leave behind. Pale blue, speckled brown. Every shell is from a different world. I keep them in a little box.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.060
cast.text: The nightingale only sings in the quiet moment between worlds. I've heard it once. The loveliest song in any world. Then it was gone.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.061
cast.text: The birds always sound happiest right after a rebuild. Like they love new worlds. Like every rebuild is a lovely surprise for them.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.062
cast.text: The world's mercy makes the birds go completely still, for just a moment. Then they all sing the same note. Then it's over, and they carry on.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.063
cast.text: I've noticed the birds never sing the countdown. They go quiet. Like it's a moment that belongs to somebody else.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.064
cast.text: Petra says the drips count the world. Pendle says the clocks. I think the birds do. One song for every world. I'm trying to keep track.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.065
cast.text: There's a little bird that follows walkers. I've heard it. It hops along behind you, chirping. I think it wants to see where you're going.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.066
cast.text: The blossom tree in my garden is the oldest tree I know. Older than the old pine in Rowan's forest, I think. It doesn't say much. It just blooms.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.067
cast.text: Some birds fly in the dark, to places nobody's ever been. I think they've seen the edge of the world. They just don't talk about it.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.068
cast.text: The cuckoo lays her eggs in other birds' nests. Maybe the world does the same. Leaves little bits of itself in other worlds. Little surprises.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.069
cast.text: I asked the robin why the world keeps changing. He sang me a whole song. I didn't understand a word of it. But I felt a lot better.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.070
cast.text: Every world, there's a new song in the garden. Just one. I write it down. I've got hundreds now. Maybe they make one big song, all together.

cast.name: vc_birdwatcher.story.071
cast.text: The birds start building nests right after the countdown. They're never surprised. They just get straight to work. I really admire that.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, sugar! Follow the buzzing!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.002
cast.text: Hey there! This way, by the hives!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Don't worry, the bees are friendly!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.004
cast.text: Hi, sunshine! Come on over!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.005
cast.text: This way! Mind the flowers, the bees are working!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! It's warm and sweet over here!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.007
cast.text: Hello! Just follow the hum!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.008
cast.text: This way, walker! I've got honey and a gift!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.009
cast.text: Over here, by the clover patch!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.010
cast.text: Hey hey! Come and say hello to the girls! The bees, I mean!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! Bzz bzz! That's my bee impression!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.greet.012
cast.text: This way, sugar! Nice and slow!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.001
cast.text: Hey, sugar! Come back! You forgot your gift!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Follow the buzzing!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.003
cast.text: This way! It's sitting right here in the sunshine!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.004
cast.text: Come back! The bees are guarding it, very politely!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.005
cast.text: Over here, walker! Don't fly off yet!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.006
cast.text: Back this way, by the hives!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.007
cast.text: Hey! Come back! It's sweet, I promise!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.call.008
cast.text: This way again, sunshine!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go, sugar! Sweet as honey!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! The bees helped. Mostly they buzzed.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.gift.003
cast.text: For you, sunshine! Have a sweet day!

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the hive! Bee safe out there! Get it?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.001
cast.text: I'm Clover! I keep the bees. Well, the bees keep me, really. They're in charge.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.002
cast.text: Summer's the best, isn't it? Warm sun, buzzing bees, and honey on everything.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.003
cast.text: Don't swat at the bees, sugar. They're just curious. They think you might be a flower.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.004
cast.text: I've got six hives. Each one has a queen, and each queen has opinions.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.005
cast.text: Honey never spoils, you know. You could keep it for a thousand worlds.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.006
cast.text: The bees dance to tell each other where the flowers are. I've tried dancing for them. They were not impressed.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.007
cast.text: It's always summer here. I've never had to wear a coat. Not once.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.008
cast.text: Listen to that hum. That's the sound of a happy hive.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.009
cast.text: Lemonade? It's homemade. Well, hive made. The bees helped with the honey.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.010
cast.text: I talk to my bees every morning. They don't talk back. But they listen. You can tell.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.011
cast.text: Bees always find their way home. Even after a rebuild. The whole world changes, and still, every bee flies straight back to its hive. How do they know?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Swarm. Everything lifts up and buzzes around for a moment. Then it all settles down in a new place.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.013
cast.text: The bees go quiet right before the countdown. A hive full of bees, totally silent. It's the strangest sound in the world. The sound of nothing.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.014
cast.text: The queen bee has lived through every rebuild. Same queen, every world. I think she knows something. Queens usually do.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.015
cast.text: There's a rumor among beekeepers that the bees are building something. Every world, a little more. Something with six sides, as big as the world.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.016
cast.text: I opened a hive once and found a honeycomb shaped like a labyrinth. A perfect little maze. The bees made it. I didn't teach them that.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.017
cast.text: The bees dance a new dance every world. I've been writing them down. If I put all the dances together, they might spell something. They haven't yet.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.018
cast.text: The world's mercy tastes like honey. I'm sure of it. Sweet and slow and warm. And it always comes when you least expect it.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.019
cast.text: Summer never ends here. The sun is always high, the flowers always open. Like the world found its favorite day and keeps playing it over.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.020
cast.text: Hazel buys honey from me for her potions. She says it's the only thing that tastes the same in every world. I think that's important. I'm not sure why.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.021
cast.text: The flowers turn to follow the sun. But here, right before a rebuild, they all turn toward the middle of the world instead. Every flower, all at once.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.022
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds the way a hive grows. One cell at a time, always building, never done. Someone's busy as a bee out there.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.023
cast.text: Some beekeepers say the world is a great big flower, and we're all the bees, buzzing around in it. Taking a little sweetness and moving on.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.024
cast.text: The bees never sting the walkers. Not once. I've watched. They buzz around you, like they're checking you're okay. Then off they go.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.025
cast.text: The enemies don't like bees. They stay well away from the hives. Smart of them. My girls are very protective.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.026
cast.text: I found a beehive in the middle of nowhere once. No flowers anywhere near it. Just a hive, buzzing, full of honey. Who's looking after it?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.027
cast.text: Every world, there's one new flower in my garden I didn't plant. Always blue. Always the same blue. The bees love it more than anything.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.028
cast.text: Clover is a lucky plant, they say. Four leaves, if you're very lucky. I've only ever found three leaf clovers. Maybe the fourth leaf is the answer.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.029
cast.text: The summer heat shimmers in the air right before the countdown. Everything gets wobbly, like the world is a little bit melting. Then it's fresh again.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.030
cast.text: Wren says birds fly between worlds. Well, bees do too. I've seen my bees fly off right before a rebuild. They come back with pollen from flowers that don't grow here.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.031
cast.text: The hive hums one note, all day long. Ambrose came by and listened. He said it's the same note as the silent pipe in his organ. That gave us both a shiver.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.032
cast.text: I asked the queen bee why the world keeps changing. She just kept laying eggs. Busy, busy. I think she's saying, don't worry about it, just keep going.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.033
cast.text: Honey from different worlds tastes different. Clover honey one world, orange blossom the next. Once it tasted like rain. I still have a jar of that one.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.034
cast.text: There's a beekeeper's rhyme. Busy bee, busy bee, what are you building, what will it be? Nobody knows the next line. The bees might.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.035
cast.text: The grass is always warm here. Lie down in it, and you can feel the world humming underneath. Just like a hive. A great big hive.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.036
cast.text: Sometimes I think the whole world is a hive, and somewhere in the middle, there's a queen. And she's the one who decides when it all changes.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.037
cast.text: Some days I think the world has no queen at all. Just a lot of little busy things, all doing their bit, and the world just sort of happens.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.038
cast.text: The fireflies come out in the summer evenings, right before a rebuild. They blink in time, all together. Five blinks, then dark. Then a new world.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.039
cast.text: I keep honey in the cellar from the very first world I remember. I've never opened it. I'm saving it for when the world finally stops changing.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.040
cast.text: Some bees fly off and never come back. Not many. Just one or two, now and then. I like to think they found the edge of the world and liked it there.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.041
cast.text: Lemonade tastes the same in every world. That's my one constant. Some people have clocks, some have the sea. I have lemonade.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.042
cast.text: I heard a buzzing once that wasn't my bees. Deeper, slower. It came from underground. Like the world has a hive of its own, down there.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.043
cast.text: The summer stars come out every night, but they're never in the same place. Commander Vega says the stars move too. Everything moves. Except honey. Honey stays put.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.044
cast.text: Old beekeepers say you should always tell the bees your news. So I told them about the rebuilding. They buzzed for a whole world. I think they were discussing it.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.045
cast.text: I think the bees have the answer, sugar. They're just too polite to tell us before we're ready.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.046
cast.text: The sun here never sets, but it never quite gets to noon, either. It's always mid morning, in midsummer. Like a long, sweet moment the world won't let go of.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.047
cast.text: Every hive has a guard bee at the door. Mine all face outward, toward the middle of the world. What are they guarding against? Or what are they waiting for?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.048
cast.text: Some walkers say the world is mean, with all those enemies. But look around. There's honey, and sunshine, and flowers. The world's got a sweet side too.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.049
cast.text: Want some honey? Just a spoonful. It makes everything a little better.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.050
cast.text: My beekeeping hat has a hole in it. The bees think it's a door. They visit my hair a lot.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.051
cast.text: I named the biggest hive Bumble Hall. It's very grand. Lots of comings and goings.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.052
cast.text: The bees always come home just before the countdown. Every bee, safely inside. Then the world changes, and they all fly out again. Like they know.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.053
cast.text: The honeycomb gets one more cell every world, even when the bees are resting. Something adds to it. Something very small and very careful.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.054
cast.text: I found a bee made of gold once, sitting on a flower. It wasn't real. It was a tiny statue. Next world, it was gone, and the flower had a bite out of it.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.055
cast.text: The clover in my field always has three leaves. Except one patch, near the hives, where every clover has five. Five leaves. I've never seen that anywhere else.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.056
cast.text: There's a rumor among beekeepers that the bees keep a map of every world, in the shape of their dances. If you could read all the dances, you'd know the way.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.057
cast.text: The summer wind smells of flowers that don't grow here. Wild roses, mint, something sweet and new. I think it blows in from the next world.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.058
cast.text: I asked the bees to show me the middle of the world. They danced for a whole world. I followed the dance. It led me back to my own front door.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.059
cast.text: The world's mercy is like a bee landing on your hand and not stinging. A little moment of trust. The world saying, I see you. You're alright.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.060
cast.text: Hazel says honey is the only thing that tastes the same in every world. I tried an experiment. She's right. Even honey from different flowers tastes the same.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.061
cast.text: Somebody leaves a tiny jar on my doorstep every world. Empty. Clean. Like they're asking for honey. I always fill it. It's always gone by the next world.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.062
cast.text: The bees make a hum that matches the world's hum. Ambrose says it's the same note. Petra says it's the same as the drips. Everybody's humming along.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.063
cast.text: There's an old hive at the edge of my field. Empty. No bees have lived in it for a thousand worlds. But sometimes I hear humming inside.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.064
cast.text: The bees build their combs in perfect six sided cells. The labyrinths out there have walls with corners just like that. I've felt them. Who copied who?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.065
cast.text: Some say the world rebuilds the way a garden blooms. Every few minutes, a new flower opens. And every flower is a whole new world.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.066
cast.text: I think the queen bee and the Builder would get on very well. Both busy. Both in charge. Both very hard to get an appointment with.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.067
cast.text: I've noticed that the bees buzz a little faster when a walker is near. Like they're excited. They don't do that for the rest of us.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.068
cast.text: The sunflowers in my garden are taller than me, every world. Every world, they're a little taller. One day they'll reach the sky. Then what?

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.069
cast.text: The sweetest thing about the world, sugar, is that it keeps trying. Every rebuild is a new try. I find that very hopeful.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.070
cast.text: The hive goes quiet when the world shows mercy. Every bee stops. Then they all start buzzing again, at once, a little happier.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.071
cast.text: Sometimes I think honey is what the world tastes like, if it could taste. Golden and warm and very old.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.072
cast.text: The bees never leave a flower half visited. They always finish. I wish the world would finish things like that. Just once.

cast.name: vc_beekeeper.story.073
cast.text: I bet the answer to the whole mystery is very simple, sugar. Like, the world is just busy. Busy, busy, busy. Like a bee.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, traveler. Follow the wind.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.002
cast.text: Hey. This way, out of the sun.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.003
cast.text: Over here, friend. Under the shade.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.004
cast.text: This way. The sand is soft, take your time.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.005
cast.text: Hello, traveler. I'm by the old tree.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.006
cast.text: Over here. Listen for the wind chimes.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.007
cast.text: This way, walker. Long road? Come rest.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.008
cast.text: Over here, friend. Water and a gift, both free.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.009
cast.text: Hey there. Follow my voice. The wind will carry it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.010
cast.text: This way. I've been waiting a while. I'm good at waiting.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.011
cast.text: Over here, traveler. Mind the dunes.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.greet.012
cast.text: Hello. Come sit, the wind's cool here.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.001
cast.text: Traveler. Come back. Your gift's still here.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.002
cast.text: Over here again. Follow the wind.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.003
cast.text: This way, friend. The sand won't mind.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.004
cast.text: Come on back. I saved it for you.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.005
cast.text: Over here. Under the shade.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.006
cast.text: Hey, walker. You left something. This way.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.007
cast.text: Back this way, traveler. Easy does it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.call.008
cast.text: Come back. The wind's been keeping it safe.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.gift.001
cast.text: Here. A gift from the road.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, friend. Travel well.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.gift.003
cast.text: For you, traveler. The wind told me you'd need it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.gift.004
cast.text: Here you go. May the road be kind to you.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.001
cast.text: I'm Sol. I wander. I've walked further than anyone, and I'm still walking.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.002
cast.text: Hear the wind in the trees? It's been telling me stories since before the first world.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.003
cast.text: Desert's hot by day, cold by night. Here, it's always somewhere in between.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.004
cast.text: Sit down, friend. Drink some water. The world will still be strange when you're done.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.005
cast.text: I've worn out more boots than I can count. Every world, a new pair is waiting by my tent.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.006
cast.text: The wind chimes on my tent were a gift. I don't remember who gave them to me.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.007
cast.text: Sand gets everywhere. Into boots, into pockets, into thoughts.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.008
cast.text: A wanderer doesn't need a map. Just good ears and a patient heart.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.009
cast.text: The trees bend in the wind, but they don't break. That's the trick of it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.010
cast.text: I like the quiet out here. Even the wind is quiet, when it's thinking.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.011
cast.text: I've walked to the edge of the world more times than I can count. There's no edge, traveler. Just more sand. And then, suddenly, a new world.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.012
cast.text: The desert has no end. I've walked straight for a whole world. When the rebuild came, I was right back here, under this tree.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.013
cast.text: The wind always blows from the middle of the world. Every world. I've walked into it, toward the middle. I never get there. The middle keeps moving.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.014
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Shifting Sands. The dunes move, the world moves, and when it settles, there's a new path to walk.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.015
cast.text: The wind carries voices from old worlds. I've heard them. Not words exactly. More like the feeling of words. Somebody saying goodbye. Somebody saying hello.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.016
