cast.text: There's an old tree out in the desert. Alone, miles from anything. Every world, it's there. I sit under it and listen. It hums.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.017
cast.text: The sand sings sometimes. Big low notes, when the dunes slide. Ambrose says it's the same note as his organ. Everything sings the same note here.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.018
cast.text: I've seen footprints in the sand that lead out into the desert and stop. Just stop, in the middle of nowhere. As if someone stepped off the world.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.019
cast.text: The wind picks up right before the countdown. A great rush through the trees. Five gusts. Then stillness. Then the new world.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.020
cast.text: Some wanderers say the world rebuilds because it's restless. Like me. It can't stay in one shape. It has to keep moving.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.021
cast.text: I've met other wanderers. They all say the same thing. They're looking for something. None of them can say what. Neither can I.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.022
cast.text: The world's mercy is like a cool breeze in the desert. You don't know where it came from. You don't know when it'll come again. But you're grateful.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.023
cast.text: Hazel says the world is a spell. Pendle says a clock. Me? I think the world is a road. And roads don't end. They just go somewhere else.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.024
cast.text: There's a ruin in the desert. Old stones in a circle. In the middle, a stone with a hole through it. If you whisper into the hole, the wind whispers back.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.025
cast.text: I whispered a question into the stone in the desert ruin. Why does the world change? The wind whispered back, why do you? I've been walking ever since, trying to work out what it meant.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.026
cast.text: The stars over the desert are bright and close. Commander Vega says she's been up there. She says the world looks small from above. Smaller than you'd think.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.027
cast.text: I found a well in the desert. Deep, cool, full of water. Every world, it's in a different place. But I always find it. Like it wants to be found.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.028
cast.text: The enemies never come out into the open desert. Too much sky, maybe. Or maybe they don't like the wind. The wind doesn't like them either.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.029
cast.text: Every grain of sand was once a rock. Every rock was once a mountain. Maybe every world was once something else, too. Something big.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.030
cast.text: Some say the desert is where old worlds go to rest. Worn down to sand. That would mean this sand is made of a thousand worlds. Feels right, somehow.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.031
cast.text: The trees whisper a word in the wind just before a rebuild. I've heard it a hundred times. I think it's, again. Or maybe, begin.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.032
cast.text: A traveler once told me the world is a circle. Walk far enough in any direction, and you'll end up where you started. I've done it. He was right. But why a circle?

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.033
cast.text: The wind chimes ring a little tune before every rebuild. Five notes. Wren says the birds sing the same five notes. Petra says the drips do too. Everything knows that tune.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.034
cast.text: I keep a stone from every world I walk through. A little pebble in my pocket. My pockets are very heavy. But each stone is different. Each one's a memory.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.035
cast.text: The sun never quite sets out here. It hangs low on the edge of the world, like it's waiting to see what happens next.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.036
cast.text: I met someone on the road once. Tall, quiet, carrying a big bag of tools. We walked together for a while. Then the countdown came, and they nodded and were gone. Was that the Builder? They didn't seem worried. Just busy, like someone with a lot of work to do.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.037
cast.text: The world is like the wind, traveler. You can't see it. You can't hold it. You can only feel where it's going.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.038
cast.text: I think the world changes because nobody's supposed to know it too well. Know a place too well, and you stop listening to it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.039
cast.text: There's a mirage in the desert I've chased for a hundred worlds. A city, shimmering, with a tall tower in the middle. I never reach it. It's always just a little further.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.040
cast.text: The trees out here grow sideways, bent by the wind. They all point the same way. Away from the middle of the world. Like they're trying to get away from something. Or point you toward something.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.041
cast.text: Some old wanderers say the first walker is still walking. Somewhere out in the desert. Still looking for the answer. Still listening.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.042
cast.text: I've walked so many worlds, I've forgotten where I started. Maybe I started here. Maybe everyone starts here, and forgets.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.043
cast.text: Sand blows into the safe places, but it never piles up. Somebody sweeps it out. Every world. I've never seen who.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.044
cast.text: The desert is the quietest place I know. In that quiet, you can hear the world thinking. It thinks slowly. Like sand pouring through a glass.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.045
cast.text: Pendle says time is a clock. I say time is an hourglass. When the sand runs out, someone turns it over. That's the rebuild. Same sand, falling again.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.046
cast.text: I'd love to meet whoever turns the hourglass. Just to ask them one question. Not why. I'd ask them, are you tired?

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.047
cast.text: Every road I've ever walked ends at a safe place. Every one. As if the world wants you to rest before you go on.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.048
cast.text: The wind is the world breathing. In, out. Slow. When it holds its breath, that's when you know the rebuild is coming.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.049
cast.text: Maybe there's no answer, traveler. Maybe the walking is the answer. Then again, a wanderer would say that.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.050
cast.text: I've got a flute I play when the wind's quiet. Only know three songs. The wind knows hundreds.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.051
cast.text: My tent has seen a lot of worlds. A few holes. A lot of stories. Like me.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.052
cast.text: Shade's precious out here. Share it with anyone who needs it. That's the rule of the road.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.053
cast.text: Every desert road I walk ends with an oasis. A small pool, a few palms, a little shade. Somebody plants them. Somebody who knows walkers get thirsty.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.054
cast.text: The dunes sing when the countdown starts. A deep, rumbling hum. The whole desert joins in. Then the new world, and the dunes are silent.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.055
cast.text: I've seen a tower in the desert, far off. Tall and thin. Every world, it's a little closer. I've never reached it. But I'm getting closer.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.056
cast.text: Some nights, the sand glows. Faint silver, where it's been stepped on. Old footprints, from old worlds, lighting up for a moment.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.057
cast.text: The wind in the trees speaks in whispers. The wind in the desert speaks in shouts. But they're both saying the same thing. Keep going.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.058
cast.text: The world's mercy, out here, is a cloud. One small cloud, passing over, giving shade. Then it's gone. But you remember it.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.059
cast.text: I asked an old lizard in the desert why the world keeps changing. He blinked at me, very slowly. I think lizards have known for a long time. They just don't care.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.060
cast.text: There's a rumor among wanderers that the edge of the world is just a mirror. You walk to it, and you see yourself walking back.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.061
cast.text: The trees lean, the sand shifts, the wind turns. Everything here moves. The only thing that stays is the question. Why?

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.062
cast.text: I once walked so far that I heard the world rebuild behind me before it caught up to me. Like a wave. It rolled past, and then I was somewhere new.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.063
cast.text: Every traveler I meet has a stone in their pocket from the first world they remember. Mine is smooth and grey. It's warm sometimes. Like it remembers too.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.064
cast.text: The desert stars are the brightest in the world. Commander Vega says she can see my campfire from up there. I wave, just in case.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.065
cast.text: Somebody leaves a full water skin under the old tree every world. I've never seen them. But the water is always cold and fresh.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.066
cast.text: I think the wanderers and the Builder are alike. Always moving. Always looking. Never quite finding it. Never quite stopping.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.067
cast.text: The wind chimes on my tent were made from pieces of old worlds. A spoon, a key, a bell, a button, a bit of glass. Five pieces. Five notes.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.068
cast.text: The sand covers everything eventually. Old walls, old paths, old worlds. But dig down, and they're still there. Every world is still there, under the sand.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.069
cast.text: Hazel once told me the world is looking for something it lost. I've been looking for things too, my whole life. Maybe the world and I are looking for the same thing.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.070
cast.text: The trees whisper louder when a walker is near. Like they're passing the news along. A walker's here. A walker's listening.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.071
cast.text: The road goes on, traveler. That's what I've learned. It always goes on. And every new bend has something you've never heard before.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.072
cast.text: There's a well in the desert that echoes your voice back five seconds late. Pendle would love it. I've told him. He said he'd come in the next world. He never does.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.073
cast.text: The wind is always at my back when I walk toward a safe place. Pushing me along. Like it wants me to rest. Like it cares.

cast.name: vc_wanderer.story.074
cast.text: Every world, I pick a direction and walk. Every world, I end up somewhere I've never been, but somehow, I always end up here, under this tree.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, little traveller. Follow the chill.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.002
cast.text: Hello. This way, through the snow.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.003
cast.text: Over here. Mind the ice, it's very smooth.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.004
cast.text: This way, my dear. Don't be afraid of the cold.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.005
cast.text: Over here. I'm by the frozen pool.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.006
cast.text: Come in, out of the blizzard. This way.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.007
cast.text: Hello, walker. Follow my voice. It carries well on the ice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.008
cast.text: Over here, my dear. I've something cool for you.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.009
cast.text: This way. Gently, gently, on the ice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.010
cast.text: Over here. The snow will guide you.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.011
cast.text: Hello. Come closer. I'm colder than I sound.

cast.name: vc_icelady.greet.012
cast.text: This way, little traveller. Into the ice cave.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.001
cast.text: Little traveller, come back. Your gift is waiting.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.002
cast.text: Over here again, my dear. Through the snow.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.003
cast.text: This way. Mind the ice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.004
cast.text: Come back. I've kept it frozen, safe and sound.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.005
cast.text: Over here. Don't wander off into the blizzard.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.006
cast.text: Back this way, walker. Follow the chill.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.007
cast.text: My dear, you've left something behind. Over here.

cast.name: vc_icelady.call.008
cast.text: This way again, to the frozen pool.

cast.name: vc_icelady.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are, my dear. Fresh from the ice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.gift.002
cast.text: Take this. Don't worry, it's warmed up a little.

cast.name: vc_icelady.gift.003
cast.text: For you, little traveller. Kept cold, kept safe.

cast.name: vc_icelady.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the ice. Stay warm out there.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.001
cast.text: I am Lady Rime. I live in the ice. It's quieter than you'd think.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.002
cast.text: Don't shiver, my dear. The cold is only unkind if you fight it.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.003
cast.text: Every snowflake is different. I've checked. All of them.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.004
cast.text: The blizzard sounds fierce, but it's mostly bluster. Like an old uncle.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.005
cast.text: I've lived in this cave since the first snow fell. It's my home. It's very cosy, in its way.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.006
cast.text: Ice is wonderful. It keeps everything just as it was. Nothing spoils. Nothing changes.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.007
cast.text: Listen to the ice creak. It's just settling. Like an old house.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.008
cast.text: I don't feel the cold. I'm not sure I ever did.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.009
cast.text: The icicles here ring like bells if you tap them. Gently, please.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.010
cast.text: Snow makes everything quiet. That's why I love it. The world finally stops talking.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.011
cast.text: Ice keeps things, my dear. Pieces of old worlds, frozen in the walls of my cave. A leaf, a feather, a coin. Things the rebuild couldn't take.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.012
cast.text: I've found something frozen deep in the ice that hums. I can't reach it. I can only listen. It hums the same tune the whole world seems to know.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.013
cast.text: They say the great clock that runs the world is under the ice. I've neither confirmed nor denied it. A lady never tells.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.014
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Thaw. Everything melts, and runs, and freezes again into a new shape. Like ice in spring.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.015
cast.text: Every snowflake is different, and every world is different. I've often wondered if they're made by the same hand.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.016
cast.text: The blizzard grows fiercer just before the countdown. Then it stops, all at once. Five seconds of perfect stillness. Then the snow begins again, in a new world.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.017
cast.text: The ice in this cave is older than the world. I've counted the layers. There are more layers than there have been worlds. Far more. So something was here first, my dear. Something cold and patient, waiting for the world to arrive.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.018
cast.text: Hazel says the world is a spell. Well, ice is a sort of spell. It stops time. Nearly.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.019
cast.text: I keep a frozen moment in a little ice box. Just a second, from a world long gone. When I hold it to my ear, I can hear someone laughing.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.020
cast.text: The ice cave grows a little deeper every world. I've never dug it. I think something is digging from the other side.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.021
cast.text: Captain Brine thinks the sea doesn't change. He's never seen my ice. The ice remembers the sea from before. It was a different sea. Warmer.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.022
cast.text: The snow falls in spirals before a rebuild. Big, slow spirals, turning toward the middle of the world. Like water down a drain.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.023
cast.text: There's a frozen door at the back of my cave. Clear ice, and behind it, darkness. I've never been able to melt it. I'm not sure I want to.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.024
cast.text: Some say the world is getting colder, every world, a tiny bit. And when it freezes solid, it will finally stay still. I don't think that would be nice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.025
cast.text: Some say the world is getting warmer, every world. And one day, the ice will melt, and whatever is frozen inside will wake up. I don't know which is true.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.026
cast.text: The world's mercy feels like a warm hand on a cold day. I'm told. I've never been cold, so I've never needed one. But I've felt it pass by.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.027
cast.text: The enemies never come near the ice. They slip, I imagine. Or perhaps they know the ice is watching.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.028
cast.text: I once froze a snowflake just before a rebuild, to see if it would survive. It did. In the new world, it was still in my hand. The only thing that came with me.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.029
cast.text: I keep a snowflake from a world long gone. It hasn't melted. Every world, it has one more point on it. It started with six. It has twelve now.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.030
cast.text: Pendle came to visit once, to listen for the great clock. He listened for a whole world. When he left, he said, it's slow. I asked what was slow. He wouldn't say.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.031
cast.text: The wind in the blizzard says names. Not ours. Names of worlds, I think. Long, old names. I've written some of them in the frost.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.032
cast.text: Snow covers everything, and makes it all look the same. Then it melts, and everything is different. That's the rebuild, my dear. Snow, and thaw.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.033
cast.text: A traveller told me the world is a snow globe, shaken every few minutes. I said, then who's holding it? He went very quiet, and left.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.034
cast.text: Ice is just water that decided to be still for a while. Perhaps one day the world will decide the same.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.035
cast.text: I've noticed the icicles point in a different direction every world. Not down. Toward someone. I've followed them. They point toward walkers. Toward you.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.036
cast.text: The frozen pool in my cave shows reflections that aren't there. A tall shape, standing at the edge. Every world, it's a little closer to the water. I don't think it means any harm. It just stands there, listening, like you.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.037
cast.text: Sprocket wants to put a machine in my cave to measure the cold. I said no. Some things are better unmeasured.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.038
cast.text: Corbin, up on the mountain, thinks the wind is the world breathing. Then the ice is the world holding its breath. And it's holding it for something.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.039
cast.text: There's a crack in the ice that's grown a little every world. Long and thin and perfectly straight. Like a line someone is drawing, very slowly.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.040
cast.text: I once heard the ice sing. A high, thin, ringing note, all through the cave. Then the countdown. Then silence. The ice has never sung since.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.041
cast.text: Lady is not my real name, you know. I've forgotten my real name. The ice took it, I think. It keeps everything, sooner or later.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.042
cast.text: Some travellers come to the ice cave to cool down. Some come to think. You came to listen. That's the rarest kind.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.043
cast.text: The cold slows everything down. Even the rebuild, I think. The world takes a little longer to change in here. As if it doesn't want to disturb me.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.044
cast.text: Every world, I find new frost patterns on my window. Ferns, feathers, stars. Last world, the frost drew a door. This world, a key.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.045
cast.text: The snow muffles all sound. In a blizzard, the world is so quiet you can hear your own heartbeat. And under that, faintly, the world's.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.046
cast.text: Some say the ice holds the answer, frozen in its heart. If you melt it, you'll have the answer, but no ice. I'd rather keep the ice.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.047
cast.text: The ice cave was here before the labyrinths. I'm sure of it. They were built around it, carefully, like someone building around something precious.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.048
cast.text: Every world, I listen for a change in the ice. A crack, a creak, a new note. That's how I know the world is still deciding. Still alive.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.049
cast.text: I wear a shawl made of frost. It's very light. It sparkles, I'm told.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.050
cast.text: Mind the icicles by the door, my dear. They're very old, and very proud.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.051
cast.text: I make ice sculptures when I'm bored. A swan, a fox, a little house. They never melt. I have quite a collection.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.052
cast.text: The ice cave sings when the wind blows across its mouth. One long note. Ambrose says it's the note of his silent pipe. Everything sings that note eventually.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.053
cast.text: There's a frozen waterfall at the back of my cave. Every world, it's frozen at a slightly different moment. As if someone keeps stopping it to look.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.054
cast.text: The snow falls upward for a single moment just before the countdown. Every flake. Then it falls down again, onto a new world.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.055
cast.text: I keep a frozen candle flame in a jar. It doesn't flicker. It doesn't melt. It doesn't give heat. It just glows. From a world long gone.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.056
cast.text: The world's mercy reaches even here, my dear. The ice glows softly, for a moment, warm and golden. I've never felt warm. But I've felt that.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.057
cast.text: There's a rumor that a walker once slept in the ice for a hundred worlds and woke up knowing the answer. When they woke, they'd forgotten it.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.058
cast.text: The blizzard always blows toward the middle of the world. The snow piles up there, in a great white mound. Every world, the mound is higher.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.059
cast.text: Ice cracks make sounds like voices. Sharp, clear, sudden. I've heard the ice say, wait, and, here, and once, you.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.060
cast.text: Every snowflake that falls in my cave has six points. Except one, every world, which has five. I catch it and keep it. I have a whole box of them.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.061
cast.text: The frozen pool has a fish in it, frozen solid. Every world, it's facing a different way. It's either very slowly swimming, or the world is turning around it.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.062
cast.text: The cold keeps things the same, my dear. That's why I love it. In a world that never stops changing, the cold is the closest thing to forever.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.063
cast.text: Corbin sends me a sheep every few worlds. To keep me company, he says. It's always very confused. I send it back with a scarf.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.064
cast.text: The deepest part of my cave is so cold that sound freezes. You can speak, and your words hang in the air. I left a question there once. It's still waiting for an answer.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.065
cast.text: There's an old saying in the snow. What the ice keeps, the world forgets. And what the world forgets, the ice remembers. I've always liked that.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.066
cast.text: Somebody leaves footprints in the fresh snow outside my cave every world. They come right up to the door, and stop. Then they go away again. Very polite.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.067
cast.text: The northern lights shimmer over the ice right before a rebuild. Green and silver. I can hear them crackling. They spell something. I've never quite caught what.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.068
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds the way frost forms on glass. One crystal at a time, very fast, following a pattern only the cold knows.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.069
cast.text: I once asked the ice why the world keeps changing. The ice answered with a crack, right down the middle of the floor. I took it to mean, mind your own business.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.070
cast.text: The ice cave is the stillest safe place, I think. Perfect for listening. In the stillness, you can hear the world deciding what to be next.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.071
cast.text: Commander Vega says the world looks the same temperature from space, every world. She hasn't been in my cave. Space doesn't know everything.

cast.name: vc_icelady.story.072
cast.text: The ice remembers every walker who passes. Your footsteps are frozen in the floor, very faintly. Every world, a new set. All of them yours.

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, lad! Or lass! Follow my shout!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.002
cast.text: Oi! This way, out of the wind!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! By the stone hut!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.004
cast.text: This way, walker! Keep your head down!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.005
cast.text: Hello there! Can you hear me over the wind? Over here!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Mind the drop on your left!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.007
cast.text: This way! The sheep are tucked in, and so am I!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.008
cast.text: Over here, friend! It's warmer by the wall!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.009
cast.text: Hello! Follow my voice up the hill!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.010
cast.text: This way! Steady on, the wind's fierce today!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! I've a gift, and a blanket!

cast.name: vc_mountain.greet.012
cast.text: Oi! Walker! Over here!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.001
cast.text: Oi! Come back! You've left your gift!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Out of the wind!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.003
cast.text: This way, walker! Back to the hut!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.004
cast.text: Come back, friend! It's still here!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.005
cast.text: Over here! Don't let the wind blow you off!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.006
cast.text: Back this way! Follow my shout!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.007
cast.text: Walker! You forgot something! Up here!

cast.name: vc_mountain.call.008
cast.text: This way again! Keep your head down!

cast.name: vc_mountain.gift.001
cast.text: Here you are. Kept it out of the wind.

cast.name: vc_mountain.gift.002
cast.text: Take this, friend. You'll need it more than the sheep.

cast.name: vc_mountain.gift.003
cast.text: For you. Wrap up warm.

cast.name: vc_mountain.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the mountain. Mind your footing.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.001
cast.text: I'm Corbin. I keep sheep up on the mountain. Well, they keep themselves. I just count them.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.002
cast.text: That howling? Just the wind. It's always howling. It's got a lot to say.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.003
cast.text: Wrap up warm, friend. The wind goes right through you up here.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.004
cast.text: I've got forty sheep. Forty one, some worlds. The extra one always looks very innocent.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.005
cast.text: The hut's small, but the walls are thick. Built them myself. Every world, they're still standing.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.006
cast.text: Fancy a cup of tea? It's mostly hot water. The wind steals the tea leaves.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.007
cast.text: The mountain's lonely, but I like it. Me, the sheep, and the sky.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.008
cast.text: My dog ran off three worlds ago. Fine dog. I'm sure she's chasing something important.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.009
cast.text: The wind blew my hat off in the first world. I've never found it. I've never stopped looking.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.010
cast.text: Up here, you can hear the whole world. Every sound drifts up the mountain eventually.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.011
cast.text: The wind is the world breathing, friend. In, and out. When it howls, the world is breathing hard. When it stops, the world is holding its breath.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Great Breath. The world breathes out, everything blows away, and then it breathes in, and there's a new world.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.013
cast.text: The wind always howls loudest just before the countdown. Like the world is taking one enormous breath before it starts again.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.014
cast.text: I count my sheep every world. Forty. Always forty. But they're never the same forty. Different faces, different bleats. Somebody swaps them.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.015
cast.text: The wind carries names up the mountain. I've heard them. Old names, strange names. Names of people and places that aren't here anymore.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.016
cast.text: Once, I heard your name on the wind. Or I think it was yours. It was a name I didn't know, said by a voice I didn't know, very kindly.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.017
cast.text: From up here, you can hear the whole world rebuild. It starts at the edges and rolls toward the middle. Like a wave coming in.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.018
cast.text: There's a cairn at the top of the mountain. A pile of stones. Every walker who reaches it adds one. It's taller every world. Nobody knows who put the first stone.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.019
cast.text: The sheep all face the same way before a rebuild. Into the wind. Toward the middle of the world. Then they lie down. Every one of them.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.020
cast.text: Lady Rime thinks the ice is the world holding its breath. I think she's right. And the wind is what happens when it lets go.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.021
cast.text: Some say there's a giant asleep under the mountain, and the wind is its snoring. If so, it's been asleep a very long time. And it's a very loud snorer.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.022
cast.text: I don't believe in giants under mountains. But I've felt the mountain move. Just a little. Just before a rebuild. Like something rolling over in bed.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.023
cast.text: The world's mercy comes up the mountain like a sudden calm. The wind just stops. The sheep look up. And for a moment, everything's warm and still.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.024
cast.text: The enemies never climb the mountain. Too steep, too windy. Or maybe the mountain just doesn't let them up.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.025
cast.text: There's a shepherd's song about the wind. The wind blows here, the wind blows there, the wind blows round the world and back. And then nobody knows the next verse.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.026
cast.text: I've stood at the top of the mountain and shouted my question to the world. Why do you keep changing? The wind took the question away. Never brought an answer back.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.027
cast.text: Hazel says the world is a spell. Mortimer says a garden. Sprocket says a machine. I say it's weather. Nobody controls the weather. It just happens. Then again, someone must decide when it rains. Mustn't they?

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.028
cast.text: The winter never ends up here. The snow never melts, the wind never stops. Like the world forgot to change the season. Or chose not to.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.029
cast.text: I found a shepherd's crook up on the high ridge once. Old and worn, not mine. Carved into the handle were five little notches. And a word. Wait.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.030
cast.text: Some nights, the wind howls a tune. Five notes, rising and falling. I've heard the same tune from Jangles's fiddle. And from the drips in Petra's cave.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.031
cast.text: The clouds move fast up here. Every world, they race toward the middle of the world, faster and faster. Then the rebuild. Then they start again, slow.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.032
cast.text: I've seen a light on the next mountain over. Just one, steady, like a lamp in a window. I've never been able to cross to it. The valley's always too deep. Someone like me lives there, maybe, wondering who lives over here.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.033
cast.text: The old shepherds used to say the wind is looking for something. That's why it never stops. It's searching every corner of the world. What for, I've asked. The wind just howls. I've never been good at understanding howling.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.034
cast.text: My sheep never get lost, no matter how the world changes. They always find the hut. Maybe there's a map in their heads. Or in their hearts.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.035
cast.text: Every world, there's a new path up the mountain. I've walked each one. They all end at the same place. The cairn, at the very top.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.036
cast.text: Commander Vega says the world looks small from space. Well, it looks big enough from up here. Big enough to get lost in, anyway.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.037
cast.text: Wind wears down the mountain, grain by grain. Every world, the mountain is a tiny bit smaller. One day, it'll be flat. What then?

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.038
cast.text: The howling wind isn't scary, once you know it. It's just loud. Like a big dog that wants attention.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.039
cast.text: I think the wind remembers every world. It's been everywhere. Blown through every street, every forest, every cave. If anyone knows, it's the wind.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.040
cast.text: There's an old saying up here. When the wind goes still, listen hard. That's when the world tells the truth. I've listened hard. I'm still waiting.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.041
cast.text: I left a bell on the cairn, so the wind would ring it. Every world, it rings five times before the countdown. Then it's still.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.042
cast.text: Sol the wanderer passed by once. We sat by the hut and listened to the wind for a whole world. Didn't say a word. Best conversation I ever had.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.043
cast.text: The sky up here is very big. Bigger than it should be. Like the world's ceiling is very high, and very far away.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.044
cast.text: I've got a theory. The world rebuilds every time the wind changes direction. I've been watching. I'm nearly sure. Nearly.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.045
cast.text: My grandfather was a shepherd. He said the world used to stay the same for a whole year. Then it was a month. Then a day. Now, a few minutes. It's speeding up, he said. Or maybe we're slowing down. I've never worked out which.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.046
cast.text: Mind the edge, friend. It's a long way down, and the wind's not kind to tumblers.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.047
cast.text: My boots are older than my sheep. And my sheep are very old.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.048
cast.text: Have a bit of cheese. Sheep's cheese. It's strong. It'll put hair on your ears.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.049
cast.text: The snow on the peak never melts, but every world, there's a new footprint at the very top. One footprint. Like someone stood there on one foot, looking out.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.050
cast.text: The wind brings snow from the north, every world. Always the north. Mortimer's moss grows north too. Something up north is calling everything.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.051
cast.text: Some nights, the wind goes quiet, and I hear singing from below the mountain. Deep, slow, gentle. Like someone humming to a baby.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.052
cast.text: The sheep never panic at the countdown. They just lie down and wait. I've learned a lot from my sheep. Mostly patience.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.053
cast.text: I've seen the world rebuild from the mountaintop. It's like watching a great cloth being shaken out and laid down again, smooth and new.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.054
cast.text: The stone hut has a door that rattles in the wind. Rattle, rattle, rattle, rattle, rattle. Five times. Then the countdown. Every world.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.055
cast.text: There's a rumour among shepherds that the mountain is the world's shoulder, and the world is a giant lying on its side. Every rebuild, it shifts in its sleep.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.056
cast.text: The world's mercy, up here, is a sudden warm breeze in the middle of winter. The sheep all look up. Then the cold comes back, and they look at me, like it was my doing.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.057
cast.text: I keep a list of every sheep's name, every world. Different sheep, different names. But the last sheep in the flock is always called the same. Wanderer.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.058
cast.text: There's a carved stone at the top of the pass. One word on it, worn almost smooth. I think it says, beyond. Or perhaps, behind. Hard to say.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.059
cast.text: The wind steals things. Hats, scarves, tea leaves. I've often wondered where it puts them all. Somewhere, there's a great pile of stolen hats.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.060
cast.text: Hazel came up the mountain once to collect snow for a potion. She said mountain snow remembers the sky. I don't know what that means. I gave her a bucket anyway.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.061
cast.text: The mountain echo takes five seconds to come back. Shout, and wait. One, two, three, four, five. Then your own voice, a little older.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.062
cast.text: The howling wind goes silent for a moment when a walker arrives. Like it's stopped to listen. Then it starts howling again, a bit louder. Showing off.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.063
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds the way weather changes. No reason, no plan. It just turns. Clouds come in, clouds go out. And the world is new.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.064
cast.text: There's a little flower that grows in the snow by the hut. Only one. Every world, it's there. White, with a blue middle. I've never seen it anywhere else.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.065
cast.text: The sheep's bells ring together sometimes, all at once, all the same note. Then the rebuild. I don't know how they know. Sheep are deeper than they look.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.066
cast.text: Commander Vega says she can see my mountain from space. She says it's the tallest point in the world. I told her, of course it is. I've climbed it.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.067
cast.text: The wind up here has been blowing since before the first world, they say. It's never stopped once. That's a lot of breath to hold.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.068
cast.text: When the wind dies down, you can hear the whole world below. Every safe place, every labyrinth, every footstep. Including yours, walker. Including yours.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.069
cast.text: Somebody leaves a bundle of firewood by the hut every world. Dry, neatly tied. Mountain air doesn't let anyone stay long enough to be seen.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.070
cast.text: I asked an old ram why the world keeps changing. He looked at me for a whole minute, then ate my hat. The wind had nothing to do with it that time.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.071
cast.text: The mountain stays, the world changes. That's what I believe. Every world, the mountain's still here, and so am I. That's good enough for a shepherd.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.072
cast.text: The howling wind isn't angry, friend. It's calling. Calling for something it lost, a long time ago. I've never found out what.

cast.name: vc_mountain.story.073
cast.text: The cairn at the top has a little hollow on one side, just the right size for a hand. Put yours in, and you'll feel it. A heartbeat. Slow and steady.

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.001
cast.text: Over here! Follow the clanking!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.002
cast.text: Hey! This way, past the big machine!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.003
cast.text: Over here, walker! Mind the sparks!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.004
cast.text: This way! Don't touch the levers!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.005
cast.text: Hello! I'm by the generator! The loud one!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! The storm's charging my batteries!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.007
cast.text: This way, quick! Before the thunder!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.008
cast.text: Over here! I invented something for you! Well, found it!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.009
cast.text: Hey there! Follow the hum of the engines!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.010
cast.text: This way! Watch out for the conveyor belt!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.011
cast.text: Over here! Safety goggles optional, curiosity required!

cast.name: vc_engineer.greet.012
cast.text: Hello, walker! By the workbench!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.001
cast.text: Hey! Come back! Your gift's still on the workbench!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Follow the clanking!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.003
cast.text: This way! Mind the sparks!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.004
cast.text: Come back! I calibrated it just for you!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.005
cast.text: Over here! Don't let the storm scare you off!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.006
cast.text: Back this way, walker! Past the big machine!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.007
cast.text: Hey! You forgot your gift! Over here!

cast.name: vc_engineer.call.008
cast.text: This way again! By the generator!

cast.name: vc_engineer.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go! Fully charged!

cast.name: vc_engineer.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! Tested it twice. Well, once.

cast.name: vc_engineer.gift.003
cast.text: For you! Built to last, at least till the next world!

cast.name: vc_engineer.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the workshop! Handle with care!

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.001
cast.text: I'm Mister Sprocket! Inventor, engineer, and collector of lightning!

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.002
cast.text: Hear that thunder? That's free electricity, walker! I just need a bigger jar.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.003
cast.text: Every machine in this factory works. I just don't know what most of them do.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.004
cast.text: I've been struck by lightning nine times. My hair has never been the same.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.005
cast.text: The conveyor belt goes round and round. I've never found where it starts. Or what it's carrying.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.006
cast.text: Gears, levers, pistons, pulleys. Beautiful, isn't it? Like music, but greasier.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.007
cast.text: Mind the steam pipes. They hiss when they're grumpy. Which is always.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.008
cast.text: I invented a machine that makes tea. It also makes toast. And sometimes, alarming noises.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.009
cast.text: A good engineer fixes things. A great engineer wonders why they broke. I'm still deciding which one I am.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.010
cast.text: The storm's my favorite weather. It's loud, it's bright, and it powers my workshop for free.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.011
cast.text: The world is a machine, walker! A huge one! And every few minutes, it resets itself, like a machine that's been switched off and on again.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.012
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Reboot. Everything shuts down, the gears spin back to the start, and up it all comes again. Clean and new.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.013
cast.text: There's a great engine somewhere under the world. I can hear it through the factory floor. Rumble, rumble, clank. It never stops.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.014
cast.text: The lightning strikes five times right before every countdown. Five bolts, five booms. Then the rebuild. I've measured it. It's very precise.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.015
cast.text: I think the lightning powers the rebuild. All that energy has to come from somewhere. Where does it go? Into the new world, I reckon.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.016
cast.text: The machines in the factory build parts I don't recognize. Pipes, walls, little bits of labyrinth. I think they're building pieces of the next world.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.017
cast.text: Hazel thinks the world is magic. Magic is just engineering that hasn't been explained yet. I've told her. She turned my wrench into a fish. The fish is fine, by the way. I keep it in a bucket.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.018
cast.text: Pendle thinks the world is a clock. A clock is a machine, so he's half right. Cinder thinks it's a forge. A forge is a workshop, so he's a quarter right.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.019
cast.text: I tried to build a machine that would stop the rebuild. It worked for one second. Then the world rebuilt anyway, and my machine became a toaster.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.020
cast.text: The storm clouds always gather over the middle of the world before a rebuild. Like the world is charging up. Then, boom. New world.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.021
cast.text: I opened a panel in the factory wall once. Behind it, more gears. Behind those, more gears. I kept opening panels for a whole world. Gears all the way down.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.022
cast.text: The machines in the factory never break. I've never once repaired them. Something fixes them between worlds. Something very good at its job.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.023
cast.text: I found a blueprint in the factory. Very old, very faded. It's a plan of the world. But it's missing one piece, right in the middle. Just a blank square.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.024
cast.text: Some say the Builder is an engineer, like me. Builds a world, tests it, finds a problem, and starts over. That's how I work, too.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.025
cast.text: If I were the Builder, I'd want feedback. So, if you're listening, Builder, the labyrinths are a bit confusing, and the enemies throw too much.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.026
cast.text: The rain in the storm is warm. That's not normal. Warm rain means something underneath is very hot. Probably the great engine. Probably.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.027
cast.text: The world's mercy is a power surge. I'm sure of it. A little extra energy, sent through the world, out of nowhere. Somebody's generous with the electricity.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.028
cast.text: The enemies don't like my factory. Too noisy, I think. Or they're scared of the conveyor belt. Can't blame them. It's very fast.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.029
cast.text: I've heard a voice in the static of my radio. Just before a rebuild. It says, recalibrating. Then it goes quiet. I've never found the broadcast.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.030
cast.text: The factory has a door I can't open. Heavy, metal, with a warning sign. The sign is blank. Who makes a blank warning sign? What's it warning about?

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.031
cast.text: Every world, the factory makes one thing I didn't ask for. Last world, it was a key. This world, it was a tiny bell. Next world, who knows.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.032
cast.text: The factory keeps making bells and keys. I think they're parts of something. If I could collect all of them, I could build it. I just don't know what it is.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.033
cast.text: Thunder is just the sound of the air moving out of the way of the lightning. Maybe the rebuild is the world moving out of the way of something.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.034
cast.text: I measured the world once, end to end, with a very long tape measure. Next world, I measured again. Same size, to the inch. Different shape. How?

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.035
cast.text: The steam pipes whistle a tune right before the countdown. Five notes. Everybody's heard that tune somewhere. I want to know who wrote it.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.036
cast.text: I tried recording the rebuild with a machine I built. When I played it back, all I heard was a click. One click. Like a switch. Who flips it? My best guess so far is, someone with a very big finger.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.037
cast.text: The lightning in the storm always strikes the same spot. A tall iron pole in the middle of nowhere. I didn't put it there. Nobody did. It's just always there.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.038
cast.text: There's a rumor among the engineers that the world is a test run. And one day, the real world will be built. When the test is finished. I'd love to see the real thing. It must be enormous. With better plumbing.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.039
cast.text: The factory has a control room with a thousand buttons. None of them are labeled. I've pressed most of them. Nothing happens. Except one. One button makes the lights flicker. I've not pressed that one again.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.040
cast.text: Captain Brine says something under the sea keeps count. I bet it's a machine. A counter, ticking up. One more world. One more world.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.041
cast.text: Mister Pendle and I argued for a whole world about whether the world is a clock or an engine. Then it rebuilt, and we had to start over. We'll get there.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.042
cast.text: The factory floor is warm, always. Put your hand flat on it, and you'll feel it humming. The world's motor, running and running.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.043
cast.text: Every machine needs fuel. So what does the world run on? I've got a theory. Curiosity. Ours. It runs on us asking why. Maybe that's why it never stops. Nobody's stopped asking.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.044
cast.text: The storm never passes. It just circles the factory, round and round, like it's guarding it. Or like it's waiting for me to finish something.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.045
cast.text: I built a compass once that points to the great engine under the world. It points straight down. Every world. Straight down. Very helpful.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.046
cast.text: The conveyor belt sometimes carries things from the old world into the new one. A cup, a shoe, a spring. Then they drop off the end, and I never find them again.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.047
cast.text: Some engineers say the world rebuilds because it's overheating. Too many walkers, too many enemies, too much going on. It needs to cool down and restart.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.048
cast.text: Maybe the world isn't overheating at all. Maybe it's warming up, getting ready for something big. That's what I'd do, if I were a world.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.049
cast.text: Lady Rime won't let me put a thermometer in her ice cave. She says some things should stay unmeasured. I say everything should be measured. We're both very stubborn.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.050
cast.text: Every answer I find in this factory comes with a new question attached, like a gear with another gear behind it. Turn one, and the next one spins.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.051
cast.text: Safety first, walker! Well, curiosity first. Then safety. Then lunch.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.052
cast.text: I keep a lightning bottle on my desk. It's empty now. The lightning got out. It's somewhere in the factory. Don't worry about it.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.053
cast.text: The rivets in the factory walls count up. One, two, three, all the way around. The last rivet is always missing. Every world.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.054
cast.text: Every machine in the factory hums a little louder right before the rebuild. Like they're all saying, here we go again, together.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.055
cast.text: I built a listening machine to hear the edge of the world. It picked up one sound. Someone, very far away, tightening a bolt.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.056
cast.text: The thunder here rolls in fives. Boom, boom, boom, boom, boom. Then silence. Then the rebuild. I've got a chart. It's very convincing.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.057
cast.text: There's a lever in the factory labeled, do not pull. I haven't pulled it. Somebody has. Every world, it's in a slightly different position.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.058
cast.text: The factory chimney puffs smoke rings. Perfect rings, one for every world. They float toward the middle of the world and disappear.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.059
cast.text: I tried to take a gear from the old world into the new one. I held it tight. In the new world, my hand was holding a flower. A metal flower.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.060
cast.text: The storm's lightning writes letters in the sky. Just for a flash. I've seen an A, an N, and something like a question mark.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.061
cast.text: Every invention I make, the world copies. I made a tiny fan last world. This world, there's a giant fan in the middle of the labyrinth.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.062
cast.text: The bus drivers out there drive like machines. Never a wrong turn, never a pause. I'd love to look under their hoods. Not that they have hoods.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.063
cast.text: I think the world was built to be fixed. Over and over. Like a machine made by someone who loves fixing things more than finishing them.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.064
cast.text: There's an old engineer's rhyme. Wind it up and let it go, where it stops, nobody knows. I always thought it was about toys. Now I'm not so sure.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.065
cast.text: The world's gears are too big to see. But you can feel them turn. Stand very still in any safe place, and you'll feel the tiny shudder of a gear moving on.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.066
cast.text: My radio once picked up a broadcast from a world long gone. A weather report. It said, sunny, with a chance of rebuilding. Ha. Somebody has a sense of humor.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.067
cast.text: The labyrinth walls are made of a material I can't identify. Not stone, not metal, not wood. Warm, hard, and very slightly springy. Like it's grown, not built.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.068
cast.text: Sometimes the storm stops just long enough for me to hear the world's engine clearly. It's running smoothly. Somebody is very good at maintenance.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.069
cast.text: I tried to build my own world in a box. A little one. It worked for five seconds. Then it rebuilt itself into a slightly better box.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.070
cast.text: The factory whistle blows once per world. Right at the rebuild. End of shift. New shift begins. Somebody keeps very strict hours.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.071
cast.text: I think the Builder is an inventor, and the world is their best invention. And every inventor knows, there's always one more improvement.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.072
cast.text: I keep a notebook of every machine I've ever found in the factory. Ninety nine machines. I'm sure there's a hundredth. It's just hiding.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.073
cast.text: The lightning rod on the roof glows faintly between worlds. In the dark, quiet in between. Like a lighthouse, helping the next world find its way.

cast.name: vc_engineer.story.074
cast.text: Somebody oils the gears between worlds. I can smell the fresh oil every time. Somebody's taking care of this place. Taking care of all of us.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.001
cast.text: Over here, cadet! Follow my signal!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.002
cast.text: Hello! This way, to the airlock!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.003
cast.text: Over here! Welcome aboard!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.004
cast.text: This way, walker. Mind the floating stuff.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.005
cast.text: Commander Vega, over here! Come in, walker!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.006
cast.text: Over here! Follow the beeping!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.007
cast.text: This way, cadet! Docking bay is open!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.008
cast.text: Hello! I'm by the control panel!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.009
cast.text: Over here! Gravity is optional, but walking helps!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.010
cast.text: This way, walker! Mission control has a gift for you!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.011
cast.text: Over here, cadet! Signal is strong!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.greet.012
cast.text: Hello, hello! Come aboard!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.001
cast.text: Cadet! Come back! Your gift is still on board!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.002
cast.text: Over here again! Follow my signal!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.003
cast.text: This way, walker! Back to the airlock!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.004
cast.text: Come in, walker! You've left something behind!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.005
cast.text: Over here! Don't drift off!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.006
cast.text: Back this way, cadet! Mission not complete!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.007
cast.text: Walker, come back! Your supplies are ready!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.call.008
cast.text: This way again! By the control panel!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.gift.001
cast.text: Here you go, cadet! Mission supplies!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.gift.002
cast.text: Take this! Packed it myself, zero gravity tested!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.gift.003
cast.text: For you, walker! Over and out!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.gift.004
cast.text: A gift from the stars! Safe travels, cadet!

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.001
cast.text: I'm Commander Vega. I fly through space, and sometimes, space flies through me. Not literally.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.002
cast.text: Welcome aboard my ship! Don't press the big red button. Or any button, really.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.003
cast.text: Space is very quiet. That's why I talk so much. Somebody has to fill the silence.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.004
cast.text: I've been orbiting this world for longer than I can count. And I can count very high.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.005
cast.text: The engines hum all the time. I find it soothing. Like a giant cat purring.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.006
cast.text: My ship's computer tells jokes. Bad ones. I laugh anyway. It's polite.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.007
cast.text: Floating is fun, once you get used to it. Just don't spill your juice.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.008
cast.text: I eat my meals out of little pouches. I miss forks. I really miss forks.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.009
cast.text: The stars are beautiful from up here. Even if all I can do is hear them hum.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.010
cast.text: Every cadet needs a good helmet, a steady hand, and a sense of wonder. I can lend you the helmet.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.011
cast.text: I've seen the world from above, walker. All of it, at once. It's round, and it's small, and it changes. Every few minutes, the whole thing ripples, and it's new.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.012
cast.text: From orbit, the rebuild looks like a wave of light rolling across the world. Starting at the edges, sweeping to the middle. Then it's done.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.013
cast.text: I call the rebuild the Fold. Like folding a map. The world folds up, unfolds, and the roads are all in different places.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.014
cast.text: There's no edge to the world. I've flown all the way around it. It just curves, and curves, and you end up back where you started.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.015
cast.text: I've picked up a signal from deep space. Very faint. It repeats every few minutes. It's the same rhythm as the countdown. Five beeps.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.016
cast.text: Somebody out there is counting along with the countdown. Somebody far away. Or somebody very close, and the signal is just bouncing back.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.017
cast.text: There's another world out there, I'm sure of it. I've seen a light, far off, that changes every few minutes, just like ours. Another world, rebuilding.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.018
cast.text: Pell the ghost has a house that floats in space sometimes. I've seen it go by. She waves. I wave back. We've never actually spoken.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.019
cast.text: The world is surrounded by quiet. Total quiet. When I fly out into it, my radio goes silent. Except for one thing. A low hum. The world's hum.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.020
cast.text: The ship's computer has a file called, answer. It's locked. I don't have the password. I've tried everything. Even, please.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.021
cast.text: I tried flying away from the world, as far as I could go. The fuel ran out right at the countdown. When the new world arrived, I was back in orbit. The world doesn't want me to leave, I think. Or it wants me to keep watching.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.022
cast.text: The stars move a little every world. Not much. But I've charted them. They're spelling something out, very slowly. It's too early to read.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.023
cast.text: Sprocket thinks the world is a machine. From up here, it looks more like a living thing. It breathes. It changes. It almost seems to think.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.024
cast.text: The world's mercy shows up on my instruments as a little flicker. A spike of energy, out of nowhere, from somewhere in the middle of the world.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.025
cast.text: My ship's sensors pick up something under the world. Something big and warm. Not moving. Just there. Waiting, maybe. Or sleeping.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.026
cast.text: Hazel asked me if the stars know why the world changes. I said I'd ask them. I've been sending them the question every world. No reply yet.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.027
cast.text: The enemies don't come up to space. Too far, I suppose. Or they don't have spaceships. That's probably it.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.028
cast.text: There's a satellite in orbit I didn't launch. Very old, very small. It beeps once every world, exactly as the rebuild happens. Someone is keeping track.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.029
cast.text: Captain Brine navigates by the stars. I told him the stars move every world. He said, so does the sea. Fair point, captain.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.030
cast.text: The ship's log has entries I didn't write. In my handwriting. About worlds I don't remember. One of them says, almost figured it out. Don't stop.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.031
cast.text: I've seen something strange from orbit. A tiny spot in the middle of the world that never changes. Every world, all around it changes, but that spot stays still.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.032
cast.text: There's a spot in the middle of the world I've tried to land on. Every time I start the descent, the world rebuilds, and the spot moves. Like it doesn't want visitors.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.033
cast.text: Space is cold and dark and very big. But it's not empty. It's full of hum. The whole universe is humming, and our world is humming along.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.034
cast.text: From up here, the safe places glow a little. Warm spots, scattered across the world. They make a pattern. I'm still working out what pattern.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.035
cast.text: Some astronauts say there's a ship like mine for every world, and each one has a commander, watching. I've never met the others. But I've heard their signals.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.036
cast.text: The engines need fuel, and every world, the tanks are full again. I never refuel. Somebody's topping me up, between worlds.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.037
cast.text: I asked mission control why the world rebuilds. Mission control is a speaker that only plays static. But the static got louder. That might be a yes.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.038
cast.text: The world is a puzzle, from up here. Pieces moving, sliding, clicking into new places. I keep waiting for the picture to be finished.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.039
cast.text: I think the world rebuilds because it's looking for the right shape. Trying different ones. Like a key trying different locks.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.040
cast.text: The countdown voice is broadcasting from somewhere, cadet. I've tracked the signal. It comes from everywhere at once. That shouldn't be possible.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.041
cast.text: Lady Rime says the world is getting colder. Cinder says it's getting hotter. From up here, it's exactly the same temperature, every world. To the degree.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.042
cast.text: Every time I fly past the moon, it's a little closer. Very slowly. One day it'll be close enough to touch. Then we'll see.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.043
cast.text: I found a message scratched into my ship's hull. On the outside. In space. It said, keep watching. How did someone write that out there?

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.044
cast.text: The view from orbit is the loneliest view there is. But then I hear a walker down there, finding their way, and I don't feel so lonely.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.045
cast.text: Some say the world is a seed, floating through space, and one day it'll land somewhere and grow into something huge. I like that idea.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.046
cast.text: My instruments say the world is getting very slightly bigger, every world. Not much. But growing. Like it's making room for something new.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.047
cast.text: There's a dark patch in space near the world where no stars shine. My radar says it's empty. My ears say something's there. Humming very softly.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.048
cast.text: I once heard someone singing over the radio. The same song the ghost choir sings, but faster. Like they were in a hurry to get to the end.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.049
cast.text: I don't need to know why the world rebuilds, cadet. I just need to know it'll be there when I look down. And it always is.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.050
cast.text: The ship's clock and Mister Pendle's clocks never agree. His are always a little behind. I think time moves faster up here. Or slower down there.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.051
cast.text: I sent a probe down to the middle of the world once. It sent back one message before it went quiet. It said, door.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.052
cast.text: Every mission needs a goal. Mine was to find out why the world rebuilds. I've been on that mission for a thousand worlds. Still the best job I've ever had.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.053
cast.text: Rule one of space travel, cadet. Always know where your snacks are.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.054
cast.text: I named the ship Wanderlust. She doesn't always go where I point her. She has her own ideas.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.055
cast.text: The world has a gentle wobble, like a spinning top. Every rebuild, the wobble starts again from the beginning.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.056
cast.text: I keep a jar of stardust on the dashboard. Every world, there's a little more in it. I never collect any. It just collects.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.057
cast.text: The world's shadow on the moon has a shape. Not round. More like a door, standing open.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.058
cast.text: The radio once picked up a voice saying, can anyone hear me? I answered. It said, oh good. Then the world rebuilt.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.059
cast.text: I've counted the safe places from orbit, every world. Somewhere between six and twelve. Never the same. Never more than twelve.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.060
cast.text: Some cadets think the Builder lives in space, looking down. I've looked everywhere up here. Nobody. Just me, and the hum.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.061
cast.text: There's a comet that passes the world once every rebuild. Same comet. Same path. It's either very punctual or very lost.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.062
cast.text: My helmet radio sometimes picks up the walkers' footsteps. Yours too. You walk like someone who's not giving up.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.063
cast.text: The airlock opens by itself sometimes, just before the countdown. A little puff of air. As if something is letting itself in. Or out.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.064
cast.text: I've measured the hum of the world in every world. It's always the same note. But the note before it changes. Like the world is building up to something.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.065
cast.text: If you could see the world from up here, you'd see it's a labyrinth too. One big labyrinth, made of little ones. And it's never finished.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.066
cast.text: Some days I think the world is a ship, like mine. Traveling somewhere. And the rebuild is just the scenery outside changing as we fly.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.067
cast.text: Mission log, entry one million. The world rebuilt again. Nobody knows why. Morale is good. Snacks are running low.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.068
cast.text: The stars spell out a letter every few worlds. So far, I've got three letters. They don't make a word yet. I'm patient.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.069
cast.text: Mister Sprocket built me a better antenna. Now I can hear the world more clearly. It sounds like someone humming while they work.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.070
cast.text: The space between the stars isn't empty, cadet. It's full of old echoes. Every world that ever rebuilt is still out there, faintly ringing.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.071
cast.text: A cadet asked me if the world is real. I said, it's real enough to walk on, real enough to get lost in. That's pretty real.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.072
cast.text: There's a frequency on my radio that only plays one word, over and over. Soon. I've been listening for a thousand worlds. Still soon.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.073
cast.text: I think the world is a message. Sent from somewhere, to someone. Every rebuild, it says it again, a little differently, hoping someone understands.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.074
cast.text: My compass doesn't work in space. But yours works down there. It always points to safety. Someone made sure of that, for you.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.075
cast.text: I once saw the whole world go dark for a moment, from orbit. Every light, every sound. Then it lit up again, brand new. It was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen.

cast.name: vc_astronaut.story.076
cast.text: The world rebuilds, but it always keeps its safe places warm. I can see the warmth from up here. Like little campfires, keeping watch.
